articles.title: I tested MSI's Pro Max Edge AI+ mini PC and its offline AI is off the charts
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
The processor may already be over a year old, yet combined with a powerful GPU, NPU and a stack of RAM, it has the raw power to comfortably run local AI. Standard mini PC performance is workstation-level, perfect for high-end creative and business use. As with the competition, the Pro Max Edge AI+ enables you to run LLMs fully offline and at speed, all made possible by the 128GB of unified memory, Strix Halo CPU and powerful integrated Radeon 8060S graphics. However, some other aspects feel dated, such as the slow 2.5GbE network; still, that local AI potential is impressive.
Reasons to buy
- + Excellent local AI
- + Huge unified memory
- + Compact workstation design
Reasons to avoid
- - Older CPU
- - RAM can’t be upgraded further
- - Large power draw for a mini PC
Why you can trust TechRadar
We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
MSI PRO MAX Edge AI+: 30-second review
The MSI Pro Max Edge AI+ is one of the most powerful mini workstations that I’ve tested, and proved to be a perfect tool for Creative application and running AI offline. Inside is the AMD’s Ryzen AI Max+ 395, however, unlike previous machines of this size that I've looked at it's backed by Radeon 8060S graphics and, crucially for running local language models it comes with 128GB of unified memory.
This combination of high powered processers means that it was able to run surprisingly large local AI models all downloaded and managed within Lemonade. The most impressive task centered around sorting more than 2,600 images, generate images using the Flux and Qwen3 Coder models through Visual Studio Code and several other supporting apps. It was also able to generate a ten page website, although quite a bit of prompting was needed.
Performance for normal creative work, using Photoshop, Lightroom and Premiere Pro was equally impressive with the machine handling batches of Sony RAW files without issue. Pushing the abilities I checked out the performance editing 4K Canon EOS R5 C footage in Premiere Pro and once again that power of the Strix Halo took the edit in its stride.
There are of course some drawbacks such as the staggeringly high price at £5,999, then there the 2.5Gb Ethernet that just feels slow for a workstation of this level, and getting the most from local AI requires plenty of setup and experimentation, but then that's just how things are with AI at the moment.
But once configured, that’s where the Pro Max Edge AI+ starts to make sense. If you need private, completely offline AI for coding, image organisation or other long-running workloads, there’s an enormous amount of processing power packed into this relatively compact machine.
MSI PRO MAX Edge AI+: Price and availability
- How much does it cost? From $5,499
- When is it out? Available now
- Where can you get it? Directly from MSI
The MSI Pro Max Edge AI+ is available from the MSI website for $5,499 (US); €5,299; £5,999. It’s also widely available from most online retailers.
- Value: 4 / 5
MSI PRO MAX Edge AI+: Specs
CPU: AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395, 16-core / 32-thread Zen 5
GPU: AMD Radeon 8060S integrated graphics
NPU: AMD XDNA NPU, up to 50 TOPS
RAM: 128GB LPDDR5X-8000 unified memory
Maximum GPU memory allocation: Up to 96GB
Storage: 2TB M.2 2280 NVMe PCIe Gen 4 x4 SSD
Rear ports: 2x USB 2.0 Type-A, 1x USB 10Gbps Type-A, 1x USB 40Gbps Type-C with DisplayPort 2.0 Alt Mode and 15W PD output, 1x HDMI 2.1, 1x DisplayPort 1.4a, 1x RJ45 Ethernet, 1x 3.5mm audio combo jack
Networking: 2.5Gb Ethernet
Wi-Fi: Wi-Fi 7
Operating system: Windows 11 Pro
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
MSI PRO MAX Edge AI+: Design
The first impressions of this mini PC are impressive. It arrives with a slightly larger form factor than I’m used to for a mini PC, but then again, this has one of the Strix Halo CPUs inside, and that’s matched with an equally impressive integrated GPU and NPU.
What marks this new machine out, despite its rather ageing CPU, is the fact that it’s been fully optimised to run LLMs with 128GB of unified RAM soldered to the motherboard and AMD Radeon 8060S integrated graphics.
The machine is by no means large at 197.5 x 188.4 x 94.5mm, and while heavier than most mini PCs, it comes in at just 2.9kg, so if you need it, it’s still perfectly portable. On the portability, I was pleased to see that the power supply is integrated into the form factor, so there’s no power brick to lug around with the machine itself.
This means it’s equally at home on your desktop or, if you’re a creative and you do need to take your machine with you, then it’s still relatively portable.
Around the body, there are plenty of ports and connectivity options, which are given space due to that larger form factor. Size-wise, it sits somewhere in the middle of a mini PC and mini tower.
On the front, you have two USB Type-A ports offering 10Gbps and one USB4 port with 40Gbps. This also supports DisplayPort 2.0 and 15W USB power output.
Alongside this USB port is a full-sized SD 4.0 UHS-II card reader that will appeal to creatives, along with a 3.5mm audio jack. The other addition on the front is a performance mode switch that you can use to quickly adapt between Performance and Eco modes.
At the rear, you have a further two USB 2.0 Type-A ports and a USB 3.2 10Gbps Type-A port, a USB Type-C port that offers 40Gbps, and again this supports DisplayPort 2.0 and 15W USB Type-C power output. The USB ports are joined by HDMI 2.1 with HDR and up to 4K 60Hz, DisplayPort 1.4, a 2.5GbE RJ45 Ethernet port and a further 3.5mm audio combo jack.
On the exterior, that pretty much rounds everything up, but inside you have two M.2 NVMe slots, one filled with a 2TB M.2 NVMe PCIe Gen 4 x4 SSD. The onboard RAM is soldered on and can’t be upgraded, but that is enough to run LLMs and many of the major creative applications with AI features.
On the design and build, it’s a shame that there is no OCuLink port for connecting out to an eGPU; even with the USB4 port, the fact that the RJ45 port is limited to just 2.5GbE is a disappointment. I would have expected that a machine of this price would have at least 5GbE, if not 10GbE. When it comes to the overall quality and design, it’s both aesthetically pleasing and exceptionally well made, as you’d expect at this price point.
- Design: 4.5 / 5
MSI PRO MAX Edge AI+: Features
As of 1 October 2026, this machine has just hit the shelves. Yet one of the headline features, the Strix Halo Ryzen AI Max+ 395, is already over a year old. This CPU features an integrated Radeon 8060S GPU and an NPU, alongside 128GB of unified LPDDR5X-8000 RAM, which enables the ultrafast processing required by many of the AI features to really push through.
That CPU, while a little older than some of the latest AI mini PCs that we’re seeing, enables the machine to be well balanced when it comes to performance, although this is still an expensive option. That CPU offers 16 cores and 32 threads with AMD’s Strix Halo Zen 5 architecture.
This is joined by the equally impressive AMD Radeon 8060S integrated graphics and integrated AMD XDNA NPU, which offers up to 50 TOPS of AI processing. This means that with all of those processors combined, there’s 126 TOPS of potential within this one small machine.
Storage capacity is catered for with two M.2 slots, each NVMe PCIe Gen 4 x4, and my review sample arrived with a 2TB module. Across the machine, there’s a decent array of ports both front and back, and it’s great to see that it features a USB4 port on both the front and back. If you do need to connect ultra-fast storage, this is perfectly possible. These ports also support DisplayPort 2.0 and 15W power output, which again is extremely handy.
On starting up the machine, it’s pre-installed with Windows 11 Pro, and MSI has included its management software, which enables you to activate certain AI features, as well as security and settings options to adjust the machine’s performance.
One of the features that I mentioned in the design section is the fact that the power supply is integrated, and this offers 300W of power, which is needed by these AI-enhanced processors to handle all of that processing.
Wi-Fi 7 supplies the wireless connectivity, which is now becoming the standard, although Wi-Fi 8 has just started to emerge on some devices. It also features a UHS-II SD card reader, again great to see, and a single LAN port at the back, which is 2.5GbE. This is a little disappointing on a machine of this price and performance. I would have expected a minimum of 5GbE and preferably 10GbE.
- Features: 4 / 5
MSI PRO MAX Edge AI+: Performance
Crystal Disk Mark Read: 6122.48
Crystal Disk Mark Write: 5827.92
Geekbench 7 CPU Multi: 21905
Geekbench 7 CPU Single: 2672
Geekbench 7 GPU: 96251
PC Mark Overall: 9990
Cinebench 2026 CPU Multi (Threads): 6932
Cinebench 2026 CPU Single (Threads): 457
Fire Strike Overall: 25009
Fire Strike Graphics: 28653
Fire Strike Physics: 29422
Fire Strike Combined: 11480
Time Spy Overall: 10777
Time Spy Graphics: 10972
Time Spy CPU: 9792
Wild Life Overall: 65611
Steel Nomad Overall: 2158
Windows Experience Overall: 8.8
Procyon: 1125
Getting into the performance of the machine, the initial setup is as straightforward as ever. Windows 11 Pro is relatively straightforward, and once you plug the machine in and connect up all the peripherals, it’s just a case of running through the final steps, connecting it online, and within about 10 to 20 minutes, the machine will be up and running, ready for you to install whichever software you want.
In this test, I’ve run a wide variety of different applications, starting off with the basics of Microsoft Office to test productivity. I’ve also installed the Adobe Creative Suite, with a focus on Adobe Photoshop, Lightroom and Premiere Pro, and alongside that, to start some of the AI testing, I’ve also installed DaVinci Resolve.
As this machine is very much focused on AI, especially with that Strix Halo processor, I’ve also installed Lemonade to manage the local LLMs and downloaded and installed a good variety of different options, including Flux, Qwen 3 and Qwen 2.5 releases, to enable a variety of different tasks that I’d later test the machine with.
Starting out with general computer use, Microsoft Office and Windows run smoothly, as you would imagine on a machine of this price and power. Microsoft Word, PowerPoint and Excel can all easily be opened at the same time, with images, data and content being transferred from one to the other without any noticeable slowdown or hesitation.
Copying and pasting images is straightforward, and as I opened multiple windows over the week of testing in the Edge browser, there was no issue or slowdown. It also proved that the Wi-Fi 7 connection to my Wi-Fi 6 hub was exceptionally solid.
Progressing on from Microsoft Office, I loaded up a few apps from the Adobe Creative Suite and, using Adobe Bridge, checked through a couple of thousand images, both JPEG and RAW, that were shot on the Sony A7 IV. Again, here you really see that processor and the Radeon 8060S GPU handle the rendering of thumbnails exceptionally quickly.
Unlike on many smaller mini PCs, there is really very little time needed for each new thumbnail to render, enabling me to quickly scroll from top to bottom through the images without having to wait to see what each file contains. Selecting a batch of images and then opening them in Adobe Camera Raw once again just showed how powerful this machine was.
While I was dealing with large Sony RAW files, and a decent quantity at a time, there was absolutely no slowdown on either individual or batch adjustments. Then, opening those up into Adobe Photoshop was equally fluid, with only a few seconds needed between ACR and the Photoshop workspace for each of the 50 images to fully load.
Even with my desktop workstation, which is a relatively powerful machine and also features 128GB of RAM and a decent GPU, what up to this point I’ve always felt was pretty fluid now seemed relatively slow in comparison. As I then switched over to Lightroom to quickly check and enhance another batch of files, it was again apparent that image editing on this machine was well below what it was capable of doing.
Even with generative expand and image generation, render times were a few seconds rather than up to a minute, which is what I have experienced with other small mini PCs. The real show of power came when I loaded up Adobe Premiere Pro and went to work on a 4K video edit using C-Log footage from the Canon EOS R5 C.
Again, it was as if I was just editing 1080p video shot on a mobile phone, and the machine could handle cuts and edits of the five-minute video without too much issue from over an hour’s worth of footage.
The only consideration here was that the footage was being imported from an external Thunderbolt 4 drive, and here I was a little disappointed that I couldn’t connect my NAS to the system so that I could network edit due to the limited speed of the 2.5GbE network port on the back. Instead, I had to rely on a traditional external SSD for storage, although there is thankfully an additional internal M.2 slot which would take additional internal storage if required.
Still, the video editing potential is there, and it’s impressively fast, but this led me directly to checking out the machine’s AI potential, and this is where things really started to develop.
To test AI performance, more specifically local AI performance, I first installed Lemonade and then, through that, downloaded a variety of different LLMs and models for different tasks.
These included Qwen 2.5-VL-7B-Instruct-GGUF, which is a vision model and was used to inspect and recognise images. I used this in combination with ExifTool to organise and label a variety of files for website creation.
I fell back on Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-GGUF, and this was absolutely superb for coding HTML and CSS Grid for the test. While this took quite a bit of additional configuration, especially training it to use Grid formats rather than straight HTML, and connecting it through Visual Studio Code, I was again impressed by just how simply it all tied together.
The biggest task that I put the machine through was file organisation, and this is a task that I’ve always put off. Even after a few months of using various different techniques to sort the images, it’s always good when one of these machines comes in so that I can start to pick up from where I last left off.
While they automate the process, it’s still relatively slow. Here I fed in over 2,634 images and used GPT-OSS-20B-NPU to really put the machine through its paces. Not only was it able to recognise the images, but it started to sort them at a relative speed, although I did fall back onto Qwen 2.5-VL-7B-Instruct-GGUF in order to complete the task, and not all images were recognised. Checking the content of those images, they were mostly nondescript or under or overexposed, so the subject wasn’t recognisable in any way.
Taking time to set up the machine is something that I found all the way along when using AI machines: they’re not ready to use out of the box, and there is a certain learning curve needed in order to configure the LLMs in a way that works for you. While they do run offline, as all tests were carried out in this review, I did utilise online AI at points to select the different models for the different tasks that I had in mind.
One of the next tests that I ran was to create a quick static website that I could then update on a regular basis. For this, I first loaded Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-GGUF through Lemonade. I also opened Visual Studio Code and installed the Continue extension. I created a folder with all the assets that I wanted for my project, including Word documents that I converted into plain text and images that were reformatted into JPEGs.
In Visual Studio Code, I was then able to use the Continue AI chat window, connect the model that I wanted and put in the prompt to create a 3D printer review website with a variety of different sections. I also uploaded some general design ideas so that it had a good plan of what it was going to create. I’d already pre-designed the look and layout using CSS Grid, as I like the speed of pure static HTML rather than a more standard CMS site. I then hit Enter and let the local model do its thing.
One of the first things that I noticed was that, within Visual Studio Code, I would have to accept file creation for each file that it generated. In this review, I haven’t yet found a workaround for this so that it can just create the files without prompting.
But checking out the HTML, it was exceptionally clean, if a little textbook, and the final result was pretty good, although there were a few minor rendering issues with the JavaScript that I hadn’t wanted it to create. For some reason, none of the images that I had given it had been included in the design, so essentially it was just CSS layout and review text.
Again, going back in and re-editing, it started to slowly develop the website into what I wanted, and this really starts to show you the power of localised AI and what’s possible. By the time the whole process was finished, the server session recorded 152,937 input tokens for what was essentially a 10-page website and processed 24,639 output tokens, which were generated across 51 requests.
To actually complete the site, I would consider around 200 requests realistic. The final response generated 406 tokens at 47.85 tokens per second, equivalent to approximately 8.5 seconds of generation, with a time to first token of 1.99 seconds, which is pretty much on par with some of the online models that I use. The entire process, which involved a little to and fro from prompts and letting the machine work through the task, was an hour.
As I went through further models and further experiments with the localised AI, I was increasingly impressed by what it was capable of doing, with the most useful application being the file sorting. I have run file sorting with some of the other AI models and been impressed, but here things seemed to take a bit of a step up, with the power of the GPU and CPU taking on most of the processing.
Quickly checking which processors were in use showed that there was no NPU involvement in the sorting process, as I was using the Qwen 2.5-VL-7B-Instruct-GGUF model. However, it did appear that there were spikes of NPU use during the processing.
When selecting the models, if you do want to make full use of that NPU, then you select an NPU-compatible model, but this varies per task, and new models are being released all the time that you can download and experiment with. This is where most of the time with AI comes in, as you do need to experiment a great deal to make the most of these machines and their AI potential.
For most users, however, if you’re just using Copilot or the built-in AI behind Photoshop or Premiere Pro, then the potential is also there, and that does fall back onto the processor and NPU, with more improvements arriving over time. The final AI test was to incorporate AI into DaVinci Resolve for some video editing.
While I’ve only just started to experiment on this front, the way that DaVinci and the AI model interact on this machine is slightly eerie and impressive, with some pretty decent rough cuts of three-channel video straight off the bat. I’m hoping that, with a bit more experimentation, I’ll get usable edits, but even in these early stages of experimentation, the potential of this machine is apparent.
While other lesser machines are able to do many of these tasks, what makes it different here is the absolute speed at which the hardware is able to cope. Because of the 128GB of onboard memory, it doesn’t stall or run out of steam partway through a task. In the final task, really just for a bit of fun, I loaded in Flux-2-Klein-9B-GGUF for some generative image creation.
Here, I asked it to create a picture of a Labrador in the New Forest in spring, summer, autumn and winter. I was able to create each of those images in less than a minute. The Flux model is a little limited in what you can actually do with it, but I was able to load a portrait of myself into the system, then use that to generate a picture of myself and a Labrador in the New Forest. This was again entertaining and surprisingly good for something that runs offline.
However, there were some of the issues that you always get with even the online models, such as extra arms and fingers where you weren’t expecting them. Still, this is fully offline AI running without any cloud server intervention.
- Performance: 4.5 / 5
MSI PRO MAX Edge AI+: Final verdict
The MSI Pro Max Edge AI+ is an impressive mini PC, although slightly larger than the small box-like machines that I usually look at, but even with a processor that is over a year old, when it is combined with the integrated Radeon 8060S GPU and NPU, it already offers impressive power.
But then, when you add in 128GB of unified RAM, a fast SSD and plenty of connectivity options, you have a machine that is finally capable of running LLMs locally. The one point about any machine like this is that they’re not simple plug-and-play systems when it comes to the AI potential.
Setting up the local language models in the way that you want to use them does take time, and for anyone just getting into local AI, expect to put aside at least a week to fully experiment with each of the models and what they can do, as well as the different model types that utilise the CPU and GPU and those that really make use of the NPU.
Once you’ve done that and you know exactly what you want to do, then it takes another day to fully set up the machine to do exactly what you want from scratch. After testing several of these machines, I now jot down the models that I need to install in order to run these tests, and even then I’m looking at a good half-day to download all of that content.
But then, once it’s set up, the potential is massive. Unlike lesser machines with less RAM and without these AI-enhanced CPUs, you can actually run proper localised language models, and the output they produce is also exceptionally good.
When you spend time not only making sure that all the downloads are there and available for them, but also training them so that they produce the style of content that you want, they become even more powerful. Personally, I found the best way to use this is to run a combination of cloud AI to help prompt the local AI into getting exactly what you want, use the paid tokens for the knowledge and the local AI for the heavy local work.
It all takes time, but compared with just a few months ago, the leap forward is massive and, really, while this machine is expensive, it does offer true offline AI if you want it.
Should I buy the MSI Pro Max Edge AI+?
| Value | Strix Halo power with the usual pricing | 4 | 
| Design | Stylish design that gives space for cooling | 4.5 | 
| Features | 128GB unified-memory enable the power to run local LLMs | 4 | 
| Performance | Powerful GPU just gives this machine the edge over some close compitition | 4.5 | 
| Overall | Incredibly powerful workstation in a compact form | 4 | 
Buy it if...
You want offline AI
Running some of the commands that I utilised in this test would cost a substantial amount if using a cloud-based option. However, here, while that process is time-consuming, there’s no additional cost.
You have long-running tasks.
The file sorting for the 2,500 images was lengthy, and that’s just the start of it, so having a machine that I can leave running in the background sorting out images is extremely appealing.
Don't buy it if...
You just need a powerful machine.
There are plenty of machines as powerful as this for general work, but without that massive AI potential, that you can buy for a far lower price.
You don’t really need local AI.
The idea of local AI is good, but for the majority of people, the free or minimum-tier options available from the major players will offer you far more than you get from this machine.
It’s only when you start to customise things that this becomes viable.

Alastair is a photographer, filmmaker and tech writer who has been working in the publishing industry since the late 1990s. For more than 25 years he has covered photography, video and technology across Future's photography, technology and gaming brands. He runs a photography and video production company and lectures in TV and film. He can usually be found testing mini PCs or prototyping and prop building with the aid of 3D printing.

articles.title: Qué empresas lideraban la venta de celulares al inicio del negocio: quiénes eran los Apple y Samsung de la época
articles.text:
Durante las décadas de 1980 y 1990, mucho antes de que Apple y Samsung se convirtieran en protagonistas del mercado de los teléfonos inteligentes, otras compañías dominaban la industria de la telefonía móvil.
Motorola, Nokia y Ericsson fueron algunas de las marcas que definieron esa etapa, con equipos que marcaron el paso de los primeros celulares comerciales a dispositivos más compactos, accesibles y preparados para las redes digitales.
Motorola fue una de las grandes pioneras del sector, mientras que Nokia terminó por convertirse en el principal fabricante mundial de teléfonos móviles a finales de los años noventa. Ericsson, por su parte, tuvo un papel relevante tanto en el desarrollo de dispositivos como en la infraestructura que permitió expandir las comunicaciones inalámbricas.
La comparación con Apple y Samsung ayuda a entender la evolución del negocio, aunque el mercado de aquella época era diferente al actual: los celulares se utilizaban principalmente para llamar y enviar mensajes, y el diseño, la autonomía de la batería, la cobertura y la resistencia eran factores decisivos para los compradores.
Motorola, la compañía que abrió el camino
La historia del teléfono móvil comercial está estrechamente vinculada con Motorola, empresa estadounidense que presentó en 1983 el DynaTAC 8000X. El dispositivo, de gran tamaño en comparación con los celulares actuales, pesaba cerca de 800 gramos y ofrecía una autonomía limitada. Su precio de lanzamiento rondaba los 4.000 dólares, por lo que estaba lejos de ser un producto accesible para la mayoría de los consumidores.
Aun así, el DynaTAC 8000X representó un hito: permitió realizar llamadas sin depender de una conexión telefónica fija. Durante los años siguientes, Motorola continuó desarrollando equipos que contribuyeron a definir el diseño de los celulares.
En 1989 presentó el MicroTAC, un modelo compacto para los estándares de la época que incorporaba una pieza abatible sobre el teclado. En 1996 llegó el StarTAC, uno de los primeros teléfonos plegables de gran popularidad comercial. Su tamaño reducido y su diseño lo convirtieron en un dispositivo emblemático de la segunda mitad de los noventa.
Motorola fue una marca de referencia durante los primeros años de la telefonía móvil, aunque el crecimiento de nuevos fabricantes y la expansión de las redes digitales modificaron progresivamente el equilibrio de fuerzas.
Nokia conquistó el mercado mundial
Si Motorola ayudó a establecer el negocio, Nokia fue la empresa que consiguió llevar los celulares a una escala masiva. La compañía finlandesa, que originalmente se dedicaba a otras actividades industriales, se convirtió en un actor central de las telecomunicaciones durante los años noventa.
En 1998, Nokia superó a Motorola y pasó a ocupar el primer puesto mundial en ventas de teléfonos móviles. Su crecimiento estuvo relacionado con la expansión de las redes GSM, la variedad de modelos y una oferta que abarcaba distintos segmentos de precios.
La marca se hizo conocida por fabricar dispositivos resistentes, con baterías de larga duración y funciones sencillas de utilizar. Modelos como el Nokia 3210 y el Nokia 3310 alcanzaron una amplia popularidad y se convirtieron en referencias de una época en la que el celular comenzaba a ser un objeto cotidiano.
El dominio de Nokia continuó durante la década siguiente. En su momento de mayor participación, alrededor de 2007, la compañía concentró cerca del 40% del mercado mundial de teléfonos móviles, según estimaciones históricas de la industria. Esa posición la convirtió en el fabricante dominante justo cuando el sector estaba a punto de experimentar una transformación profunda.
Ericsson y los otros fabricantes que competían por el mercado
La sueca Ericsson fue otro de los nombres importantes de la telefonía móvil. Además de fabricar teléfonos, desarrolló infraestructura de telecomunicaciones y participó en la evolución de los estándares digitales que permitieron conectar a millones de usuarios.
Su trayectoria estuvo vinculada con GSM, una tecnología que facilitó la expansión de las redes móviles en Europa y otros mercados. En 2001, Ericsson y Sony formaron una empresa conjunta para fabricar teléfonos bajo la marca Sony Ericsson, que posteriormente ganó notoriedad con equipos orientados a la música y la fotografía.
El mercado también contaba con otros fabricantes relevantes. Siemens, de Alemania, destacó con productos como el S10, presentado en 1998 y reconocido por incorporar una pantalla a color. Panasonic y Alcatel también comercializaron teléfonos populares en distintos mercados, mientras que empresas como Samsung comenzaron a ampliar su presencia internacional.
La llegada del iPhone cambió las reglas
El lanzamiento del iPhone en 2007 modificó las expectativas sobre lo que podía hacer un teléfono. La pantalla multitáctil, la navegación por internet y la integración de aplicaciones impulsaron un modelo de negocio distinto al de los celulares tradicionales. La expansión de Android, presentado en 2008, aceleró esa transformación.
Nokia y Motorola tuvieron dificultades para adaptarse al nuevo escenario, mientras que Ericsson dejó de competir como fabricante independiente de celulares tras la evolución de su alianza con Sony. Samsung, por su parte, consiguió consolidar su posición con una amplia gama de teléfonos inteligentes.
Así, las empresas que habían definido la primera etapa de la telefonía móvil cedieron protagonismo a nuevos líderes. El cambio no fue inmediato ni respondió a una sola causa, pero mostró que, en tecnología, la experiencia acumulada no garantiza el liderazgo cuando las reglas del mercado cambian.

articles.title: Notebook com RTX 3050: 6 modelos que valem a pena em 2026 • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Notebook com RTX 3050: 6 modelos que valem a pena em 2026
Encontre o melhor notebook com placa RTX 3050 dedicada para jogos casuais e criação de conteúdo leve; guia reúne modelos Lenovo, Asus, Acer e HP
Os notebooks com GeForce RTX 3050 continuam sendo uma opção de entrada para quem procura um portátil capaz de lidar com jogos e aplicações que utilizam aceleração gráfica.
A GPU pertence à arquitetura Ampere e oferece recursos como ray tracing, DLSS e NVIDIA Reflex, mas existem diferenças importantes entre cada modelo.
O Tecnoblog apresenta seis notebooks com a placa de vídeo dedicada da Nvidia para comprar em 2026, trazendo seus pontos fortes e fracos.
O Lenovo LOQ combina o Intel Core i5 de 13ª geração com a GeForce RTX 3050 de 6 GB, sendo voltado para jogos e aplicações que dependem de alto processamento gráfico.
O processador tem 10 núcleos e 16 threads, enquanto a GPU dedicada trabalha com TGP de até 95 W (limite máximo de energia que garante frequências mais altas e maior performance sob estresse). Esse conjunto permite utilizar recursos gráficos como ray tracing e DLSS, dentro dos limites da RTX 3050.
A memória RAM DDR5 de 16 GB é instalada em dois módulos, e o armazenamento fica a cargo de um SSD de 512 GB. O notebook também oferece dois slots de memória e dois espaços para SSD M.2.
A tela de 15,6 polegadas tem resolução Full HD, painel IPS, 144 Hz, 300 nits, cobertura de 100% do espaço sRGB e suporte a G-Sync. A taxa de atualização favorece movimentos mais fluidos em jogos compatíveis, enquanto a cobertura de cores torna a tela mais adequada também para tarefas de design.
O Asus TUF Gaming F16 é um notebook gamer para quem busca uma tela maior. O painel IPS de 16 polegadas (1920 x 1200 pixels) utiliza proporção 16:10 e taxa de atualização de 144 Hz, oferecendo mais espaço vertical do que uma tela Full HD convencional.
A resolução e o formato também servem para produtividade, enquanto essa frequência favorece a fluidez em jogos e outros conteúdos compatíveis. O painel tem cobertura de 45% NTSC, portanto, não é recomendado para projetos que necessitem de ampla reprodução de cores.
O processamento fica por conta do Intel Core 5 210H, com oito núcleos e frequência de até 4,8 GHz. A placa dedicada traz 6 GB GDDR6 e TGP de até 65 W, além dos 8 GB de RAM e SSD de 512 GB. Como os 8 GB podem limitar a utilização de jogos e apps mais exigentes, a possibilidade de upgrade é essencial neste modelo.
O Lenovo IdeaPad Gaming 3i pertence a uma geração anterior da linha e combina o Intel Core i5-11300H, de 11ª geração, com uma GeForce RTX 3050 de 4 GB para jogos. O processador tem quatro núcleos e oito threads, enquanto a GPU dedicada acrescenta recursos como ray tracing e DLSS.
Ele traz memória de 16 GB DDR4 e armazenamento em SSD NVMe de 512 GB. Essa quantidade de RAM permite trabalhar com mais aplicações simultaneamente sem depender tanto de memória virtual. A tela de 15,6 polegadas tem resolução Full HD, painel WVA/IPS e acabamento antirreflexo, com brilho de 250 nits.
A taxa de atualização informada para esse modelo é de 60 Hz, inferior em fluidez a outros modelos deste guia. A conectividade inclui Wi-Fi 6, Bluetooth 5.0, USB-C, duas USB, HDMI e Ethernet, enquanto a bateria tem capacidade de 45 Wh. O sistema operacional de fábrica é Linux.
Essa versão do Acer Nitro V15 combina Core i5 e GeForce RTX 3050 de 6 GB para quem busca bom desempenho em jogos casuais. O processador de 13ª geração possui oito núcleos e frequência de até 4,6 GHz. Já a GPU dedicada tem TGP de até 80 W e pode ser utilizada também em softwares de edição de vídeo e renderização.
A configuração de fábrica traz 8 GB de RAM DDR5 em um módulo, com dois slots disponíveis e suporte informado pela Acer para até 32 GB. O SSD de 512 GB utiliza interface PCIe 4.0 e há dois slots M.2, sendo um ocupado e outro livre.
A tela IPS de 15,6 polegadas tem resolução Full HD, 144 Hz e brilho de 250 nits, além de cobertura de 45% NTSC. Entre as portas estão HDMI 2.1 e USB-C com Thunderbolt 4, além de três USB-A. A Acer informa autonomia de até sete horas de uso.
O ASUS TUF Gaming A15 é ideal para jogadores e criadores de conteúdo que buscam um desempenho sólido em jogos em Full HD e tarefas de produtividade pesadas sem ter que investir em categorias top de linha.
A combinação do processador AMD Ryzen 7 7445HS de seis núcleos e 12 threads com os 16 GB de RAM garante alta velocidade e excelente fluidez para multitarefas e jogos exigentes.
A placa de vídeo GeForce RTX 3050 operando em até 75 W com Dynamic Boost entrega o desempenho necessário para rodar títulos atuais com estabilidade, aproveitando o painel Full HD IPS de 144 Hz com Adaptive-Sync para imagens sem travamentos.
Outro grande diferencial é a capacidade de expansão, já que conta com dois slots de memória e dois slots M.2 para SSD NVMe, além de conectividade completa com Wi-Fi 6, USB-C com DisplayPort, HDMI 2.1 e porta Ethernet.
O HP Victus 15 é recomendado para jogadores e estudantes que procuram um modelo de entrada versátil, capaz de rodar jogos com fluidez em Full HD e executar softwares com aceleração gráfica sem estourar o orçamento.
O processador Intel Core i5 de 13ª geração, equipado com oito núcleos que alcançam até 4,6 GHz, entrega a capacidade computacional necessária para lidar com tarefas cotidianas do dia a dia e atividades multitarefa moderadas.
A placa de vídeo GeForce RTX 3050 de 6 GB oferece uma margem extra de memória VRAM para sustentar taxas de quadros mais estáveis, tirando pleno proveito da tela Full HD IPS de 144 Hz em títulos competitivos.
O modelo vem de fábrica com 8 GB de RAM DDR4 e 512 GB de SSD, trazendo a vantagem de possuir dois slots de memória acessíveis para quem planeja fazer um upgrade futuro de memória e expandir o desempenho.
A escolha deve considerar o conjunto do notebook, e não apenas o nome da GPU. Alguns pontos ajudam a diferenciar as configurações:
Sim. A RTX 3050 para notebooks é adequada principalmente para jogos em Full HD, mas o nível de qualidade gráfica e a taxa de quadros variam conforme o jogo e a configuração da máquina. Recursos como o DLSS podem ajudar a aumentar o desempenho em jogos compatíveis com a tecnologia.
Sim. A RTX 3050 pode acelerar tarefas de edição de vídeo, renderização e outros programas que utilizam GPU, além de oferecer suporte aos drivers NVIDIA Studio. Porém, o desempenho depende também do processador, quantidade de RAM e da própria configuração de potência da GPU.
A versão de 6 GB tem mais espaço para armazenar texturas e outros dados gráficos, reduzindo a possibilidade de a quantidade de VRAM se tornar uma limitação em determinadas situações. Porém, os 2 GB adicionais não significam, isoladamente, um aumento proporcional de desempenho.
A RTX 3050 de 6 GB também possui uma configuração diferente da versão de 4 GB, com mais núcleos CUDA. Por isso, a diferença entre os modelos não se resume à quantidade de VRAM, e o TGP do notebook continua sendo importante para determinar o desempenho.
Vale a pena investir em notebooks com RTX 4060 se a diferença de preço couber no orçamento.
Essa GPU oferece uma margem de desempenho gráfico consideravelmente maior e traz 8 GB de VRAM, além da arquitetura Ada Lovelace e suporte ao DLSS 3. Já a RTX 3050 pode fazer mais sentido quando o objetivo é jogar em 1080p sem gastar tanto.
Na prática, o consumo e o aquecimento não dependem apenas do modelo da GPU. O TGP definido pelo fabricante, o sistema de refrigeração e o perfil de desempenho do notebook também influenciam esses fatores.
A RTX 4060 Laptop usa a arquitetura Ada Lovelace, mais eficiente energeticamente que a arquitetura Ampere da RTX 3050. Isso permite que a GPU entregue mais desempenho mantendo uma relação de desempenho por watt mais favorável, embora o consumo dependa da configuração de cada notebook.
A RTX 3050 Laptop tem faixa de potência de 35 a 80 W, enquanto a RTX 4060 Laptop opera entre 35 e 115 W. Por isso, uma RTX 4060 configurada com TGP mais alto pode consumir mais energia e gerar mais calor que uma RTX 3050 de menor potência.

articles.title: Passer le péage sans s’arrêter : ce badge Fulli voit 1 an de frais de gestion offerts
articles.text:
Les vacances de la Toussaint démarrent le 17 octobre dans les trois zones, et beaucoup de familles vont reprendre l’autoroute. Le badge Fulli Balade ne facture que les mois où il sert, mais son tarif évolue le 1er novembre : voici ce que change le code RENTRE26.
Fulli, la marque de télépéage née chez APRR et AREA, propose avec Balade un badge pour ceux qui ne roulent pas tous les mois. Ses frais de gestion, 1,90 € puis 2,10 € par mois à partir du 1er novembre, ne sont dus que les mois où le badge passe un péage. Avec le code RENTRE26, le badge Fulli Balade est livré sans ses 11 € de frais de mise en service ni frais de gestion pendant 12 mois, seuls 4,90 € de livraison restant à régler. L’offre court jusqu’au 16 novembre inclus. Elle est réservée aux particuliers circulant en France avec un véhicule de classe 1, 2 ou 5.
Avec le code RENTRE26, le badge télépéage Fulli Balade ne coûte que 4,90 € de livraison : mise en service à 11 € et 12 mois de gestion offerts.
Pourquoi choisir le badge Fulli Balade ?
- Une facture qui suit vos départs : les mois sans trajet sur autoroute coûtent 0 €. Pour une voiture qui roule surtout pendant les vacances, les douze premiers mois de frais sont en plus couverts par le code.
- Des voies réservées au télépéage : le badge ouvre les voies « t » et « t30 », ces dernières sans arrêt jusqu’à 30 km/h. Plus de carte bancaire à sortir à chaque barrière.
- Sans engagement, avec un suivi en ligne : aucune durée minimale, un prélèvement le 15 du mois suivant les trajets, et une application Fulli sur iOS et Android pour suivre les consommations et factures.
Toussaint, ponts, week-ends en famille : un badge pour les trajets ponctuels
Les vacances de la Toussaint 2026 courent du samedi 17 octobre au lundi 2 novembre, aux mêmes dates dans les trois zones : départs et retours se concentrent sur les mêmes week-ends. Aux barrières, une voie t30 détecte le badge jusqu’à 30 km/h, sans arrêt au guichet. Les péages sont regroupés sur un seul relevé, prélevé le 15 du mois suivant. Fulli ne précise pas de délai de livraison sur la page de l’offre : pour partir dès le premier week-end, mieux vaut commander tôt.

articles.title: Warehouse robot maker Ultra Robotics bags $62M - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Warehouse robot maker Ultra Robotics bags $62M
Ultra Robotics Corp. today announced that it has raised $62 million in funding over two rounds.
Fortune reported that the company received the bulk of the capital, $50 million, through a Series A investment led by Framework Ventures. Ultra’s seed round was jointly led by Y Combinator and NextView Ventures.
Ultra sells a warehouse robot called OP1 Operator. It resembles a humanoid robot attached to the end of a traditional robotic arm. OP1 Operator uses a pair of grippers in the shape of forklift prongs to carry out its work.
The robot has a vertical reach of up to 10 feet, which enables it to take merchandise off warehouse shelves. If an item accidentally falls to the ground, OP1 operator can pick it up.
The inbound shipments that a warehouse receives often combine many different types of items in the same container. For example, an electronics supplier might group together components that belong to the same laptop series. In such situations, warehouse operators separate the contents of the container into bins that each contain a single type of component. That makes it easier to process merchandise for shipping.
Ultra says OP1 Operator can automate the task. It can also perform kitting, which is essentially the opposite operation. In kitting mode, OP1 Operator mixes and matches items from different warehouse containers into the same parcel. That’s necessary when a shopper orders multiple items from an online store.
OP1 Operator also handles the final packaging stage of the workflow. It can place the items that it assembled during the kitting stage into a package, seal it and add a shipping label. Ultra says that OP1 Operator supports multiple types of packaging including envelopes and plastic bags.
The robot is mounted on a flat base with wheels. There is no engine: Workers can move the OP1 Operator between different warehouse sections by manually rolling it. Once the robot is in place, the wheels lock to prevent it from tipping over.
OP1 Operator plugs into a standard wall outlet, which removes the need to charge and maintain batteries. A second cable links it to the local network. OP1 Operator’s computer uses the connection to share data from the onboard sensors with other robots. Ultra uses the data to enhance the artificial intelligence models that power its hardware.
The company says that its AI models don’t require extensive configuration on customers’ part. As a result, OP1 Operator can be set up in a few hours. Ultra claims that a single unit is capable of processing up to 1,000 items per day once it’s up and running.
“The robots that are actually changing the world are the ones doing valuable work for real people,” said Ultra founder and Chief Executive Jon Miller Schwartz. “And this isn’t some far-off dream. It’s happening right now.”
Ultra will use the new capital to finance engineering initiatives and expand the adoption of its robots.

articles.title: Xbox Names Former Reddit Product Chief As CEO of Minecraft Studio Mojang
articles.text:
Friday, October 9th 2026
Xbox Names Former Reddit Product Chief As CEO of Minecraft Studio Mojang
Xbox has hired a social media product veteran to run Mojang. In a memo to staff on October 8, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma said Maria Angelidou-Smith, most recently chief product officer at Reddit, will join as CEO of Mojang and Minecraft. She starts on October 19 and reports directly to Sharma. Angelidou-Smith replaces Kayleen Walters, who moves over to lead XP, the new Xbox division for film, TV, merchandise, and live experiences. Walters had run Mojang since February 2025, and Xbox says Minecraft went from 350 million copies sold to more than 425 million in that time.
Angelidou-Smith's background is in community products, with no game studio role mentioned. According to the memo, she spent nearly a decade at Meta, where she led Facebook Groups along with Events, Creators, Search, Profile, and Monetization. She later led product and technology at HR software company Personio and joined Reddit in November 2025. Sharma wrote that Mojang already has an exceptional game development team, so Xbox went looking for someone who has "built products for communities at enormous scale" and understands how creators, technology, and monetization come together. Her first order of business, apparently, is to learn from the teams and the community.The hire fits how Xbox has been talking about Minecraft recently. When Sharma announced 3,200 layoffs in July, she had Mojang and King report directly to her and described both as studios that have become platforms. Angelidou-Smith takes over a game that, according to Sharma, still pulls in more than 300,000 first-time players on an average day, with its first new dimension in over 14 years, The Sift, due in 2027. Xbox hasn't announced any change to how Minecraft makes money, though the memo's mention of monetization will probably make some players uneasy.
Sources:
				Xbox, 				via The Hollywood Reporter

articles.title: Lo mejor que le puede pasar a un arándano es que se lo coma un lobo
articles.text:
Cuando pensamos en el lobo, irremediablemente lo asociamos a un depredador de ciervos, ovejas, conejos y similares, , pero su dieta es más variada de lo que parece. De hecho, algunas manadas en verano comen mucha fruta. Y resulta que ese hábito frugívoro tiene consecuencias para el medio ambiente: sin ir más lejos, son una bendición para los arándanos.
Ojalá me coma un lobo. No dijo nadie nunca, salvo quizás los arándanos: un estudio de la Universidad de Minnesota ha descubierto el efecto de los lobos (de su ingesta) sobre la germinación de los arándanos. Concretamente, aquellas semillas que se habían comido los lobos germinaron en un 96 % frente al 69% de las que no. Además, también germinaron más rápido: para el día 19 ya habían salido la mitad, mientras que para las semillas no digeridas hubo que esperar hasta el día 26.
La digestión es una bendición. Vaya por delante algo, la ingestión de semillas por animales suele aumentar la germinación y hasta la calidad, sirva como ejemplo el café de civeta que se llama así porque sale de la civeta, un pequeño mamífero similar a un hurón. Eso sí, depende del tipo de animal: entre los cánidos hay resultados desiguales: zorros rojos y coyotes la mejoran, pero otras especies como perros domésticos, zorros grises, zorros cangrejeros y también coyotes, la reducen o no la modifican.
Según el equipo de investigación de este estudio con lobos de Minnesota y arándanos, que las semillas germinen más y más rápido probablemente sea por la escarificación química o mecánica de la cubierta de la semilla, es decir, que el paso por el intestino desgasta la cubierta de la semilla, de modo que le facilita absorber agua y percibir las señales de germinación.
Cómo lo hicieron. Para llegar a esa conclusión, recogieron cinco excrementos frescos de lobo del ecosistema del norte de Minnesota que estaban repletos de fruta digerida, los secaron y los congelaron. A partir de ahí, probaron 802 semillas de esos cinco excrementos que extrajeron a mano (literal, eso dice el paper) y las pusieron a germinar en el laboratorio, en papel de filtro y con condiciones controladas de luz y temperatura durante 60 días: a un lado, esas semillas digeridas, al otro, 484 semillas sin digerir de plantas silvestres recogidas durante tres años distintos.
Por qué importa. Porque si el lobo mejora la germinación y, además, se desplaza mucho, podría ayudar a que los arándanos se diseminen y lleguen a lugares nuevos. Según Alex Gross, primer autor del estudio, los lobos tienen capacidad de esparcir estas semillas mucho más lejos que zorros, coyotes u osos. Pero eso es todavía una hipótesis, porque aún no se ha medido cuánto tiempo permanece una semilla de arándano en el aparato digestivo del lobo. Y explican que aunque esto se ciñe a este experimento, también podría suceder en otros lugares donde los lobos coman fruta.
A falta de repetir el experimento con muestras más grandes y constatar cómo funciona en el bosque y no en el laboratorio, esta es en definitiva, una razón más para proteger al lobo y su papel en el ecosistema en el que vive: sabemos su posición dentro de la cadena trófica, pero más allá de la depredación resulta que también funciona como dispersor y potenciador de semillas.
Portada | Hans Veth

articles.title: Cuánto tiempo demora la revisión de WhatsApp cuando se suspende una cuenta
articles.text:
La revisión que WhatsApp realiza cuando bloquea una cuenta se completa en un plazo de 24 horas, explica la plataforma
WhatsApp indica que el plazo de 24 horas comienza cuando el usuario solicita la revisión. Además, aclara que solo puede revisar un número de teléfono por apelación. Si no aparece la opción para solicitar una revisión, el bloqueo es definitivo y no puede apelarse.
Para consultar el estado de la solicitud, hay que abrir WhatsApp. La plataforma advierte que contactarla fuera del proceso de revisión o desde la cuenta de otra persona no acelerará el trámite ni influirá en la decisión.
Por qué WhatsApp suspende o bloquea cuentas
WhatsApp puede bloquear una cuenta cuando detecta actividades que vulneran sus reglas o que pueden afectar a otros usuarios.
La plataforma señala que toma esta medida frente a casos de spam, fraude y conductas que comprometan la seguridad dentro del servicio. También prohíbe utilizar la aplicación con fines ilegales, no autorizados o inaceptables.
Entre las prácticas que pueden derivar en un bloqueo figuran el envío de mensajes masivos o automáticos, la suplantación de identidad y la difusión de información falsa o engañosa.
WhatsApp también contempla las amenazas, el acoso, los mensajes que incitan al odio y cualquier contenido que promueva delitos violentos, ponga en peligro a niños o coordine acciones dañinas.
La restricción alcanza, además, a quienes vulneren derechos de privacidad, propiedad intelectual o publicidad de la empresa, de otros usuarios o de terceros.
La compañía puede suspender cuentas que intenten acceder sin autorización a sus sistemas, enviar virus, interferir en la seguridad del servicio o crear perfiles mediante mecanismos automatizados.
Las normas incluyen la prohibición de recopilar datos de usuarios de forma indebida, revender el servicio, desarrollar herramientas similares sin permiso y presentar reportes fraudulentos o sin fundamento.
WhatsApp recuerda que cada persona es responsable de proteger su dispositivo y su cuenta, y debe informar de inmediato cualquier uso no autorizado o falla de seguridad.
Estas medidas buscan evitar daños a la plataforma y a la comunidad, según las condiciones de uso. Un bloqueo puede aplicarse cuando la actividad detectada incumple esas obligaciones o afecta la seguridad colectiva.
Cómo recuperar una cuenta de WhatsApp suspendida o en revisión
Si una cuenta de WhatsApp fue suspendida, el usuario debe abrir la aplicación y buscar la opción para solicitar una revisión. El proceso de apelación permite que WhatsApp evalúe el bloqueo y se aplica a un solo número de teléfono por solicitud.
La plataforma indica que la revisión se completa en un plazo de 24 horas desde que se presenta el pedido.
Para consultar su estado, hay que abrir WhatsApp. Si no aparece la opción de revisión, el bloqueo es definitivo y no se puede apelar. Contactar a WhatsApp por vías externas o desde otra cuenta no acelera ni modifica la decisión.
Qué nuevas funciones hay en WhatsApp
WhatsApp, la aplicación de mensajería de Meta, incorporó nuevas funciones para llamadas, herramientas de seguridad y opciones para usar el servicio en más dispositivos.
Entre las novedades, permite hacer y recibir llamadas de audio y video desde WhatsApp Web, transferir una llamada grupal entre dispositivos, activar una sala de espera mediante enlaces y reducir el ruido de fondo. Incorporó video en alta definición desde los primeros segundos de la comunicación.
Los grupos permiten fijar una hora de cierre para las encuestas, ocultar nombres de quienes votan y editar preguntas durante 15 minutos.
La mención @todos avisa; en grupos de más de 32 personas, queda para los administradores. WhatsApp permite crear grupos con participantes de un chat existente.
En seguridad, la verificación en dos pasos usa una contraseña extensa y las claves de acceso pueden configurarse en más de un dispositivo móvil. Las actualizaciones se implementan gradualmente y su disponibilidad varía según la región y el sistema operativo del usuario.

articles.title: IBM brings enterprise AI orchestration to TechXchange’s agenda - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
IBM connects enterprise AI orchestration to production readiness ahead of TechXchange
Enterprise AI orchestration must account for agents working across the data, applications and infrastructure businesses already use. As organizations move beyond experiments, running those systems consistently brings questions of access, oversight and operational control into sharper focus.
Those deployment challenges will help shape the discussion at IBM TechXchange 2026, taking place Oct. 26–29 in Atlanta. IBM Corp. plans to bring practitioners together to share how they are addressing production demands, including sovereignty, according to Bruno Aziza (pictured), group vice president of software, data, AI, automation and security at IBM.
“My belief is that the market is increasingly hybrid,” he said. “Hybrid data, hybrid operations, hybrid automation. The complexity is not in eliminating the hybrid world; the complexity is mastering the hybrid world.”
Aziza spoke with theCUBE Research’s Dave Vellante and John Furrier for IBM’s AI Operating Model interview series, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed the technologies, operating practices and governance needed to scale AI across the business ahead of TechXchange. (* Disclosure below.)
Enterprise AI orchestration requires continuous oversight
Giving employees tools to build agents creates both a management challenge and an opportunity to improve their work. Enterprises need visibility into what those employees are deploying and a way to coordinate it across their systems, Aziza explained.
“That’s going to be where governance breaks … the [number of agents] that’s created by your employees will outpace what you can manage,” he said. “So, you really need to build a platform that’s going to allow you to catch up.”
IBM’s AI operating model connects agent orchestration, data integration, hybrid operations and sovereignty. Oversight needs to extend across applications, clouds and data, with alerts that allow organizations to understand and respond when problems arise, according to Aziza.
“[People] tend to think about compliance, stopping innovation, whereas I think what we want to do is have a continuous system that enables people to innovate,” he said. “Your employees are going to innovate. You want to give them the tools to do that.”
Sovereignty reaches beyond data location
Sovereignty presents another test of how thoroughly enterprises understand their operating environments. Choosing where information resides addresses only part of the problem; organizations also need to establish responsibility for the surrounding systems and activities, Aziza noted.
“You have to think about data: Where should it live? You have to think about the technology: Which layers should be run by whom? You have to think about the operations: Who can, in fact, run that? Then you have to think about regulations: How are you staying in touch with that?” he said.
IBM’s Sovereign Core is designed to support control across those dimensions, with more than 200 compliance frameworks mapped to controls, according to the company. Evaluating partners therefore requires examining how their capabilities work together across the enterprise, rather than assuming an individual offering addresses the full scope of sovereignty, Aziza explained.
“True sovereignty really is across data, technology, operations and regulation. If you don’t have a complete answer to that, you might actually go down a silo that will be detrimental to your organization,” he said.
TechXchange puts production experience in the spotlight
IBM’s AI operating model brings together data, agentic workloads, hybrid cloud and infrastructure automation. Making enterprise AI orchestration work across those dimensions requires connecting agents to existing business processes and accommodating both batch and real-time data, Aziza explained. TechXchange will bring those implementation questions into practitioner discussions, with customer examples from organizations including Citigroup Inc., CVS Health Corp. and DoorDash Inc.
“I think culture is not something you put on walls. Culture is what you do,” he said. “One of the things that attracted me to IBM is a very customer-centric culture. What you will see at the conference is [that] the majority of our content is customer content; it’s practitioners exchanging.”
The conference is designed to address the diverse environments customers operate in rather than focus on one vendor’s cloud or application, Aziza explained. As models and tools change, practitioners need opportunities to compare implementation decisions with peers who have faced similar challenges. Those exchanges can help leaders assess their choices beyond the guidance they receive from vendors, he added.
“What [customers] have to turn to is someone they know and trust and say, ‘How did you design that?’” he said. “I think building for a world that changes, building for the dimensions of hybrid, is the only way you can win today.”

articles.title: Holafly : l’eSIM Europe à adopter pour rester connecté sans compter
articles.text:
Cartes, traduction, photos, messageries : Holafly joue la carte de l’illimité
Holafly propose une eSIM Europe avec données illimitées, pratique pour enchaîner plusieurs pays sans changer de carte SIM ni surveiller constamment sa consommation mobile.
Une eSIM Europe pensée pour les gros consommateurs de données
L’eSIM Europe de Holafly permet de voyager avec des données mobiles illimitées dans 33 pays européens, sans avoir à changer de carte SIM au fil du séjour. Le forfait démarre à 3,79 € pour une journée, tandis que les formules les plus courantes vont de 11,37 € pour 3 jours à 68,90 € pour 30 jours.
L’intérêt est assez simple : une fois l’eSIM installée, il devient possible d’utiliser Google Maps, les réseaux sociaux, les services de streaming ou les applications de messagerie sans compter chaque gigaoctet consommé.
Les principaux tarifs actuellement affichés sont :
- 3 jours : 11,37 €
- 5 jours : 18,50 €
- 7 jours : 25,50 €
- 10 jours : 33,90 €
- 15 jours : 46,90 €
- 30 jours : 68,90 €
Par ailleurs, l’offre couvre plusieurs destinations européennes avec une connexion 4G LTE et 5G lorsque le réseau local le permet. La qualité de connexion peut toutefois varier selon la couverture disponible, notamment dans les zones rurales ou montagneuses.
Une solution pratique pour garder Internet pendant tout le voyage
Ce qui m’a surtout intéressée dans cette offre, c’est la tranquillité qu’elle peut apporter lors d’un voyage itinérant. En passant d’un pays à l’autre, la question du forfait mobile revient vite : combien de données restent-il, faut-il acheter une nouvelle SIM, le réseau fonctionnera-t-il à l’arrivée ? Avec une formule illimitée, une bonne partie de ces préoccupations disparaît.
L’installation reste également assez simple. L’eSIM peut être configurée depuis l’application Holafly ou à l’aide du QR code envoyé après l’achat. Elle s’active ensuite à destination, ce qui permet de préparer le téléphone avant le départ sans commencer prématurément la période de validité.
En plus, le numéro habituel peut rester associé à la carte SIM principale. Il est donc possible de continuer à utiliser ses applications de messagerie comme WhatsApp avec son numéro habituel, tandis que l’eSIM Holafly prend en charge les données mobiles. L’offre prévoit aussi 1 Go de données partageables par jour avec d’autres appareils, selon les conditions du forfait.
Il faut cependant garder en tête qu’il s’agit d’une eSIM dédiée aux données : elle ne fournit pas de numéro local pour les appels et les SMS classiques. Pour un séjour de quelques jours ou plusieurs semaines, son intérêt se situe surtout dans la simplicité et la liberté d’utilisation.
Au final, Holafly Europe illimitée vise surtout les voyageurs qui utilisent beaucoup leur smartphone et souhaitent éviter les mauvaises surprises liées à la consommation de données. Pour 30 jours, les 68,90 € demandés représentent un budget certain, mais ils offrent une formule simple à gérer pour parcourir plusieurs pays européens sans surveiller chaque giga.

articles.title: Intentó robar un radar subido a un patinete y ahora se enfrenta a una pena de dos a cuatro años de cárcel
articles.text:
Octubre de 2025, unos agentes de tráfico esperan pacientemente junto a la carretera. Delante, un radar móvil capta la matrícula de todos aquellos que superan la velocidad máxima permitida. Instantes después, el radar deja de fotografiar, roto en el suelo.
Casi un año después, hay un sospechoso.
¿Qué ha pasado? La Guardia Civil ha detenido a una persona sospechosa de intentar robar un radar móvil. Los hechos, explican medios como Cadena Ser o La Razón se remontan a octubre de 2025 cuando una persona a bordo de un patinete eléctrico intentó robar un radar móvil que estaba en funcionamiento en la carretera N-301, en las inmediaciones de La Roda (Albacete).
El presunto autor de los hechos se enfrenta ahora a dos graves acusaciones. Una de ellas contempla una pena de prisión de dos a cuatro años por dejar inutilizado el equipo siendo los daños superiores a los 1.000 euros.
¿Por qué? Para entender lo sucedido hay que remontarse a octubre del año pasado. Entonces, una patrulla de Tráfico se encontraba junto a la carretera nacional N-301 realizando labores de vigilancia. En ese momento, un usuario de un patinete eléctrico apareció para intentar robar el equipo.
La intervención del agente más próximo impidió que esto sucediera pero la intervención acabó con el cinemómetro fuera de servicio. A continuación, el agente trató de perseguir al ladrón, pidiendo refuerzos. Sin embargo, esta persona consiguió escapar entre los caminos anexos a la carretera, siempre según la versión que ha hecho pública la Guardia Civil.
¿Y ahora? Señalan en la información que fue a finales de septiembre cuando los agentes consiguieron detener al sospechoso. Y es que la persona que intentó robar el radar se había vestido completamente de negro, con casco integral y gafas oscuras para no ser reconocido.
Finalmente, el sospechoso ha sido detenido en la localidad de La Roda y para dar con él ha tenido que intervenir el GIAT (Grupo de Investigación y Análisis del Tráfico). Estos agentes están especializados en rastrear por redes sociales las infracciones relacionadas con la seguridad vial.
En este caso, se cree que la persona sospechosa es quien robó el radar porque, entre otras investigaciones, se ha comprobado que se jactaba de haber realizado la acción y animaba a otros usuarios a hacer lo mismo, explican en 20 Minutos.
¿Cuál es el castigo? Según ha informado la Guardia Civi, a este sospechoso de 32 años se le acusa de haber infringido los artículos 263.1 o el 265 del Código Penal en el que se señala que inutilizar los medios (aunque sea de forma temporal) que utilizan las Fuerzas y Cuerpos de Seguridad conlleva una pena de prisión de dos a cuatro años cuando el daño supera los 1.000 euros. En este caso, el daño se ha valorado en 4.000 euros.
Además, también se tendrá en cuenta la tentativa de hurto, recogido en el artículo 234 del Código Penal, donde se señala que la pena de prisión puede ir de tres a seis meses o quedarse entre los 15 días y los tres meses.

articles.title: Jusqu'à 1 000 dollars pour trahir Apple, l'offre choc de Microsoft
articles.text:
Microsoft a dégainé une campagne au slogan cocasse : « Break up with your MacBook », comprenez « rompez avec votre MacBook ». Elle s’accompagne d’un programme de reprise pouvant atteindre 1 000 dollars pour un portable Apple échangé contre un Surface Laptop Ultra, dévoilé le même jour. Jamais l’entreprise n’était montée aussi haut pour débaucher les clients de Cupertino.
Une guerre de reprise vieille de dix ans
Dès 2014, Microsoft proposait jusqu’à 650 dollars pour un MacBook Air troqué contre une Surface Pro 3, avant une déclinaison plus modeste à 300 dollars l’année suivante. Rebelote en octobre 2016, avec un plafond identique de 650 dollars, cette fois pour convertir les MacBook Pro et Air aux Surface Book et Surface Pro, une offre alors réservée aux États-Unis et prolongée d’un mois. Quelques semaines plus tard, l’entreprise se félicitait de son meilleur programme de reprise à ce jour, sans publier le moindre chiffre de bascules effectives.
À l’époque, l’argument massue s’appelait l’écran tactile, dont les MacBook restent d’ailleurs privés aujourd’hui. Microsoft avançait que 97 % des possesseurs de Surface utilisaient régulièrement cette fonction. Dix ans plus tard, le montant a presque doublé et le terrain de bataille s’est déplacé vers l’intelligence artificielle.
Un divorce facturé 2 600 dollars
La reprise sert d’appât vers une machine positionnée tout en haut du panier : le Surface Laptop Ultra démarre à 2 599,99 dollars, un tarif de MacBook Pro bien équipé. Présenté comme le Surface le plus puissant jamais produit, il embarque du matériel NVIDIA RTX Spark pensé pour l’IA locale et la 3D exigeante, adopte une charge magnétique en USB-C et promet des performances maintenues sur batterie. Ce dernier point vise frontalement le terrain où les puces Apple Silicon ont bâti leur réputation. La cible est assumée : les professionnels qui renouvellent machinalement leur MacBook à chaque génération.
Les éditions précédentes du programme étaient cantonnées aux États-Unis, et rien n’indique pour l’heure qu’une déclinaison française soit prévue cette fois. Si vous espériez en profiter depuis l’Hexagone, mieux vaut donc tempérer vos ardeurs. Le montant maximal devrait par ailleurs dépendre du modèle rendu et de son état, selon la logique habituelle de ce type d’offre. L’outil d’estimation nous donnait une valeur de reprise à un peu plus de 300 dollars pour notre Macbook Pro (16 pouces, M1 Pro, 16 GB de RAM et 1 TB de stockage). La boutique en ligne de Microsoft cumule déjà reprise et remises directes sur les autres machines de la gamme Surface.

articles.title: Nvidia RTX Spark AI laptops hit pre-order — here are 3 I recommend
articles.text:
Pre-orders open for Nvidia’s RTX Spark workstations — and these are the 3 local AI laptops I’d buy for business
The most expensive configurations will set you back $7,000
Running AI locally is becoming an increasingly attractive option for small businesses that want more control over their data, predictable computing costs, and the ability to experiment with the technology without relying on cloud services. Nvidia's new RTX Spark laptops could make that easier, combining powerful processors, Blackwell graphics, and large amounts of unified memory in portable computers.
Pre-orders are now open, with the first models scheduled to ship on October 16. Prices start at $2,599.99, although more powerful configurations can cost considerably more.
There are models from all of the major manufacturers, including Microsoft, Asus, Lenovo, HP, and Dell, but for small businesses looking to run local AI models and develop applications, these are the three laptops I'd recommend.
My top 3 RTX Spark laptops for AI
Microsoft's 15-inch Surface Laptop Ultra is one of the least expensive ways to get Nvidia's new RTX Spark hardware, with pre-orders starting at $2,599.99. The Surface Laptop Ultra is available with up to 128GB of unified memory.
I'd consider the entry-level model for a small business exploring internal AI assistants, document analysis, coding tools, and other relatively modest local AI applications.
HP's 16-inch laptop features a 3K OLED touchscreen and can be configured with up to 128GB of unified memory.
HP's 24GB and 32GB versions use a smaller RTX Spark chip, while configurations with 48GB or more feature the full 20-core Grace CPU and 6,144-core Blackwell GPU.
For more demanding AI projects, I'd look closely at the 64GB or 128GB versions rather than just choosing the cheapest model.
The Asus ProArt P16 is a good choice for small businesses that combine AI development with creative work. It features a 16-inch display and offers up to 128GB of unified memory and 2TB of storage.
Why RTX Spark makes sense for small businesses
One of the main attractions of running AI locally is the ability to process information without sending every request to a cloud-based service, which could be handy for anyone working with confidential documents, proprietary code, customer information, internal research, and so on.
Nvidia's RTX Spark platform combines a Grace CPU with a Blackwell GPU, with unified memory configurations ranging from 24GB to 128GB. The full chip includes a 20-core CPU and 6,144-core GPU, while the lower-end version has an 18-core CPU and 5,120-core GPU.
The memory configuration is particularly important for local AI, since larger models can require much more memory than conventional business applications. That said, memory capacity alone doesn't guarantee performance. The size of the model, its precision, software compatibility, and available GPU resources all affect how well it runs.
For a small business taking its first steps into local AI, I'd start by looking at the Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra, which is one of the more affordable RTX Spark options.
If your business needs more memory for larger models, HP's OmniBook Ultra 16 is worth considering, particularly in its 64GB and 128GB configurations.
For companies combining AI development with video editing, image generation, and other creative applications, the Asus ProArt P16 offers another option.
The new RTX Spark laptops are scheduled to start shipping on October 16, with pre-orders available through Best Buy and other manufacturers.

articles.title: Galaxy A04s perde suporte após três anos no Brasil • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Galaxy A04s perde suporte após três anos no Brasil
Celular da Samsung recebeu apenas uma grande atualização de sistema no mercado nacional.
A Samsung encerrou o suporte de software para o Galaxy A04s. O smartphone foi retirado da lista oficial de aparelhos que recebem updates de segurança, indicando que não irá receber mais novas versões do Android nem patches regulares de proteção.
A última atualização trouxe o pacote de segurança de agosto de 2026. A mudança não significa que o celular deixará de funcionar, mas a ausência de novos patches pode aumentar a exposição a vulnerabilidades descobertas daqui para frente.
O Galaxy A04s foi lançado globalmente em agosto de 2022 com Android 12 e termina seu ciclo rodando Android 14, com a interface One UI 6.1. Ele chegou ao Brasil pelo preço de R$ 1.299.
A Samsung cumpriu o ciclo previsto para o aparelho e ofereceu duas grandes atualizações de sistema: o celular saiu de fábrica com o Android 12, passou pelo 13 e, depois, o Android 14. O aparelho ganhou atualizações de segurança durante cerca de quatro anos após seu lançamento global.
No entanto, o ciclo de suporte acompanhou a estreia global em 2022, e não sua chegada ao Brasil. Por aqui, o Galaxy A04s só foi lançado oficialmente em fevereiro de 2023 e já chegou com Android 13. Portanto, quem comprou o aparelho no lançamento nacional recebeu apenas uma grande atualização de sistema.
A Samsung removeu o Galaxy A04s da página de updates mensais, trimestrais ou semestrais, mas ainda é possível encontrá-lo em marketplaces e vendedores independentes no Brasil. Anúncios no Mercado Livre mostram aparelhos anunciados como novos por quase R$ 1 mil.
O Galaxy A04s foi lançado no país com 4 GB de RAM, 64 GB de armazenamento e processador Exynos 850. A ficha técnica inclui tela LCD de 6,5 polegadas com resolução HD+ e taxa de atualização de 90 Hz, câmera principal de 50 megapixels e bateria de 5.000 mAh com carregamento de 15 W.
Considerando o fim das atualizações, o Galaxy A04s passa a exigir cautela de quem ainda pretende comprá-lo usado ou em estoque antigo. Modelos de entrada mais recentes já recebem períodos bem maiores de suporte oficial. Os Galaxy A07 e Galaxy A17, por exemplo, chegaram ao Brasil com promessa de seis atualizações do Android e seis anos de patches de segurança.

articles.title: NVIDIA Throws RTX Spark Launch Party in Berlin on October 16. You Can Be There, it's Public
articles.text:
Friday, October 9th 2026
NVIDIA Throws RTX Spark Launch Party in Berlin on October 16. You Can Be There, it's Public
NVIDIA is marking the retail launch of its RTX Spark laptops with a public party in Berlin, and anyone aged 18 or older can attend. The RTX Spark Launch Celebration takes place on October 16, the same day the first laptops ship, at XPERION on Alexanderplatz. NVIDIA is presenting it as "a new beginning for Windows PCs" in the run-up to GTC Berlin, and the evening combines a stage program with hands-on demo stations and a laptop raffle. The company is even lighting up the Berlin TV Tower in NVIDIA green for the occasion.
Entry is free, although registration through Luma is required beforehand. The queue opens at 18:00 local time and doors open at 18:45. XPERION sits inside the Saturn store at Alexanderplatz 3, and capacity is limited, especially for the stage show. NVIDIA recommends arriving early for that reason, since that is how visitors secure entry, a spot in the raffle, and a goodie bag. The Berlin event is a chance to try RTX Spark hardware in person, across AI, creative, and gaming workloads.Stage Shows, Demos, and Jensen-Signed LaptopsOn stage, NVIDIA has lined up creators AlexiBexi, FalcoPunch, and Alex Wätzel, along with talks from CD Projekt Red, the studio behind The Witcher 3 and Cyberpunk 2077. Demo stations will let visitors try RTX Spark systems in creative apps, AI agent workflows, and games. That includes DLSS 5, which only debuted in early September with NBA 2K27. Another highlight is the raffle, where NVIDIA is giving away five ASUS ProArt P14 laptops signed by CEO Jensen Huang. All guests also get a goodie bag with a six-month GeForce NOW Ultimate membership that NVIDIA values at over €130 (while supplies last). Food and drinks are covered, too, and select RTX Spark laptops will be sold on-site with special offers.
What RTX Spark Brings to Windows PCsAs a refresher, RTX Spark is NVIDIA's Arm-based platform for Windows PCs, announced together with Microsoft at Computex in June. The N1X chip at its center pairs up to 20 Grace CPU cores with a Blackwell RTX GPU carrying up to 6,144 CUDA cores, and it supports as much as 128 GB of unified memory. NVIDIA offers the N1X in two versions. The faster one has 20 CPU cores, a 6,144-core GPU, and anywhere from 24 to 128 GB of unified memory. The other version drops to 18 CPU cores and a 5,120-core GPU with 24 to 32 GB, and it is only meant for laptops. 
NVIDIA says the chip delivers one petaflop of FP4 AI performance and can run language models with around 120 billion parameters locally, without sending data to the cloud. Creators are the second target, and Adobe is reworking Photoshop and Premiere for the Windows on Arm platform. Gaming comes third, where NVIDIA claims over 100 FPS at 1440p in AAA titles with DLSS 5. Those are NVIDIA's own numbers, so reviews of retail units will have to show how the chip holds up in practice.
NVIDIA also released its RTX Spark toolkit for game developers in July, and EA, Embark, and Ubisoft signed on at Gamescom with titles such as Apex Legends, ARC Raiders, and Anno 117: Pax Romana. At the October 7 event, Microsoft promised "hundreds" of games on day one and showed Gears of War: E-Day running at 60 FPS on the Surface Laptop Ultra.
RTX Spark Pricing and AvailabilityNVIDIA and Microsoft had teased October 7 as the big day, and that is when preorders opened at Microsoft's Windows and Surface event in San Francisco, with the first laptops shipping on October 16. Microsoft's Surface Laptop Ultra starts at $2,599 with the 18-core N1X chip, a 5,120-core Blackwell GPU, and 24 GB of unified memory, and it climbs to a steep $5,899 with the 20-core chip and 128 GB memory. The ASUS ProArt P14 being raffled in Berlin also starts at $2,599.99 in the US, and ASUS had already pointed to an October launch for its larger ProArt P16, which starts at $2,799.99. Dell, HP, Lenovo, and MSI have laptops in the first wave as well, and NVIDIA says compact RTX Spark desktops will follow in November.
GTC Berlin Follows Days LaterThe launch party is also a warm-up for GTC Berlin, which runs from October 20 to 22. CEO Jensen Huang's keynote is set for October 21 at the Tempodrom, from 11:00 to 13:00 CEST, and it will also be livestreamed for those who can't make it. As for the RTX Spark launch party, readers in or around Berlin who want hands-on time with RTX Spark before buying are advised to register soon, as a free event with signed laptops up for grabs probably won't have room to spare for long.
