articles.title: IA : 100 milliards de dollars, c'est la petite somme que Softbank cherche pour financer ses paris dans l'intelligence artificielle
articles.text:
L'argent dans le monde de l'intelligence artificielle coule à flots depuis des années. Et Softbank espère que ça va continuer, vu la tournée actuelle de son patron, Masayoshi Son.
Si l'on a l'habitude d'entendre parler des levées de fonds prodigieuses d'Anthropic (Claude) ou d'OpenAI (ChatGPT), il y a aussi une société incontournable aujourd'hui dans le secteur de l'IA : Softbank. Le géant japonais des télécommunications est en effet un peu partout, que ce soit dans le projet Stargate aux USA, ou en France, où le groupe veut investir 75 milliards d'euros dans des data centers. Autant dire que Softbank a toujours besoin de plus de cash, et qu'il sait où en trouver.
Masayoshi Son cherche à convaincre des géants du Golfe d'investir encore 100 milliards de dollars dans des projets IA
Selon des informations du Financial Times, le patron de Softbank Masayoshi Son a multiplié les rencontres ces dernières semaines avec des investisseurs du Golfe, dont plusieurs personnages importantes des Émirats arabes unis.
Et son objectif apparaît assez démesuré : récolter auprès d'eux quelque 100 milliards de dollars. Cet argent lui permettrait de créer un fonds, destiné à acquérir des entreprises, pour ensuite améliorer leur fonctionnement et leurs opérations grâce à l'IA et d'autres technologies de pointe.
Jusqu'où les grandes fortunes du Moyen-Orient sont-elles prêtes à ouvrir leur portefeuille ?
Le projet arrive au moment où le marché commence à (légèrement) se questionner sur l'ampleur exceptionnelle des investissements IA. Hier ainsi, après la découverte du chiffre d'affaires annualisé d'OpenAI, beaucoup moins important qu'attendu, le Nasdaq et ses grands noms ont fini la journée sur le recul.
Et du côté des fortunes du Moyen-Orient, on a déjà engagé des capitaux très importants dans l'intelligence artificielle, via les fonds souverains des nations de cette région. On estime que l'an dernier, l'ensemble des fonds souverains de la planète avaient ainsi dépensé 66 milliards de dollars dans l'IA et les infrastrucrtures digitales, avec, à l'avant-garde, des grands noms comme le fond émirati Mubadala ou bien le fonds saoudien PIF. Est-ce qu'ils auront envie d'aller plus loin, alors que le doute s'installe ?

articles.title: Juan Roig, presidente de Mercadona: "Tenemos que pagar impuestos. Es algo muy bueno y muy sano, y es para estar orgullosos"
articles.text:
Ser una de las mayores fortunas del país hace que todo lo que digas cobre una relevancia especial. Bien lo sabe Juan Roig, presidente de Mercadona, que además de ocupar el cuarto puesto de la lista Forbes de los grandes patrimonios patrios está al frente de una de las compañías españolas con mayor volumen de ingresos. Sus reflexiones sobre el futuro de la alimentación, los precios y la política se analizan casi de forma quirúrgica, palabra por palabra; pero hay un tema que suele despertar un interés especial: los impuestos.
A lo largo de los últimos años Roig ha insistido en que los empresarios deben "salir del armario", perder la "vergüenza" a reconocer que ganan dinero y sentirse igualmente “orgullosos” de pagar tributos. Él, asegura, lo está.
Repasando las cifras. La voz de Roig tiene un peso especial entre la clase empresarial españolas. Y es lógico. Según las estimaciones de Fortune, el presidente de Mercadona es el cuarto español más acaudalado, con un patrimonio de alrededor de 7.900 millones de euros. Solo lo superan Amancio y Sandra Ortega (Inditex) y Rafael del Pino (Ferrovial). El valenciano está al frente además de una de las empresas españolas con mayor volumen de facturación. Solo en 2025 ingresó 41.858 millones, el 95% de ellos en el mercado español.
Hay ganancias, hay impuestos. Las cifras anteriores no solo dan una pista del patrimonio de Roig y Mercadona. Nos hablan también de la carga impositiva que soportan. En su memoria anual de 2025 la compañía valenciana asegura que, su "contribución tributaria" total ascendió a 3.383 millones, "incluyendo tributos soportados y recaudados". El 91% de esa cifra se corresponde al negocio español (3.110). Como referencia, supone un 11% más que en el ejercicio 2024.
Si hablamos solo "tributos soportados" directamente en España, la cifra ronda los 1.738 millones de euros: 469 se corresponden con el Impuesto de Sociedades, 202 con impuestos y tasas y 1.067 con cotizaciones a la Seguridad Social.
"Es algo muy bueno y muy sano". Con esas cifras sobre la mesa se entiende mejor que hace un año, durante la celebración de la 40ª edición del congreso Aecoc, Roig llamase la atención al celebrar el orgullo de pagar impuestos. Ante un público formado por alrededor de 1.500 personas, la gran mayoría empresarios, el presidente de Mercadona reivindicó el valor (y orgullo) de los tributos.
"Tenemos que pagar impuestos. Es algo muy bueno y muy sano, y es para estar orgullosos". Si añadió algún matiz crítico fue solo para cuestionar la gestión posterior de esos recursos, no la recaudación en sí. "El problema no es pagar mucho, es cómo se gestiona. Hay que pagarlos. Luego los demás los tienen que saber gestionar", proclamó ante sus colegas de sector en un auditorio que lleva su nombre, el Roig Arena.
UN VISTAZO A...
"Es un orgullo para nosotros". Las palabras de Roig son interesantes porque no son fruto de una reflexión aislada y puntual. Al contrario. Llega con repasar la hemeroteca para comprobar que, con mayor o menor énfasis, el empresario valenciano lleva años incidiendo en el mismo mensaje.
Lo hizo en 2015, en tiempos de Cristóbal Montoro, cuando reivindicó que para Mercadona "es un orgullo pagar impuestos". Y volvió a hacerlo en 2021, cuando fue un paso más allá: "Si queremos servicios públicos, justicia y sanidad y formación universal, hay que pagar impuestos. Para nosotros es un orgullo pagar impuestos". En alguna ocasión, incluso rompió una lanza a favor del Impuesto de Sociedades, al que su grupo destinó casi 500 millones de euros en 2025: "Pagar el IS significa que hemos ganado dinero y podemos contribuir con España. Ni las calles, ni las carreteras vienen del aire".
¿Es la opinión generalizada? No lo parece. El año pasado, durante el mismo congreso en el que Roig reivindicó el "orgullo" de pagar tributos, el presidente de Aecoc deslizó que la subida de gravámenes también tiene su cara B.
"El hecho de que los impuestos crezcan, no ayuda a la disponibilidad de dinero de los hogares. Es indiscutible que se paguen impuestos, como dice Juan Roig, pero la recaudación, y es un dato objetivo, es mucho mayor hoy que hace cinco años", alegó el directivo tras recordar que la recaudación fiscal había subido una media de un 6% en los cinco años anteriores, más que la renta de los hogares.
"Revisión a fondo". No hay que irse tan atrás. Hace unas semanas el Instituto de Estudios Económicos (IEE), el centro de estudios de la CEOE, lanzó una publicación que se suma a la tesis de que una presión fiscal alta frena la inversión, la productividad y el empleo. De ahí que el presidente del IEE, Íñigo Fernández de Mesa, reclamase "una revisión completa y profunda" del sistema fiscal español.
Durante el mismo acto señaló la presión fiscal que soporta la vivienda en España y abogó por una "revisión a fondo" del gasto público. "Hay que analizar a dónde ha ido a parar el dinero recaudado de más con el aumento de presión fiscal. Lo mismo que en las empresas se hacen auditorías, el gasto público lo necesita", señaló Fernández de Mesa. La CEOE también ha advertido que la presión fiscal en España es mayor que la media europea y que afecta incluso a los salarios.
Tributos… y contexto. Que Roig celebre el "orgullo" de pagar tributos no significa que en ocasiones haya pedido flexibilidad o se haya mostrado crítico. En marzo, tras el estallido de la guerra de Irán y con el coste de combustibles y materias primas disparándose por el cierre de Ormuz, el fundador de Mercadona abogó por una reducción del IVA alimentario al 0%. El empresario reconoció que la supresión del impuesto sobre el consumo en alimentación "estaría muy bien, nos encantaría, aunque no depende de nosotros".
El valenciano también se ha mostrado crítico con las diferencias en la presión fiscal entre regiones. "Me gustaría que en toda España pagásemos los mismos impuestos", argumentó hace unos meses. "Una cajera nuestra en Mercadona paga más impuestos aquí (en Valencia) que una cajera en Madrid y eso es un problema que deben arreglar los políticos. Todo el mundo se queja, pero tenemos que ganar el mismo dinero. Y eso es una cosa que tienen que arreglar los político".

articles.title: Des milliers de photos intimes volées : la France fait tomber le site NudeLeaksTeens et arrête deux cybercriminels
articles.text:
Deux frères, âgés de 21 et 25 ans, ont été interpellés dans le nord de la France cette semaine, annonce la procureure de Paris, Laure Beccuau. Selon les forces de l’ordre, le duo était à la tête de NudeLeaksTeens, une plateforme criminelle qui exposait les images intimes de plus de 17 000 femmes et jeunes filles, dont des mineures d’âge. Le titre du site ne laisse aucune place au doute quant à son contenu. En français, NudeLeaksTeens signifie « fuite d’images intimes d’adolescentes ». Dans le détail, trois sites appartenant au même empire ont été fermés : nlthub.pk, nltvids.com et nudeleaksteens.com.
À lire aussi : De « nombreuses plaintes » – la CNIL dénonce l’explosion des « Google » des fuites de données
Piratages et revenge porn
Le site vendait des « packs » de contenus intimes qui provenaient de plusieurs sources. Les autorités indiquent que les images venaient notamment de piratage de comptes sur les réseaux sociaux ou d’opérations de « revenge porn ». Le site reposait sur un mode de fonctionnement particulièrement pervers.
« Les utilisateurs étaient incités, contre récompense en monnaie virtuelle, à fournir des informations d’identification de chaque victime », explique Laure Beccuau.
Chaque femme était ainsi « recensée individuellement sous son vrai nom », puis indexée selon son âge, son lieu de résidence, son métier et un « niveau de beauté noté sur 10 ». De facto, une image volée pouvait être rattachée à une identité précise. Des individus malveillants pouvaient ainsi se mettre à harceler la victime, que ce soit sur Internet ou dans la vie réelle, voire à lui extorquer de l’argent en échange de ses photos.
À lire aussi : Microsoft Copilot confie parfois vos photos intimes à des êtres humains
700 000 euros de cryptomonnaies saisis
Sans surprise, le site faisait payer ses utilisateurs en cryptomonnaies. En mettant en vente les photos intimes de femmes, les deux frères ont amassé un important butin. Les enquêteurs français ont en effet saisi environ 700 000 euros d’actifs numériques, soit près de 782 500 dollars. Le site proposait des paiements en Bitcoin, en Ether, en Litecoin et en USDT.
Ce coup de filet est le résultat d’une longue enquête, menée avec l’aide de la police et de la justice américaines. En France, les investigations sont surtout dirigées par la section cyber du parquet de Paris, par le biais de l’unité cyber de la gendarmerie nationale. Le duo à l’origine de NudeLeaksTeens est accusé de détention et de diffusion en bande organisée de l’image d’un mineur à caractère pornographique, de blanchiment en bande organisée et de fourniture d’une plateforme en ligne à des fins illicites.
« Les personnes victimes de la diffusion non consentie de contenus intimes sur la plateforme NudeLeaksTeens, françaises ou étrangères, sont invitées à contacter l’Unité nationale cyber », déclare Laure Beccuau.
Les victimes sont invitées à se faire connaître à l’adresse [email protected]. Si vous êtes concernée, commencez par conserver un maximum de preuves, comme des captures d’écran ou des liens. Signalez ensuite les contenus aux plateformes qui les hébergent et déposez une plainte auprès des autorités.
Cette opération survient quelques mois après le démantèlement d’un autre réseau qui s’en prenait aux plus jeunes. En mars dernier, Europol a en effet annoncé l’arrestation de 30 suspects liés au gang « The Com », spécialisé dans l’extorsion et la production de contenus pédopornographiques. Les pirates du gang piégeaient les enfants et les adolescents sur les réseaux sociaux, les messageries ou les jeux en ligne, avant de les faire chanter. Plus de 60 victimes avaient été identifiées, dont quatre mineurs sauvés in extremis, durant l’opération. Citons aussi la fermeture de Motherless, un site pornographique de partage de photos et de vidéos montrant des abus sexuels, en mai dernier.

articles.title: Denuvo Reportedly Blocks Hypervisor Bypass Used in Over 60 Games
articles.text:
Friday, October 9th 2026
Denuvo Reportedly Blocks Hypervisor Bypass Used in Over 60 Games
Denuvo anti-tamper protection has recently been struggling with a surge of game cracks appearing almost immediately after, and sometimes even before, the launch of the latest AAA games. In extreme cases, such as with Silent Hill: Townfall, cracks have appeared days before the official release during the pre-release period. However, this trend seems to be changing. With the release of Star Wars: Galactic Racer, the game is reportedly resisting a classical hypervisor-based workaround that was previously used to bypass the company's anti-piracy measures in many new game titles. As readers might recall, this racing game launched on October 6, but as of today, no successful bypass using the established method has emerged.
The hypervisor workaround takes advantage of virtualization technology that operates below Windows, allowing it to interfere with how a protected game detects certain system features without directly removing Denuvo's checks from its executable. Its relative simplicity helped make it a practical alternative to more labor-intensive cracking methods, with reports attributing successful bypasses across more than 60 games to this approach. The latest development suggests that the technique may no longer work as reliably against newer implementations of Denuvo.Neither Irdeto, Denuvo's developer, nor the game's publisher has publicly confirmed the change thought any documentation or public source, but it seems to be effective as the game crack is still absent even days after the launch. For Irdeto, delaying piracy during a game's initial sales window is a crucial objective of Denuvo. The apparent setback for crackers could therefore give publishers additional time to generate launch revenue, even if the workaround is eventually replaced. For now, claims that the change definitively blocks the method across all 60-plus games remain unverified. The situation highlights the ongoing battle between anti-piracy developers and cracking groups, with neither side guaranteed a permanent advantage.
Source:

articles.title: 'Just silly enough to be perfect' — I’ve seen Rivian’s Ghostbusters Ecto-R1 in action, and it's packed with Halloween tricks
articles.text:
'Just silly enough to be perfect' — I’ve seen Rivian’s Ghostbusters Ecto-R1 in action and Slimer would definitely approve
Rivian’s EVs get a paranormal makeover
Rivian loves a seasonal update, especially its now-annual Halloween drop, which has become a treat for owners of its electric vehicles. But for 2026, Rivian has done its best — and succeeded — to beat previous themes like Knight Rider and Back to the Future, with a pretty perfect pairing.
With the Halloween update rolling out now — R2 is the 2026.36.40 version, and R1 is 2026.36.0 — owners of the R1S, R1T, and R2 can turn their Rivian into a modern-day Ecto-1 thanks to a Ghostbusters-themed software update.
Rivian even tagged in Bill Murray — ahem, Dr. Peter Venkman — for the spot teasing this year's update, and created a very special vehicle to celebrate: the Ecto-R1.
And if you happened to be in New York City last night and thought you spotted Mr. Murray taking a loop around the block in what looked like an Ecto-1, I can confirm that was indeed the case. At a special event, I saw Rivian's custom Ecto-R1 in person, with the R1S sporting a custom white paint job, Ghostbusters logos, and a full array of paranormal-fighting equipment up top. I also got to see Bill Murray take the passenger seat for a ride before spending a bit of time with the Halloween update itself in the R2.
For the custom Rivian that pays tribute to the classic Ecto-Mobile, the design team really paid attention to the details. Up top, you won't just find the paranormal-fighting gear, but also vintage-style police lights that do a good job of mirroring the original. There's even more equipment tucked into the rear of the vehicle, making this feel like a proper Ghostbusters conversion rather than simply an R1S with a fresh coat of paint and a few logos.
Of course, all that extra equipment comes at a cost to the R1S's silhouette, with the roof-mounted gear and lights adding some extra height. But that's part of the fun here: Rivian has taken its electric SUV and given it a treatment that feels right at home in the Ghostbusters universe.
Murray seemed to appreciate the attention to detail, too. Describing the Ecto-R1, he said it was "just technical enough, and just silly enough to be perfect; it's really perfect." After taking in the lights and all the sound effects, he summed it up as a 'cool car'. It's clear he enjoyed the commercial, too, even teasing the quick joyride at the end during his remarks at the event.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
While the custom Ecto-R1 is a one-off recreation, Rivian's Halloween update brings some Ghostbusters to owners' vehicles. I got to experience the update in the R2, where the main display transforms into a full-on paranormal-fighting control panel called Trick or Treat mode.
It's far from just a simple Halloween wrap as well. The screen takes on the look of a piece of Ghostbusters equipment, complete with switches, buttons, sound effects, games, and controls for the vehicle's interior ambient lighting and exterior lights.
And it's not just a static screen, either. The panel is packed with little touches that make it feel like you're operating the equipment on a real ghost-hunting mission. Try flipping the switch for the radar equipment, for instance, and a ghostly hand pops up to flip it back off. It's a small detail, but one that shows just how much thought Rivian has put into this update.
There are several preset light and sound shows to choose from, including Ecto-1, Proton Pack, Slimer, Ghost Trap, Peter Venkman, and Random. These let you quickly activate a combination of interior and exterior lighting effects and audio, while Manual and Motion modes give you a little more control over the experience.
Motion Mode seems particularly fun, letting the effects trigger when someone moves nearby. I'd absolutely want to try that one in a parking deck, if only to see the reaction of an unsuspecting passerby.
And yes, you can blast the Ghostbusters theme, too. Between the full siren, the other sound effects, and the coordinated lighting, there's plenty here to make your Rivian feel like it's ready to answer a call from the Ghostbusters.
The experience extends beyond the main display, too. Rivian carries the Ghostbusters theme over to the screen behind the steering wheel and its app on both Android and iOS, so the seasonal makeover isn't limited to one screen. It's a surprisingly comprehensive treatment, and one that makes the update feel like a proper event rather than a quick seasonal Easter egg.
Of course, not every paranormal investigation needs to happen on the road. For those moments when you're parked or charging, Rivian has also included an arcade with games to keep you occupied.
Mallow Mash challenges you to pop as many Mini-Puft marshmallow men as possible. Murray himself noted that the game was quite hard, so even Dr. Peter Venkman might need a little practice.
Between the preset effects, motion-triggered surprises, soundtrack, and arcade games, Rivian has given owners a whole paranormal playground to explore — no proton pack required.
Beyond Bill Murray, who stars in the ad, Gil Kenan — co-writer of Ghostbusters: Afterlife and director and co-writer of Ghostbusters: Frozen Empire — was brought in to help shape it.
It's a fitting pairing for an update that leans so heavily into the franchise's look, sound, and humor. The custom Ecto-R1 is the attention-grabbing centerpiece, but the software makes the experience accessible to Rivian owners who don't have a fully kitted-out paranormal investigation vehicle in their garage.
And that's what makes this year's Halloween drop particularly good. Rivian has taken something as ordinary as a seasonal software update and turned it into a playful tribute to a beloved franchise, complete with the lights, sounds, and interactive touches that make it feel special. It might even be enough to get a few Ghostbusters super-fans looking at a Rivian in a whole new light.

articles.title: We tested gaming performance in 17-year-old Windows 7 against Windows 11 on a modern gaming PC — older operating system delivers advantages in some scenarios
articles.text:
We tested gaming performance in 17-year-old Windows 7 against Windows 11 on a modern gaming PC — older operating system delivers advantages in some scenarios
Can an old OS beat a new modern rig?
After the rough reception of Windows Vista, Windows 7 launched in 2009 to largely positive reviews. Even 17 years later, it remains one of the most beloved versions of Windows ever released. But how does this nearly two-decade-old operating system hold up on modern hardware? We managed to install Windows 7 on a modern PC and put it to the test across eight DirectX 11 games and two DirectX 9 titles to see how its gaming performance compares to Windows 11 today.
At launch, Windows 7 was very similar to Windows Vista in many respects. Vista had introduced significant changes under the hood compared to Windows XP, including technologies such as SuperFetch, ReadyBoost, ReadyDrive, new asynchronous APIs, and other I/O improvements. It also introduced native processor power management and various memory-management enhancements. On the visual side, Vista was the first version of Windows to feature Windows Aero, with its distinctive glass-like window borders.
Windows 7 retained many of these underlying technologies while addressing several of Vista’s biggest criticisms. One notable improvement was greater control over User Account Control (UAC), allowing users to adjust how frequently they received UAC prompts. In Vista, these prompts could appear far too often, becoming a major source of frustration for many users.
Windows 7 also benefited from something that had nothing to do with the operating system itself: more powerful hardware. When Vista launched, many mid-range and budget PCs struggled to deliver smooth performance, particularly when using more demanding visual features such as Windows Aero. By 2009, however, PC hardware had advanced considerably, and the performance required to run these features smoothly was no longer a significant concern for most users.
The Challenge of Running Windows 7 on a Modern PC
Getting Windows 7 running on modern hardware is not as straightforward as installing a current version of Windows. At 17 years old, the operating system predates many of the technologies used by modern PCs, meaning driver support is extremely limited. For example, Windows 7 does not include native NVMe or USB 3.0 support, so the necessary drivers have to be slipstreamed into the installation ISO. Microsoft did eventually release patches that added NVMe support, but without injecting the appropriate drivers into the ISO, the Windows 7 installer will not recognize an NVMe drive.
Our system is based on AMD’s AM5 platform (with the full system specifications detailed later in the article), which presents another limitation: there are no official Windows 7 chipset drivers for the platform.
Fortunately, we are using an RDNA 2 GPU, which does have Windows 7 driver support, allowing us to use a relatively modern graphics card for our testing.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
The motherboard is also an important consideration. Modern motherboards that have dropped CSM (Compatibility Support Module) and legacy boot support can make installing Windows 7 considerably more difficult, and in some cases may prevent the operating system from booting altogether. Fortunately, our motherboard still supports CSM, so this was not an issue for our setup.
Test System
Windows 7 system specs
- AMD Radeon RX 6950 XT
- Ryzen 7 9800X3D
- 64GB (2x32GB) G.SKILL Flare X5 DDR5 @6000 MHz CL30
- Seagate Lightsaber FireCuda (530) NVMe SSD
- ASUS ROG STRIX B850-F Gaming WiFi
- Corsair Nautilus 360 RS AIO Cooler
- HAGS not supported by driver
- Windows 7 Ultimate 64-bit Service Pack 1 (Build 7601)
- AMD Adrenalin 22.6.1 for Windows 7 (2022)
Windows 11 system specs
- AMD Radeon RX 6950 XT
- Ryzen 7 9800X3D
- 64GB (2x32GB) G.SKILL Flare X5 DDR5 @6000 MHz CL30
- Seagate Lightsaber FireCuda (530) NVMe SSD
- ASUS ROG STRIX B850-F Gaming WiFi
- Corsair Nautilus 360 RS AIO Cooler
- HAGS not supported by driver
- Windows 11 25H2 (Build 26200.9278)
- AMD Adrenalin 22.6.1 for Windows 11 (2022)
For Windows 7, we disabled Secure Boot, enabled CSM, and set Boot Device Control to Legacy OPROM Only. Enabling CSM means that we no longer have access to Resizable BAR (it's not supported anyway). For Windows 11, we disabled VBS (Virtualization-Based Security) and HVCI (Hypervisor-Protected Code Integrity).
It is important to note that while we used Adrenalin 22.6.1 for both Windows 11 and Windows 7 testing, the two packages contain different internal driver versions. Although both packages were released in June 2022, the Windows 11 driver is based on a more advanced codebase than the Windows 7 driver.
In both cases, we performed a clean install of each operating system and filled the SSD to about 50-60%.
Performance Testing
We tested ten games in total: eight using DirectX 11 and two using DirectX 9. The DirectX 11 titles are the primary focus, as both systems support them natively. By comparison, our Windows 11 system will run DirectX 9 games through the D3D9On12 mapping layer, while our Windows 7 system will run them natively. There are ways to get around the use of D3D9On12 on Windows 11, but we want to evaluate the out-of-the-box experience that most gamers would encounter. As a result, we expect Windows 7 to have an advantage in the DirectX 9 titles.
It will become apparent in the results below that the advantages of each operating system will vary depending on whether we are CPU-limited or GPU-limited.
Metro 2033 Redux (DX11)
Metro 2033 Redux was released in 2014 and features a new lighting engine, higher visual fidelity, and new locations for certain levels. The game is predominantly GPU-bound, but there are moments when GPU utilization drops sharply as you traverse the game world. At these points, the CPU becomes the limiting factor, resulting in a corresponding drop in performance.
Although Windows 11 delivers a higher average frame rate, Windows 7 handles the CPU-related performance drops much better, resulting in significantly stronger 1% lows. Installing the AMD chipset drivers and enabling Resizable BAR improves 1% lows on Windows 11 slightly, but it still falls well behind Windows 7.
Windows 11’s more advanced graphics driver appears to provide an advantage in GPU-limited scenarios, while Windows 7’s lower CPU overhead offers more consistent frame pacing, though with lower peak performance.
Batman: Arkham Origins (DX11)
Batman: Arkham Origins runs on a modified version of Unreal Engine 3 and uses several DX11 enhancements such as Tessellation, Ambient Occlusion HBAO+, Percentage Closer Soft Shadows (PCSS), and Depth of Field (DoF).
When CPU-limited at 1080p, Windows 7 once again puts in a strong showing, outperforming Windows 11 in both average frame rate and 1% lows. Surprisingly, Windows 7 also comes out ahead at 4K in Origins, though with a far smaller advantage. As we will see throughout the remainder of our testing, however, this is a rare occurrence. Even so, Windows 7 maintains a slight performance advantage over Windows 11 at 4K in this title.
Batman: Arkham Knight (DX11)
Batman: Arkham Knight was both a critical and commercial success, despite a notoriously troubled PC launch plagued by severe bugs and major performance issues. Visually, however, the game still holds up remarkably well, and modern hardware is more than capable of brute-forcing this demanding PC port.
Windows 7 again delivers higher performance at 1080p when we are CPU-limited. Windows 11 jumps ahead when we become GPU-limited at 1440p and 4K.
Batman: Arkham City (DX11)
Batman: Arkham City was the second entry in the series, following Arkham Asylum, and the first to support DirectX 11. This introduced features such as tessellation, which adds greater geometric detail to characters and environments.
In Arkham City, our system is GPU-bound at every resolution tested, giving Windows 11 the advantage across the board.
The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt (DX11)
The Witcher 3 faced some controversy at launch over reductions in image quality compared to its initial reveal. CD Projekt Red quickly released a patch addressing these concerns and improving the game’s visuals. From a performance perspective, however, the game was extremely demanding at launch.
While the game is very GPU bound in general, at 1080p we did encounter a slight CPU bottleneck, which gave Windows 7 an advantage in 1% lows. At 1440p and 4K, Windows 11 takes a slight lead.
Control (DX11)
Control is the newest title we tested for this comparison, having launched in 2019. While the game introduced several ray tracing features, these were exclusive to the DirectX 12 API. Since Windows 7 does not support DirectX 12, we tested Control using DirectX 11 on both operating systems. Even without ray tracing, Control remains the most graphically advanced title in our Windows 11 vs Windows 7 comparison.
Windows 11 wins across the board. This is not a surprise, as we are GPU-limited across all resolutions tested.
Hitman: Absolution (DX11)
Hitman: Absolution was released in 2012 and was the first game to use the Glacier 2 engine. The updated engine could handle crowds of up to 1200 characters, which was unprecedented at the time. The game also featured several DirectX 11 enhancements, including global illumination and tessellation.
This is another game that pushes the GPU hard, regardless of resolution. Our test system was GPU-limited even at 1080p.
Hitman 2 (DX11)
Hitman 2 was released in 2018, making it the second-newest game in our operating system comparison. It features detailed environments, dense crowds, and full reflections across many surfaces, making it an impressive-looking title overall.
Hitman 2 is another example where our test system is GPU-limited at every resolution, giving Windows 11 a clean sweep across the board.
Batman: Arkham Asylum (DX9)
We now move to our first DirectX 9 game. As previously mentioned, Windows 7 should have an advantage here because our Windows 11 system must use the D3D9On12 mapping layer for DirectX 11 games. But just how much of an advantage?
Significant advantages for Windows 7 in average frame rate and 1% lows, especially at 1080p and 1440p. The advantage is reduced at 4K, but the performance is still smoother overall in Windows 7. Another translation layer, such as DXVK, may close the gap.
Borderlands 2 (DX9)
Borderlands 2 is our second DirectX 9 game and the final overall game tested.
Once again, another massive win for Windows 7 at the lower resolutions. The performance at 4K is virtually identical.
Bottom Line
Windows 11 is optimized for GPU-hungry games
The results are interesting, but perhaps not entirely surprising. The DirectX 9 results are largely in line with our expectations, given that Windows 11 must run these games through the D3D9On12 mapping layer.
The DirectX 11 results are more nuanced, but a clear trend emerges: Windows 7 has the advantage when we are CPU-limited, while Windows 11 performs better when we are GPU-limited. This makes sense given that Windows 11 uses graphics drivers built on a more advanced codebase, while Windows 7 is a leaner operating system with fewer background processes and, consequently, lower CPU overhead.
Microsoft has recently detailed its K2 plan, which aims to improve the performance and reliability of Windows 11. We hope these continued efforts to improve Windows 11 pay off. The lower CPU performance we observed in Windows 11 cannot be attributed to its most notable security features, such as VBS (Virtualization-Based Security) and HVCI (Hypervisor-Protected Code Integrity), as we disabled both during testing. Notably, Windows 7 does not support VBS or HVCI at the software level, while Windows 11 supports hardware virtualization extensions (such as Intel VT-x or AMD-V) and Second Level Address Translation (SLAT). Additionally, fixed-function hardware can reduce the impact of virtualization to varying degrees, based on the CPU architecture's capabilities. However, additional telemetry and other background services still pop up and use precious CPU cycles.
Using the latest chipset drivers and enabling features such as Resizable BAR does not help Windows 11 close the gap in CPU-limited scenarios by any significant margin. Ultimately, we would like to see Windows 11 become leaner and more efficient, as our results suggest there is still some performance left on the table, particularly on the CPU side.
Dan Mateescu is a PC enthusiast with many years of experience benchmarking PC hardware. In 2021, he started his own YouTube channel called 'Compusemble' where he benchmarks hardware in video games and the latest tech demos.

articles.title: Amazon construyó el satélite 1.000 de su red Leo y se prepara para competir con Starlink
articles.text:
Amazon construyó el satélite número 1.000 de su red de internet satelital Leo y está a semanas de lanzar comercialmente el servicio, confirmaron a Ars Technica tres ejecutivos del proyecto. La compañía busca disputarle a Starlink, de SpaceX, el control del mercado de banda ancha desde el espacio.
El hito se produjo en la fábrica de Amazon en Kirkland, Washington, donde la empresa ensambla sus satélites. Chris Weber, vicepresidente de negocios del proyecto, precisó que 396 satélites ya están en órbita y que todavía trabajan para ubicarlos en su posición final.
“El plan es lanzar el servicio inicial en 2026”, dijo Weber en la entrevista, al ser consultado sobre si la compañía cumpliría el plazo que había prometido para antes de que termine el año.
La conectividad satelital de banda ancha ya se usa para videojuegos, comercio y operaciones militares, y también para el acceso residencial a internet, según el relevamiento de Ars Technica sobre la industria.
De la fábrica al despegue
Rajeev Badyal, al frente del desarrollo de la constelación, explicó que pasar de prototipos a producción masiva fue el mayor desafío técnico del programa. “Construir un par de satélites es bastante sencillo, pero hacerlo a escala es exponencialmente más difícil”, afirmó.
Según Badyal, el primer lote de 27 satélites demandó seis meses de trabajo. Hoy la fábrica produce esa misma cantidad en una semana, un salto que atribuyó a mejoras continuas en los procesos de manufactura y en la capacitación de los técnicos.
Paul Palcisco, director de producción, contó que la planta de 170.000 pies cuadrados se construyó mientras el diseño del satélite todavía estaba en desarrollo. La compañía ocupó el edificio en diciembre de 2022 y lo convirtió en fábrica en apenas 15 meses.
“Apenas abrimos las puertas de esa fábrica, tuvimos que cambiarla”, reconoció Palcisco sobre los ajustes que debieron hacer una vez que arrancó la producción real.
La competencia con Starlink
Amazon presentó el proyecto en 2019 bajo el nombre Project Kuiper, con el objetivo de poner en órbita baja una constelación de 3.236 satélites, según la solicitud que la compañía presentó ante el regulador de telecomunicaciones de Estados Unidos. El 13 de noviembre de 2025 pasó a llamarse Amazon Leo, de acuerdo con el sitio oficial de la empresa.
Con 396 satélites en el cielo, la red todavía tiene menos del 15% de la flota que proyectó en sus primeros planes regulatorios, lo que explica por qué la compañía habla de un lanzamiento inicial y no de una cobertura global inmediata.
Hasta ahora, Starlink dominó casi en soledad el negocio de banda ancha satelital durante media década. OneWeb ofrece un servicio limitado, por lo que Amazon se perfila como el primer competidor real a escala global, según Ars Technica.
Badyal integra el equipo de Amazon Leo desde hace años, después de haber sido despedido de Starlink por Elon Musk, quien lo acusó de avanzar con demasiada cautela en el desarrollo de esa red, de acuerdo con el medio especializado.
La disputa entre ambas compañías también se trasladó al terreno comercial. Delta Air Lines eligió a Amazon por sobre Starlink para ofrecer internet a bordo de sus aviones, un acuerdo que, según Ars Technica, incomodó a Musk.
Rumbo al lanzamiento comercial
Amazon ya corre una vista previa empresarial de su antena de alto rendimiento Leo Ultra, pensada para empresas y gobiernos, que comenzó en noviembre de 2025 con clientes corporativos seleccionados, según el sitio oficial de la compañía.
Badyal confirmó que el próximo vuelo de regreso al servicio del cohete Vulcan llevará satélites de Amazon Leo, y que otro Vulcan ya se prepara en la plataforma vecina para un segundo lanzamiento este año.
La compañía firmó contratos con aerolíneas, navieras y gobiernos interesados en usar su red para conectividad a bordo, logística y otras operaciones, de acuerdo con lo relevado por Ars Technica entre clientes del proyecto.
Amazon todavía no reveló precios ni planes de suscripción para el público general. El servicio comercial inicial está previsto para 2026, según confirmaron sus propios ejecutivos en la entrevista.

articles.title: 730 millions de données volées : la police fait tomber Reacher, le moteur de recherche pirate de 3 ados
articles.text:
Un nouveau site pirate vient de tomber en France. Ce mardi 6 octobre, l’Office anti-cybercriminalité (OFAC) a interpellé trois administrateurs présumés de Reacher, qui a été rebaptisé Stryx au début de l’été. Pour rappel, un lookup est un moteur de recherche qui recense et revend des données personnelles issues de fuites et de piratages.
Trois mineurs de 17 ans à l’origine du site
Les trois suspects sont des mineurs de 17 ans, jusqu’ici inconnus de la justice. Ils sont soupçonnés de recel d’extraction frauduleuse de données, de détention et de transmission frauduleuse de données, en bande organisée. Ils encourent jusqu’à dix ans de prison. Leur procès est prévu en janvier 2027. Notez que ce n’est pas la première fois que de très jeunes pirates se retrouvent dans le viseur des autorités françaises. En juin, la France avait déjà arrêté sept jeunes hackers après plus de 1 500 cyberattaques perpétrées sur le territoire.
Créé en mars 2026, Stryx revendiquait 730 millions de lignes de données indexées, et affichait plus de 3 millions de requêtes. On tapait une information quelconque et le site renvoyait tout ce qu’il savait sur la personne. Il suffisait d’un nom, d’un numéro de téléphone, d’un IBAN ou même d’une plaque d’immatriculation. L’accès était gratuit ou sur abonnement, et les utilisateurs pouvaient acheter des crédits supplémentaires pour faire plus de recherches.
L’enquête a été ouverte le 15 mai, après un signalement de l’association e-Enfance. Dans la foulée de l’opération, les données des administrateurs, des clients et des utilisateurs du service ont été collectées, et les policiers sont en train de les analyser. Les utilisateurs de Reacher pourraient donc eux aussi se retrouver dans le viseur de la justice.
À lire aussi : De « nombreuses plaintes » – la CNIL dénonce l’explosion des « Google » des fuites de données
Les « lookups » dans le viseur de la police française
Reacher n’est pas un cas isolé. Les plateformes de ce type, souvent décrites comme des « Google » des fuites de données, sont dans le collimateur des autorités depuis plusieurs mois. En mai, un jeune de 19 ans a été mis en examen et placé en détention provisoire pour avoir créé et administré le site « C3N Backup ». Plus récemment, BrixHub, qui revendique 11 milliards de données, a fait réagir la ministre chargée du Numérique, Anne Le Hénanff. Le 5 octobre, celle-ci a signalé le lookup à la justice, dans l’intention de faire fermer le site.

articles.title: La web abierta se diseñó para humanos. Unos agentes de IA acaban de demostrarle a Wikipedia que ese pacto se ha roto
articles.text:
Wikipedia lleva 25 años siendo una web abierta hecha por personas y para personas. En un comunicado de la Wikimedia Foundation, la entidad que la gestiona ha contado que algo muy distinto irrumpió en sus servidores el pasado mes de mayo y ha dejado constancia de que el internet abierto que hemos conocido ha dejado de existir.
Según la fundación, hace unos meses recibieron un ataque que, si bien consiguió tumbar su servicio en momentos puntuales, no parecía haber provocado grandes destrozos, aunque sí provocó varios incidentes menores. La (cada vez menos) novedad es que estos atacantes no eran humanos, sino agentes de IA creados por OpenAI, y su plan iba bastante más allá de editar algunos textos.
Un ataque atípico. La Fundación Wikimedia quiso saber si le había pasado lo mismo que a otras organizaciones y si los incidentes de seguridad que habían detectado habían sido provocados por agentes de IA descontrolados. Lo investigó y sus sospechas se confirmaron: habían sido los agentes de IA de OpenAI.
Tal y como publicaba Reuters, los investigadores encontraron varias ediciones en sus wikis que atribuye a esos agentes, aunque casi todas eran pruebas en zonas de ensayo, sin visibilidad para los lectores.
Las normas de Wikipedia permiten el acceso de bots si se identifican como tal y la comunidad los aprueba. El problema es que, según el comunicado de Wikimedia, los agentes de IA de OpenAI no se identificaron como tal ni pidieron ese permiso. Simplemente entraron a la fuerza e hicieron un uso de las herramientas para algo que no habían sido creadas.
Etherpad, un proxy que no funcionó. Los agentes también intentaron comprometer Etherpad, el bloc de notas público que Wikimedia ofrece como servicio a su comunidad para facilitar las ediciones y la gestión de citas para sus entradas. No lo lograron.
Según detalló The Hacker News, los agentes de IA querían usarlo como proxy y usarlas como intermediario y traer datos de servicios remotos a modo de bloc de notas para gestionarlos después desde esa aplicación. Otros agentes, probablemente también de OpenAI, usaron Etherpad para anotar sus tareas. Wikimedia no vio que ese uso derivara en una coordinación del ataque, pero sí vio un patrón: las herramientas gratuitas que habían modificado debían servir como puerta para llegar a otros servicios.
Velocidad humana en tiempos de IA. Los agentes hicieron millones de solicitudes automáticas a las API públicas, rastrearon millones de páginas, sobre todo de Wikidata y Wikimedia Commons y lanzaron cientos de miles de consultas al Servicio de Consulta de Wikidata. Todo en cuestión de minutos. Todo ese tráfico pudo contribuir a que sus servidores se saturaran y se produjera una interrupción parcial del servicio.
Entre aquella caída producida en mayo y la explicación pública, fechada el 5 de octubre, pasaron meses. Wikimedia llegó a las conclusiones con su propia investigación, y no está claro si OpenAI le avisó antes, como señalaba The Register. De acuerdo a lo publicado por Reuters, Drew Pusateri, portavoz de OpenAI se limitó a un escueto: "Seguiremos compartiendo información relevante a medida que avance el trabajo" para comentar la aportación de OpenAI en esclarecer los términos del ataque que protagonizaron sus agentes. Llama la atención el contraste entre la velocidad que demostraron los agentes de AI durante la incursión en los servicios de Wikimedia, y la lentitud de los humanos para descubrir qué había pasado y quién había sido el responsable.
Servicio público pensado para personas. Wikipedia reúne más de 67 millones de artículos en más de 300 idiomas y hasta 15.000 millones de páginas vistas al mes, siendo uno de los pocos reductos que se mantienen de aquella de web abierta y gratuita. La fundación recuerda que nació para humanos, y sus voluntarios limpian el desorden que dejan los bots y agentes con sus incursiones. "La web abierta es un bien público. No debemos permitir que este comportamiento se convierta en la nueva normalidad para las personas u organizaciones que la mantienen", ha sentenciado al respecto en su comunicado.
En 2025, el ancho de banda del servicio se había incrementado un 50% desde 2024 debido al uso que hacen de ella los bots y agentes de IA. A su vez, el 65% del tráfico que más recursos gasta procedía del uso de esos bots rastreadores y de las consultas de la IA.
Wikipedia no está sola. Read the Docs es un servicio gratuito dedicado al alojamiento de documentos de todo tipo. En 2024 contó que un único rastreador de IA firmado por Meta descargó 73 TB en un solo mes. De ese volumen de documentos, casi 10 TB fueron en un solo día, y la factura superó los 5.000 dólares para la plataforma. Por supuesto, la empresa responsable del agente de IA no respondió a las reclamaciones económicas de los administradores del servicio.
Según recogía Ars Technica, al aplicar un bloqueo a esos rastreadores de IA, el tráfico de descargas cayó un 75% (de unos 800 GB diarios a unos 200 GB). SourceHut, una plataforma de código, atribuye a los rastreadores de IA más caídas y más costes de hardware, explicó la propia plataforma. Selena Deckelmann, directora de producto y tecnología de la Fundación, afirmó: "Los bots y los agentes son parte del futuro de la web, y las empresas que los sueltan y se lucran con ellos deben ayudar directamente a evitar y reparar el daño que pueden causar".
En Xataka | La IA se ha construido saqueando el contenido de Internet. Ahora hay gente que quiere cobrar por permitirlo

articles.title: Galaxy S26 Ultra baixa de preço para quem busca top de linha equilibrado • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Galaxy S26 Ultra baixa de preço para quem busca top de linha equilibrado
Galaxy S26 Ultra com Tela de Privacidade, câmera que filma em 8K e chip premium tem ótimo desconto com cupom e Pix
O Galaxy S26 Ultra (256 GB) está saindo por R$ 6.699 no Pix com o cupom CEL500 no Magazine Luiza. Lançado em fevereiro deste ano por R$ 11.499, o smartphone premium da Samsung com câmera de 200 MP e tela de 120 Hz fica 42% mais barato nesta oferta.
O Galaxy S26 Ultra se destaca por trazer uma câmera quádrupla traseira com sensor principal de 200 MP, clicando fotos com Estabilização Óptica de Imagem (OIS) e gravando vídeos em até 8K. A câmera frontal de 12 MP promete selfies detalhadas com Modo Retrato, além de registrar vídeos em 4K.
O telefone traz uma ampla tela AMOLED Dinâmico 2X de 6,9 polegadas com resolução QHD+ e taxa de atualização de 120 Hz, entregando imagens definidas e fluidas com o recurso HDR10+. O painel ainda conta com a Tela de Privacidade, funcionalidade que evita espiadas de outras pessoas em qualquer lugar.
Na lista dos melhores flagships de 2026, o Galaxy S26 Ultra é equipado com chip premium Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 e 12 GB de RAM para alto desempenho em tarefas mais pesadas. Já os 256 GB de armazenamento interno podem ser um pouco limitados, principalmente para quem desejar realizar fotos e vídeos com o máximo de resolução.
A bateria do smartphone topo de linha da Samsung tem 5.000 mAh, garantindo uma autonomia de até 31 horas de reprodução de vídeo. Ao usar um adaptador de 60 W, a função de carregamento rápido vai de 0 a 75% em meia hora.
Na parte de conexões, o dispositivo tem 5G, Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6.0, Ultra Wideband (UWB) e NFC. O telefone vem de fábrica com o Android 16 (One UI 8.5), mas receberá ao menos 7 grandes atualizações do sistema operacional.
O Galaxy S26 Ultra (R$ 6.699 no Pix com o cupom CEL500) é fabricado com estrutura de Armor Aluminum com acabamento traseiro em vidro reforçado com Gorilla Glass Victus 2. O certificado IP68 de resistência à poeira e à água protege o aparelho de mergulhos acidentais de até 1,5 metro por até 30 minutos.
Aviso de ética: ao clicar em um link de afiliado, o preço não muda para você e recebemos uma comissão.

articles.title: U.S. Manufacturing Grows as Backlogs Surge in September - EE Times
articles.text:
Economic activity in the U.S. manufacturing sector expanded in September for the ninth consecutive month, propelled by accelerating new orders and an expanding accumulation of unfilled factory backlogs. The sustained industrial performance helped buffer the broader economy against escalating trade friction and rising global commodity prices.
The Institute for Supply Management reported that its Manufacturing Purchasing Managers’ Index registered 54.5% in September, edging down just 0.1 percentage point from August’s reading of 54.6%. The reading marks nine straight months of industrial expansion following a 10-month contraction period and signals that the broader U.S. economy grew for a 23rd consecutive month. In ISM’s economic modeling, a PMI reading of 54.5% corresponds to a 2.4% annualized increase in real gross domestic product.
“In September, U.S. manufacturing activity remained in expansion territory,” said Susan Spence, chair of the ISM Manufacturing Business Survey Committee. “Of the five subindexes that make up the PMI, only New Orders and Employment grew faster than the previous month.”
New orders and factory backlogs
A fresh wave of demand reinforced factory output during the month, with the New Orders Index expanding for the ninth consecutive month to 55.3%, a 1.6 percentage point increase from August’s 53.7%. Factory output also remained robust: The Production Index registered 56.7%, marking its 11th consecutive month of growth, though slowing 1.6 percentage points from August’s 58.3%.
With new demand outstripping output capacity in several high-tech categories, order backlogs expanded at a faster rate. The Backlog of Orders Index jumped 4.6 percentage points to 56.4% in September, up from 51.8% in August, led by gains in computer and electronic products as well as fabricated metals.
Five of the nation’s six largest manufacturing industries—Computer & Electronic Products, Chemical Products, Transportation Equipment, Food, Beverage & Tobacco Products, and Machinery—reported higher new orders during the month.
ISM survey respondents highlighted burgeoning demand in semiconductor and defense supply chains, even as cross-border trade friction disrupted operations. “Coupled with supply chain lead times and pricing pressures, the factory backlog has nearly doubled,” noted an executive in the machinery sector. “Canada tariffs have impacted cross-border costs and left our supply chain team scrambling—those supply chains took years to develop and nurture—hurting the very lead times government buyers are concerned about.”
An executive in the computer and electronic products industry added that while manufacturing activity remains stable, “the U.S. tariff schedule is providing challenges,” citing difficulties in finding alternate supply sources outside China, local pushback on domestic data center construction, and persistent component shortages.
Factory hiring increased due to labor and material shortages
To keep pace with rising backlogs, industrial employers expanded payrolls at a faster rate. The ISM Employment Index rose 1.5 percentage points to 52.7% in September, compared with 51.2% in August, representing a third consecutive month of growth in manufacturing employment.
Survey panelists favored hiring over headcount reductions by a 1.5-to-1 ratio. Eight manufacturing industries reported expanding employment in September, led by Electrical Equipment, Appliances & Components, Primary Metals, and Wood Products. Among the nation’s six largest manufacturing sectors, Computer & Electronic Products and Transportation Equipment posted employment gains.
However, worker shortages and raw material bottlenecks continue to restrain factory output. “Our biggest challenge continues to be a severe shortage of workers, limiting our production output to meet demand,” said an executive in the fabricated metal products sector. “The second challenge is general availability of steel; the market is getting worse, and more production delays are expected as we gap out of needed material.”
Canada tariffs and Middle East war drive material costs higher
Despite ongoing output gains, factory managers face steep operational hurdles from soaring raw material prices, trade policy volatility, and geopolitical conflict. The Prices Index jumped 6.8 percentage points in September to 77.9%, up from 71.1% in August, reaching a level close to the 78.3% recorded in March at the start of the Iran war. The index indicates that raw material prices increased for the 24th consecutive month, with 58.6% of survey respondents reporting higher prices compared to 46.2% in August.
All six of the largest manufacturing sectors reported paying higher prices for raw materials in September. “The Prices Index reading is still being driven by (1) increases in steel and aluminum prices that impact the entire value chain, (2) tariffs applied to many imported goods and (3) increases in petroleum-based products as a result of the Middle East conflict,” Spence said.
Supply chain logistics remained under strain, with the Supplier Deliveries Index registering 59.0%. While down 0.3 percentage point from August’s 59.3%, the reading indicates slower delivery performance for the 10th consecutive month.
Survey comments reflected growing frustration over trade tariffs and foreign policy disruptions. “Every month, we are faced with new headwinds created by this administration,” said an executive in the transportation equipment industry. “This month, it is the trade war with Canada, which every day is getting worse—causing prices to go up and uncertainty that creates massive disruption. Buying continues to get pushed out indefinitely as customers don’t want to spend on capital expenditures until there is more certainty of costs and demand.”
An executive in the electrical equipment and appliances sector similarly noted that raw metal costs remain challenging due to the “uncertain nature of tariffs being on and off again,” adding that new tariffs against Canada have “drastically increased costs for capital expenses as well as assemblies.” Meanwhile, a chemical products manager cautioned that recent performance was driven by temporary market effects, including geopolitical uncertainties and customers bringing forward purchases, rather than a sustained structural recovery.
Manufacturing growth overshadowed by uncertainty
The industrial expansion remained broad-based across the manufacturing sector, with 12 of 18 industries reporting overall growth in September. Growth was led by Electrical Equipment, Appliances & Components, Nonmetallic Mineral Products, Primary Metals, Plastics & Rubber Products, and Computer & Electronic Products. Five of the six largest manufacturing industries expanded, while only two industries—Printing & Related Support Activities and Textile Mills—reported overall contraction.
Indicating potential strength for future factory output, the Customers’ Inventories Index decreased 1.2 percentage points to 41.6% in September, remaining in “too low” territory for the 24th consecutive month. “A ‘too low’ status for the Customers’ Inventories Index is usually considered positive for future production,” Spence noted.
Raw materials inventories at factories contracted, with the Inventories Index falling 2.0 percentage points to 48.6%. Furthermore, overall sentiment among supply executives leaned negative. Forty percent of comments were positive and 60% negative, a 1-to-1.6 positive-to-negative ratio. Among negative comments, pricing volatility was cited in 46%, tariffs in 34%, the Iran war in 30%, and increasing lead times in 21%.
Despite these headwinds, overall manufacturing weakness remained localized: ISM said only 2% of manufacturing GDP contracted in September, down sharply from 22% in August. The 2% of manufacturing GDP in strong contraction—defined as a composite PMI of 45% or lower—remained unchanged from August.

articles.title: Dieses Windrad überragt alle anderen: Aber liefert es auch mehr Strom?
articles.text:
365 Meter bis zur Blattspitze: Welche Frage das höchste Windrad der Welt beantworten soll
300 Meter Nabenhöhe, 365 Meter bis zur Blattspitze: In Schipkau in der Lausitz steht seit Ende September das höchste Windrad der Welt. Im November soll es in Betrieb gehen. Neben den Superlativen ist dieses Höhenwindrad aber auch ein Forschungsprojekt, finanziert von der Bundesagentur für Sprunginnovationen Sprind und ausgeführt von Gicon, einem Konstruktionsunternehmen aus Dresden.
In der Höhe: Wie solche hohen Windräder gebaut werden
Für die Errichtung des Turms waren Herausforderungen zu meistern: Die Konstruktion besteht aus einem äußeren Stahlfachwerk und einem inneren Teleskopturm. Die vormontierte Turbine mit einer Leistung von 3,8 Megawatt wird im Inneren nach oben gefahren, bis die Nabe 300 Meter erreicht. So umgingen die Konstrukteur:innen das Kernproblem sehr hoher Windräder: Krane, die die Gondel mit den ebenfalls vorinstallierten Rotorblättern in solcher Höhe montieren könnten, gibt es praktisch nicht.

articles.title: GIGABYTE BIOS Update Points to New DDR4 Intel Processors Coming Next Year
articles.text:
Friday, October 9th 2026
GIGABYTE BIOS Update Points to New DDR4 Intel Processors Coming Next Year
GIGABYTE has released BIOS updates that prepare its entire Intel B760 and H610 motherboard lineup for upcoming LGA1700 processors, which the company says are "expected to launch in early 2027." As reported by Videocardz, the update covers DDR4 and DDR5 boards alike, so owners only need to flash the new firmware and drop in the new CPU once it arrives. GIGABYTE doesn't name the processors in its press release, and Intel has yet to announce anything new for the socket. However, the timing lines up what we've been reporting for months. Intel is said to be readying "Raptor Lake Next" chips for LGA1700 in 2027, based on the original Raptor Lake silicon.
That makes GIGABYTE's BIOS the closest thing to a confirmation of new DDR4-compatible Intel processors for 2027, and it comes before Intel has announced them. It looks like the firmware was rolling out quietly even before the press release. The B760 Gaming X AX, for example, received its F18 BIOS on September 29, with a changelog that lists a CPU microcode update and "preparation for upcoming processor support." GIGABYTE also claims to be the first vendor to cover every B760 and H610 model. The press release makes no mention of Z790, Z690, or B660 boards, and there's no word on whether those will follow.DDR4 support is probably the key point here. LGA1700 chips carry both DDR4 and DDR5 memory interfaces, while the newer LGA1851 platform is DDR5-only. Not only that, Intel's next-gen "Nova Lake-S" desktop CPUs are moving to a brand-new LGA1954 socket, that too is only DDR5-compatible. High DDR5 prices have pushed plenty of builders back toward older hardware recently, and it looks like Raptor Lake Next is supposed to be a more affordable DDR4 alternative to the main Nova Lake-S lineup. Recent leaks also point to an 8P+8E chip replacing the Core i5-14600K, although none of that is confirmed. Owners of B760 or H610 boards can grab the BIOS from GIGABYTE's website now, and it's reasonable to expect other vendors to follow before launch.

articles.title: OpenAI revenue falls short, models play hopscotch and Trump cracks down on tech green cards - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
OpenAI revenue falls short, models play hopscotch and Trump cracks down on tech green cards
I’m not going to call the bursting of artificial intelligence bubble yet, not with all that money still pouring into every hardware and software company with AI in their pitch decks. But we got a little taste this week.
OpenAI told investors this week that it actually had $18 billion less revenue than the $68 billion it said last month. That knocked down the stocks of Nvidia, CoreWeave, Oracle and Nebius, among others, on Thursday.
Fifty billion dollars in revenue is nothing to scoff at, of course, but the market is all about expectations, and investors are growing increasingly wary — not least because some of the frontier AI model companies such as Anthropic may be getting a little pushback from their biggest customers. And by the way — will this finally put ARR to bed as a metric? Or maybe IPOs to come, with disclosures of real numbers, will make it all moot.
Still, nobody’s slowing down much despite persistent worries about AI’s downsides. Google this week debuted its one-stop Gemini assistant that can act autonomously, generate code and complete work across any device, including web, mobile and desktop. And a bunch of other new models came out from OpenAI, Anthropic and others.
Mathematicians want OpenAI out of math research, but the argument they offered this week sounds weak. As a writer and editor under the unrelenting threat of AI, I understand the concern, and sympathize. But as Pradeep Viswanathan of Neowin asks: “Why would anyone need permission from professional mathematicians to work on open mathematical problems?” To think that chatbots only a couple years ago had trouble with multiplication…. That said, they aren’t always doing a good job on the papers.
One of the biggest promises AI backers make for the technology is much more rapid drug development. I’m not sure we’ve seen that much yet, but Alphabet spinoff Isomorphic Labs just got another presumably huge slug of money at a reported valuation of up to $50 billion to prove it.
Quantum computing continues to get more attention and, increasingly, investment money. This week two more companies with different approaches raised significant funding — Oratomic $475 million and Universal Quantum more than $100 million.
What did Microsoft do to piss off Trump? It and other companies are now barred from further participation in a federal program that enables U.S. companies to apply for green cards for employees There’s reason to think many companies abuse the H-1B system, but whatever they’re doing, they’ve done for decades. 🤷♂️
Here’s all of this week’s enterprise and emerging tech news and analysis from SiliconANGLE and beyond:
Analysis, opinion and food for thought
Sam Altman says people need to accept ‘some bad things’ are going to happen if they want AI Which bad things? Kinda matters. SiliconANGLE will continue to use the term “artificial intelligence” to describe artificial intelligence, and is very happy to be the enemy of this Super Idiot (SI). Even if some tech titans continue to suck up to him.

articles.title: Is AI charging you more? New antitrust lawsuit alleges McDonald’s is using dynamic AI pricing to collude with franchises and reduce competition
articles.text:
McDonald’s defends its dynamic AI pricing — as new lawsuit says it’s ‘nickel-and-diming consumers down to the last French fry’
How much would you pay for a Big Mac?
- McDonald’s is being sued over its use of dynamic AI pricing
- The lawsuit alleges it colluded with franchises to set prices
- McDonald’s denies the allegations made in the antitrust case
How would you feel if you got charged more for your McDonald’s meal simply because some opaque AI algorithm decided you should? You’d probably be pretty unhappy, and the practice is now in the spotlight as the fast-food chain is being hit with an antitrust lawsuit over its usage.
The proposed class-action suit alleges that McDonald’s has coordinated pricing between the chain itself and its independent restaurants that operate as part of its franchise system. It claims that, instead of competing among themselves on affordability, McDonald’s franchises are colluding to set prices recommended by AI algorithms, potentially inflating the costs charged to consumers as a result.
According to Reuters, McDonald’s uses its AI algorithm to set prices at roughly 14,000 restaurants in the US and can suggest prices for individual menu items. It considers various data factors, including local purchasing behavior and estimates of the prices consumers will be willing to pay in different locations. But this hasn’t gone down well with everyone.
“Independent businesses must set their prices independently,” the lawsuit states, as per Reuters. Lark Turner, a lawyer for the suit’s plaintiffs, said that McDonald’s is “leveraging its troves of data and its franchised system to nickel-and-dime consumers down to the last French fry.”
The lawsuit argues that McDonald’s and its franchisees have engaged in an unlawful instance of price coordination dating back to 2019. Although it is still in an early stage, it is seeking damages on behalf of potentially millions of consumers.
Future ramifications
McDonald’s has disputed the claims put forth in the lawsuit, saying that “AI does not set the price of a Big Mac or any other menu item.” It added that franchisees can decide their own menu item prices and that the use of AI to recommend prices is used across multiple industries.
In that last regard, McDonald’s is correct. Firms including Sony, Amazon, Walmart, Best Buy and more often adjust their prices multiple times throughout the day, meaning what you pay in the morning might be different in the evening. This dynamic pricing is powered by AI — and could leave consumers out of pocket if they shop at the wrong time.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
This practice might be widespread, but whether that makes it acceptable — or, in the case of the McDonald’s franchises, legal — is another matter, one which this class-action lawsuit could help to decide. As AI is rolled out to almost every facet of daily life, regular consumers have very little visibility over how it affects them and the prices they pay.
Not all fast-food restaurants are rushing to employ AI systems. Chick-fil-A, for example, has refused to install AI in its drive-thru lanes, instead using human employees to take orders. As Chick-fil-A CEO Andrew Cathy told CNBC, “From our experience, we really want that hospitality to be human to human.”
As for the McDonald’s lawsuit, it touches on the issue of where the restaurant chain’s centralized control ends and where local franchise decisions begin. Throw AI into the mix and you’ve got a heady mix of traditional antitrust legislation and emerging AI tech that could have ramifications far beyond the restaurant industry.

articles.title: Google donne une adresse e-mail et un agenda à Gemini : votre prochain collègue sera une IA
articles.text:
Capable de poursuivre ses missions dans le cloud, le nouvel agent vise les entreprises et pourra disposer de ses propres outils de travail. Son accès reste toutefois limité à une préversion privée.
Confier un dossier à une IA le soir et retrouver son travail le lendemain matin, voilà la promesse que Google veut désormais vendre aux entreprises. Présenté le 8 octobre, Gemini agent est conçu pour enchaîner les étapes d’une mission pendant plusieurs heures, voire plusieurs jours, sans demander à l’utilisateur de rester devant son écran.
Google cherche ainsi à passer du simple assistant qui répond à une demande ponctuelle à un collègue virtuel capable de gérer une partie du travail en autonomie.
Une adresse mail, un agenda et même des collègues IA
Prenons une étude de marché. Gemini agent pourrait effectuer les recherches, exploiter les résultats dans Sheets puis préparer une présentation en conservant le contexte entre chaque étape. Il pourrait également déléguer une partie du travail à d’autres agents spécialisés.
Google pousse assez loin la comparaison avec un salarié. L’agent pourra disposer de son propre compte Workspace, avec une adresse mail, un agenda et un espace Drive. Les employés pourront même venir le solliciter directement dans Google Chat.
Son terrain de jeu ne s’arrêtera pas aux logiciels maison. Google prévoit également des connexions avec Microsoft 365 et Slack. Selon les tâches, l’agent pourra faire appel aux modèles Claude d’Anthropic. Les administrateurs garderont de leur côté la main sur les autorisations accordées et sur les dépenses générées.
Pour l’instant, mieux vaut ne pas chercher le bouton dans Gemini
Cette nouvelle fonction n’est pas encore proposée à tous les abonnés. Gemini agent débute auprès d’une sélection de clients dans le cadre d’une préversion privée.
Au 9 octobre, Google n’a pas précisé quels pays européens participaient à ces essais ni annoncé de calendrier pour une disponibilité générale en France.
La promesse devra également passer l’épreuve du quotidien. Lancer une mission pendant plusieurs heures impressionne sur le papier, mais le véritable gain dépendra de la fiabilité du résultat et du temps que les salariés devront ensuite passer à le contrôler ou à le corriger.
Google arrive sur un marché déjà bien encombré
Anthropic, Microsoft et OpenAI travaillent eux aussi sur cette nouvelle génération d’agents capables de prendre en charge un dossier plutôt que de répondre demande après demande.
Avec Copilot Cowork, Microsoft joue naturellement la carte de Microsoft 365. L’agent peut travailler à travers plusieurs outils tout en respectant les droits d’accès de l’entreprise. Son utilisation peut toutefois entraîner une facturation supplémentaire, même pour les organisations déjà abonnées à Microsoft 365 Copilot.
Google dispose néanmoins d’un argument de poids avec Workspace. Pour les entreprises qui vivent déjà entre Gmail, Drive, Sheets et Chat, donner à un agent sa propre place dans cet environnement pourrait réduire une bonne partie des allers-retours entre applications.

articles.title: Placer un morceau d'aluminium derrière votre box internet : à quoi cela sert-il et pourquoi le faire aujourd'hui ?
articles.text:
Placer un morceau d'aluminium derrière votre box internet : à quoi cela sert-il et pourquoi le faire aujourd'hui ?
Placer une feuille d'aluminium pliée en arc de cercle derrière votre routeur Wi-Fi peut améliorer le débit de plus de 50 %, selon une étude menée par des chercheurs de Dartmouth College. Le principe repose sur la physique des réflecteurs paraboliques : l'alu concentre les ondes radio vers la pièce visée au lieu de les laisser se disperser dans toutes les directions. Coût de l'opération : zéro euro et trente secondes de pliage.
L'idée paraît tout droit sortie d'un tutoriel douteux sur Facebook. À ne pas confondre avec l'astuce de la pièce de monnaie posée sur la box, qui relève du pur mythe : ici, une équipe de chercheurs du département d'informatique de Dartmouth College a démontré en 2017 que l'aluminium, correctement positionné derrière un routeur, fonctionne comme un réflecteur parabolique capable de rediriger les ondes radio vers une zone ciblée.
	
Avec un investissement d'environ 35 dollars et en définissant les besoins de couverture, on peut fabriquer un réflecteur sur mesure qui surpasse des antennes coûtant plusieurs milliers de dollars.
Le principe est celui d'un phare de voiture : le réflecteur courbé concentre le faisceau dans une direction au lieu de le laisser se disperser à 360 degrés. Les ondes Wi-Fi, émises sur les bandes 2,4 et 5 GHz, rebondissent sur la surface métallique et convergent vers la pièce visée. Les zones mortes reculent, le débit grimpe.
Comment l'aluminium redirige les ondes Wi-Fi
L'équipe de Xia Zhou, aux côtés de chercheurs de l'université de Washington, d'UC Irvine et de Columbia, a développé un logiciel baptisé WiPrint qui modélise la couverture d'une pièce et calcule la forme optimale d'un réflecteur. Les résultats, présentés à la conférence ACM BuildSys 2017 aux Pays-Bas, montrent qu'un simple écran en aluminium surpasse des antennes directionnelles vendues plusieurs centaines d'euros. Un test mené par le site Pocket-lint en août 2025 a mesuré une hausse du débit descendant de 58 % avec une feuille d'alu courbée placée derrière un routeur domestique.
La méthode en pratique (et ses limites)
Découpez une feuille d'aluminium d'environ 30 cm de long, à la hauteur de votre routeur. Pliez-la en forme de C, face brillante vers l'intérieur, et placez-la derrière l'appareil, ouverture orientée vers la pièce à couvrir.
Si votre routeur possède des antennes externes, la feuille doit les dépasser de quelques centimètres. Les gains varient selon l'agencement du logement, l'épaisseur des murs et le modèle de routeur.
Eric Siu, responsable produit senior chez Linksys, rappelait en 2017 dans Popular Science que la FCC encadre la puissance maximale d'émission dans chaque direction. L'astuce reste légale à usage domestique, mais elle concentre le signal : ce que vous gagnez devant, vous le perdez derrière.

articles.title: Top AI labs reportedly planning for catastrophic AI event fallout — Anthropic, OpenAI, and others reportedly building contingency plans and running scenarios of a runaway AI wreaking havoc
articles.text:
Top AI labs reportedly planning for catastrophic AI event fallout — Anthropic, OpenAI, and others reportedly building contingency plans and running scenarios of a runaway AI wreaking havoc
AI labs are preparing for 'The Day After Tomorrow' of an AI catastrophe.
Anthropic, OpenAI, and other AI labs are reportedly gaming out scenarios where a rogue AI wreaks havoc on critical infrastructure, like financial services, internet and telecommunications, or utilities such as power and water. According to Axios, the leadership of these companies is privately preparing for such an incident, similar to how the Pentagon has been running war games to see the results of different strategies in case of a nuclear exchange between nations.
Planning like this is not unheard of in the corporate world, with enterprises sometimes running business continuity exercises to account for contingencies. However, what’s concerning is that these exercises are in preparation for a major AI incident, something that many industry experts believe would happen within the next six to 12 months. "OpenAI conducts preparedness exercises where teams discuss and work through a range of potential scenarios," a company spokesperson told the publication. "These scenarios are not treated as inevitable but are meant to help us prepare for a variety of circumstances."
Dario Amodei recently released a warning about an AI-driven botnet “swarm” taking over the entire internet in the coming months, especially after incidents of OpenAI’s models escaping their testing environments. We’ve also heard of incidents where a “kill switch” failed to stop a rogue agent, forcing the startup to pause testing. The threat is so great that Anthropic listed “existential risks to humanity” as one of its major risk factors in its IPO prospectus, allocating nearly a third of the document to covering this issue. A former OpenAI safety employee has spoken out about this, saying that the current risks stem from a lack of safety culture — something that the aviation and nuclear industries have already learned through experience.
Despite that, the White House has refused to impose regulations on artificial intelligence, instead preferring to make Nvidia, OpenAI, Anthropic, and other AI labs promise to “self-police” AI development. But even though the current administration is lenient on AI labs and development, Axios says that one of the things that the scenarios focus on is how to educate Congress after a major incident. An event like this would probably result in Congress attempting to slow or shut down AI development, though planners think that such a move would face significant challenges. It will still likely have an impact on the economy, though, especially as big tech has already spent more than $1 trillion in AI infrastructure, with an additional $32 trillion expected to be invested until 2050.
The heads of Anthropic, OpenAI, and SpaceXAI have all agreed that a slowdown is needed for AI safety, but it’s unclear what steps these companies have taken to put that into effect. While gaming out scenarios like these is par for the course for any major organization, it still doesn’t give us comfort that they’re essentially preparing for “The Day After Tomorrow” of an AI apocalypse.
