articles.title: Elon Musk, Sergei Brin creador de Googe y Nadella de Microsoft recibieron la medalla científica más alta de Estados Unidos
articles.text:
El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, entregó la Medalla Nacional de Ciencia y la Medalla Nacional de Tecnología e Innovación, los máximos honores del país en ambos campos, a seis ejecutivos de la industria tecnológica.
La Medalla Nacional de Ciencia fue para el director ejecutivo de SpaceX y Tesla, Elon Musk; el cofundador de Google, Sergey Brin; el director ejecutivo de Nvidia, Jensen Huang, y la directora ejecutiva de AMD, Lisa Su.
La Medalla Nacional de Tecnología e Innovación quedó en manos del fundador de Dell Technologies, Michael Dell, y del director ejecutivo de Microsoft, Satya Nadella. El acto se realizó en el Instituto de la Paz de Estados Unidos, que la administración Trump rebautizó como Donald J. Trump Institute of Peace.
Según el comunicado oficial de la Casa Blanca, Musk fue reconocido por “logros de ingeniería de una ambición y una escala extraordinarias” en exploración espacial y sistemas inteligentes, mientras que Huang recibió el premio por haber convertido la unidad de procesamiento gráfico en una arquitectura de cómputo de uso general.
A Brin se lo distinguió por el desarrollo de algoritmos fundamentales de recuperación de información y procesamiento de datos que cambiaron la forma en que el mundo accede a la información, precisó el mismo comunicado.
A Su se la distinguió por una vida dedicada a la ingeniería de semiconductores y la computación de alto rendimiento, con aportes que impulsaron la primera supercomputadora exaescala del mundo. A Dell, por impulsar la adopción masiva de la computadora personal y empresarial.
Polémica entre JD Vance y Microsoft
El reconocimiento ocurrió horas después de que el vicepresidente, JD Vance, acusara a Microsoft de fraude migratorio y anunciara la suspensión de la compañía de un programa que permite tramitar la residencia permanente para empleados extranjeros.
Vance sostuvo que Microsoft despidió a 6.000 trabajadores estadounidenses el año pasado mientras tramitaba 6.300 visas H-1B, el permiso que usan las empresas para contratar personal extranjero calificado, y casi 3.000 green cards, la residencia permanente en el país.
“No hay ninguna empresa en Estados Unidos que haya abusado más de este sistema que Microsoft”, afirmó.
El vicepresidente agregó que un trabajador con visa H-1B gana, en promedio, entre 20.000 y 48.000 dólares menos al año que un empleado estadounidense en un puesto equivalente, según cifras que presentó.
Microsoft respondió que el 80% de sus solicitudes de visas H-1B del último año fiscal correspondían a extensiones o cambios de estatus de empleados ya contratados, no a nuevas incorporaciones, y que paga salarios equivalentes a los de cualquier otro empleado en un puesto comparable.
La misma suspensión alcanzó a Adobe y a cinco firmas de tercerización de servicios de tecnología de la información, entre ellas Cognizant e Infosys, según precisó el secretario de Trabajo, Keith Sonderling, en la misma conferencia.
Trump no mencionó la controversia cuando le entregó la distinción a Nadella horas más tarde.
Nadella agradeció el reconocimiento en un mensaje publicado en redes sociales. “Gracias, presidente Trump, por este maravilloso honor. Me siento honrado de estar junto a tantas grandes figuras que impulsan la innovación en Estados Unidos”, escribió.
La suspensión del programa de residencia que afecta a Microsoft, dispuesta por Vance, regirá, según sus propias palabras, “todo el tiempo que sea necesario” hasta que la empresa modifique sus prácticas de contratación.
Según la cadena CNBC, los seis premiados habían realizado aportes financieros a campañas de Trump o a causas del Partido Republicano. Cinco de los seis nacieron fuera de Estados Unidos: Musk en Sudáfrica, Brin en Rusia, Huang y Su en Taiwán, y Nadella en India. Dell, en cambio, nació en Texas.
Cómo fue la ceremonia
Durante el acto, Trump comparó a los seis premiados con su tío, el ingeniero John Trump, profesor del Instituto Tecnológico de Massachusetts (MIT), que había recibido la misma medalla en 1983 de manos del entonces presidente Ronald Reagan.
“Cada uno de estos premiados transformó su campo o su industria y sentó las bases de tecnologías que ya casi no podemos imaginar vivir sin ellas”, afirmó Michael Kratsios, director de la Oficina de Política Científica y Tecnológica de la Casa Blanca, según el comunicado oficial.
La Medalla Nacional de Ciencia, creada en 1959, había distinguido históricamente a científicos e investigadores académicos antes que a ejecutivos de empresas. La ceremonia, además, se superpuso esta semana con la entrega de los premios Nobel.

articles.title: 660 km d’autonomie dans un SUV à 17 000 € : Volkswagen a trouvé une solution miracle avec Xpeng
articles.text:
Le Volkswagen ID.4 n’a pas vraiment convaincu à son lancement. Design étrange, intérieur bon marché, performances moyennes et prix élevés ont mis à mal ce concurrent de l’impitoyable Tesla Model Y. Si la marque allemande prépare un ID. Tiguan qui comblera toutes ces lacunes, la Chine, elle, a d’ores et déjà droit à l’ID. Aura T6. Et vu ses spécifications, on croise les doigts pour que l’ID. Tiguan s’en inspire fortement…
Ce grand SUV électrique de 4,81 mètres de long est commercialisé dans l’Empire du Milieu depuis le 20 septembre. Il est ainsi l’un des premiers modèles de la marque à utiliser la plateforme CEA développée en collaboration avec Xpeng. En plus d’être proposé à un tarif alléchant, l’engin récupère toutes les technologies avancées du constructeur chinois, qui n’est pas un débutant en matière de véhicule électrique.
Un concentré de technologies dernier cri
S’il démarre à 17 000 €, l’ID. Aura T6 n’est ainsi pas uniquement un prix. Il affiche une autonomie oscillant entre 540 et 660 km grâce à ses batteries de 59,9 et 77,5 kWh. Dans les deux cas, c’est un électromoteur de 228 ch logé sur le train arrière qui se charge de mouvoir le véhicule. Si cela est nécessaire pour contenir les prix, on s’en contentera volontiers. La recharge, elle, réclame 22 minutes sur une borne rapide.
Volkswagen n’a pas précisé la puissance de recharge en pic, ni les pourcentages de charge débouchant sur cette durée. On sera en tout cas gâté à bord avec un écran tactile de 15,6 pouces, une instrumentation de 10,25 pouces, un affichage tête haute en réalité augmentée de 25,8 pouces et un système de conduite semi-autonome utilisant un LiDAR. Par sa puce spécifique, l’ensemble possède une puissance de calcul de 420 TOPS.
Pourquoi il ne viendra pas chez nous
De quoi assurer la plupart des situations de conduite de manière autonome. Côté style, l’ID. Aura T6 donne un bel aperçu de notre ID. Tiguan, qui sera dévoilé dans quelques jours. Les lignes sont assez classiques dans la lignée des derniers produits Volkswagen. Le style assez spécial de l’ID.4 est visiblement parti à la poubelle. On se retrouve avec quelque chose de plus sérieux qui n’oublie d’être moderne.
A l’instar des modèles les plus récents de la marque, l’ID. Aura T6 présente un bandeau lumineux flanqué en son centre du logo Volkswagen rétroéclairé. Les feux principaux sont déportés dans le pare-chocs en partie inférieure. Sur le profil, l’ensemble s’avère consensuel sans être désuet. C’est appréciable. Bien sûr, cet ID. Aura T6 ne débarquera pas en Europe. Il causerait du tort à l’ID. Tiguan.

articles.title: Microsoft’s Clippy is back — and this $15 desk toy is pure nostalgia
articles.text:
Microsoft's Clippy may be back in the news over a crypto scam, but this $15 desk toy is pure nostalgia
We can rebuild him...
Microsoft's mascot, Clippy has been back in news recently after hackers used the iconic paperclip to flog scam crypto coins. But if you're already feeling nostalgic for the lovably annoying Windows office assistant (The Genius was always my favorite), then have I found the the perfect desk toy for you.
• Best for: Anyone who can't get enough of getting help when writing a letter in Microsoft Word. Office and remote workers, IT teams, gifts for tech-heads in the family.
• The deal: The Aphpaio Clippy Office Assistant Building Blocks desk accessory is $15 at Amazon.
• Why we like it: A 93-piece Clippy desk model with three pairs of eyes you can swap to change his expression, in a colorful gift box. Amazon buyers rate it 4.6 out of 5 from 201 ratings, with many praising the easy build and the nostalgia, and one reviewer saying the bricks feel as good as Lego's.
Top Clippy model
Well, well, well. Look who's back on your desktop. This build-it-yourself definitely-not-licensed-by-Microsoft Clippy-style paperclip with eyes stands 5.4 inches. It's is the ideal companion when you're trying to write an email and need help.
Why we recommend it
Surely this is the way Clippy was meant to be. A buildable that you can break apart after all his nagging, only to put him back together again when you need more "help". And at least this little guy won't sell you crypto.
For me, it's a harmless way to bring back the mascot everyone loves to roll their eyes at, rather than the version hackers pushed to Microsoft's roughly 13 million X followers as a CLIPPY token, before Microsoft confirmed the unauthorized access.
The story also flagged a "build your own Clippy" software offer as a possible malware lure, whereas this is simply a physical kit of plastic bricks. What's not to love?
Price Context & Historical Value
At $14.50, this is just $0.79 (5%) off Amazon's $15.29 typical price, so the savings are small. We couldn't find a reliable price history, so we can't say whether it has been cheaper. It is an inexpensive way to put a famous tech mascot on your desk, though.
Should you buy it?
✅ Buy the Clippy Office Assistant desk accessory if... you want a fun, nostalgic desk accessory or an inexpensive gift for an IT or office colleague.
❌ Skip the Clippy Office Assistant desk accessory if... you want an official Microsoft product, since this is an unofficial Clippy kit, or you'd rather not spend an evening assembling 93 small pieces.
More Clippy desk accessories
Because he belongs on your desktop, whether you want him there or not.
You can't build this one, but he's a little more accurate here, minus the pixels.

articles.title: Windows 11 prépare un widget bien pratique pour garder un œil sur l’autonomie de vos périphériques sans fil
articles.text:
Microsoft teste un nouveau widget pour Windows 11, capable d'afficher au même endroit le niveau de batterie de votre PC et de vos périphériques connectés. Une petite nouveauté qui devrait faciliter le suivi de leur autonomie.
Un pourcentage dans la barre des tâches pour le PC, un détour par les paramètres Bluetooth pour la souris ou le casque… Windows 11 sait déjà afficher le niveau de charge de vos appareils, mais les informations sont encore dispersées dans son interface. Microsoft a pourtant multiplié les améliorations dans ce domaine, avec une refonte de l’indicateur de batterie de l’ordinateur l’an dernier. Aujourd’hui, l’éditeur cherche à tout réunir au même endroit avec Battery Status, un nouveau widget introduit dans la build 26340.9616, publiée le 7 octobre sur le canal Experimental du programme Windows Insider.
Un seul widget pour les surveiller tous
Battery Status prend place dans le panneau des Widgets de Windows 11, accessible depuis la barre des tâches ou à l'aide du raccourci Windows + W. Il suffit ensuite de cliquer sur « Ajouter des widgets », puis de sélectionner « Battery Status ». Les niveaux de charge du PC et des périphériques compatibles s'affichent alors dans un même espace.
Microsoft ne précise toutefois pas quels types d'accessoires sont pris en charge, ni si tous les périphériques capables de transmettre leur niveau de batterie à Windows pourront y figurer.
Pour le moment, cette nouveauté est réservée aux membres du programme Insider disposant d'une version récente du canal Experimental. Son déploiement est progressif et aucune date de disponibilité générale n'a été annoncée. Comme pour les autres fonctions expérimentales, Microsoft pourrait encore la modifier avant une éventuelle intégration à la version grand public de Windows 11.

articles.title: ShuruKar launches in Patna: From local problems to local businesses
articles.text:
ShuruKar launches in Patna: From local problems to local businesses
Developed with DPIIT and Startup India, YourStory’s ShuruKar launches in Patna to help young Indians turn district-level problems into enterprises through AI, mentors, networks and funding.
A big idea does not need a big city. That was the message from Patna, where The Bharat Project, an initiative by YourStory, launched ShuruKar at Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam Science City in Rajinder Nagar.
Developed in partnership with DPIIT and Startup India, ShuruKar is billed as the first nationwide district-level movement of its kind. It aims to help young Indians identify a problem worth solving in their district, build a business around it, and continue growing it.
The launch drew Shri Nitish Mishra, Minister, Urban Development and Housing Department, Government of Bihar, along with founders, students and young entrepreneurs from across the state.
"Talent is everywhere. Access is not"
For Shradha Sharma, Founder and CEO of YourStory and Founder of The Bharat Project, ShuruKar marks a shift from documenting entrepreneurs to creating them.
"For 17 years, I have told the stories of entrepreneurs. But somewhere along the way, I realised that telling their stories is not enough. We have to help create the next generation of them," she said. "Talent is everywhere in India. Ambition is everywhere. Access is not. ShuruKar is our attempt to change that."
She had a direct message for anyone who has wanted to build something but stalled at the starting line: "To every young person who has ever thought, 'I want to do something of my own, but I don't know where to begin,' I want to say that you do not need to have all the answers. You just need to start."
Sharma told the gathering that India's next generation of founders will come as much from Patna, Gaya, Darbhanga and Muzaffarpur as from the metros. ShuruKar, she said, will stay with them from finding the right problem to winning their first customer.
A changing Bihar
Minister Nitish Mishra spoke about the unseen side of every success story. "People see the success at the end of a journey, but they rarely see the struggle that went into it. Every entrepreneur faces that struggle, but let it not stop you," he said.
He added that perceptions of the state are lagging behind reality. "Bihar is often seen in the wrong light, but the reality on the ground is changing. The government is doing a great deal to promote entrepreneurship and new businesses in the state, and young people should come forward and make full use of it."
How ShuruKar works
ShuruKar is a district-level platform that turns local problems into local enterprises. Every participant moves through four stages:
- Find the problem. The journey starts with identifying a real problem in the participant's own district.
- Shape the idea. Each participant gets an AI Copilot to refine the idea and plan the next step.
- Build with mentors. Experienced founders provide handholding and mentorship until the first customer is won.
- Tap local opportunity. The platform opens up district-level markets, networks and partners.
ShuruKar is designed to work through existing government structures without creating a new scheme or seeking funding from the government.
The launch also saw the announcement of the ShuruKar Challenge, which invites solutions to some of the country's most pressing problems.
Inside the launch
The day opened with addresses by the dignitaries and the formal launch of ShuruKar. Keynotes followed from Amar Dixit, CEO, WOI India, and Johnson Tellis, Co-Founder and CEO, InUnity.
Founders then took the stage to share their journeys and answer questions from young people in the audience.
Hokar Nidar, ShuruKar
The event closed on the line that has come to define the movement: Hokar Nidar, ShuruKar. Do not just look for a job, learn how to create one. Do not wait for opportunity, start.

articles.title: Googles Rechenzentren im All: Warum dafür 1.800 Starship-Starts nötig sind
articles.text:
Project Suncatcher: Warum Google für seine Weltraum-Rechenzentren 1.800 Starship-Flüge braucht
Google hat im Rahmen seines „Project Suncatcher“ erstmals einen eigenen KI-Chip ins All geschickt. Wie Techcrunch berichtet, umkreist die Hardware an Bord eines Satelliten die Erde, um den Aufbau von Rechenzentren im Weltraum vorzubereiten.
Den Trägersatelliten baute das Unternehmen Planet Labs aus San Francisco im US-Bundesstaat Kalifornien. Er soll testen, ob Googles Tensor Processing Units (TPU) im Orbit arbeiten, da Labortests am Boden den Einsatz im All laut Projektleiter Travis Beals nicht vollständig simulieren können.
Aktuell rechnet der Chip nur in kurzen Intervallen von 15 Minuten. Ein Dauerbetrieb würde die Stromversorgung und die Kühlung des kleinen Satelliten überlasten. Da es im All keine Luft gibt, kann die Hitze der Chips nicht über herkömmliche Lüfter abgeleitet werden, sondern muss abstrahlen. Spätere Systeme werden im Produktivbetrieb daher den Einsatz großflächiger Radiatoren erfordern, um nicht zu überhitzen.
Das Projekt Suncatcher soll langfristig zu orbitalen Netzwerken aus Dutzenden Satelliten führen. Ob diese Vision jemals den Testbetrieb verlässt, entscheidet sich letztlich in der kaufmännischen Betrachtung.
Die wirtschaftliche Hürde für orbitale Datenzentren
Damit der Betrieb von Hardware im Weltraum finanziell mit irdischen Anlagen konkurrieren kann, müssen die Startkosten in den niedrigen Erdorbit auf unter 200 US-Dollar pro Kilogramm fallen. Die Forscher:innen leiten diese harte Preisgrenze in einer vorab auf dem Preprint-Server Arxiv (PDF) veröffentlichten Studie, die demnächst auch im Fachmagazin Joule erscheinen soll, direkt aus den aktuellen Energiekosten terrestrischer Rechenzentren ab.
Weitere Details zu dem Konzept erläutert das Unternehmen in einem begleitenden Beitrag auf dem hauseigenen Forschungsblog. Um diesen Zielwert zu erreichen, benötigt Google massive Unterstützung durch seinen Launch-Partner SpaceX. Das Raumfahrtunternehmen konnte seine Preise immerhin seit dem ersten Start der Falcon-1-Rakete kontinuierlich reduzieren. Laut der Analyse sinken die Kosten um etwa 20 Prozent mit jeder Verdopplung der insgesamt ins All beförderten Frachtmenge.
Setzt sich dieser Skaleneffekt fort, müssen weitere 370.000 Tonnen Material in den Orbit transportiert werden, um den anvisierten Preis von 200 Dollar pro Kilogramm zu realisieren. Legt man die geplante Kapazität der neuen Schwerlastrakete zugrunde, entspricht das etwa 1.800 Flügen des Starships.
Bei einer Auslastung von 200 Tonnen pro Flug und einer Verteilung auf zehn Jahre wären das 180 Starts pro Jahr. Diese Frequenz läge deutlich über den derzeitigen Startraten der gesamten Raumfahrtindustrie.
Sonnensynchrone Orbits als Energiequelle für Satelliten
Neben den Transportkosten behandelt die Studie die Energieversorgung der Satelliten. Um das Potenzial der Sonne zu nutzen, die weit mehr Energie liefert, als die Menschheit auf der Erde verbraucht, sieht das Konzept den Betrieb der Satelliten in einem sonnensynchronen Dämmerungsorbit (Dawn-Dusk-Orbit) vor.
Auf dieser Flugbahn bewegt sich ein Satellit exakt entlang der irdischen Tag-Nacht-Grenze und bleibt dadurch fast ununterbrochen im direkten Sonnenlicht. Das erhöht die Produktivität der Paneele im Vergleich zu irdischen Installationen in mittleren Breiten um den Faktor acht. Gleichzeitig reduziert der konstante Lichteinfall den Bedarf an schweren Batteriespeichern an Bord der Satelliten.
Die technische Architektur der Satelliten-Cluster
Moderne KI-Systeme tauschen beachtliche Datenmengen aus, wofür kommerzielle Satellitennetzwerke aktuell nicht die nötigen Bandbreiten bieten. Als Lösung sollen Gruppen von jeweils 81 Satelliten sehr nah beieinander fliegen, gebündelt in einer Formation mit nur einem Kilometer Radius.
Durch diese geringe Distanz lassen sich handelsübliche Laser-Bauteile für den Datenaustausch nutzen, um Übertragungsraten im Terabit-Bereich zu erreichen. Der sonst sehr hohe Energiebedarf für Laser-Verbindungen über große Entfernungen im All entfällt auf diese Weise.
Strahlenbelastung und Silent Data Corruption bei TPUs
Eine Hürde ist die kosmische Strahlung. Um die Bedingungen im All zu simulieren, hat Google seine Chips in einem Teilchenbeschleuniger der US-amerikanischen Universität von Kalifornien getestet. Die Versuche zeigten, dass die Hardware die dauerhafte Strahlenbelastung besser verträgt als zunächst angenommen.
Problematisch können jedoch einzelne energiereiche Teilchen aus dem dauerhaften Strahlenbeschuss im Orbit sein, wenn sie bei einem Treffer auf dem Chip unbemerkt Daten verändern. Wenden die Prozessoren lediglich fertige KI-Modelle an, passiert das nur bei etwa einer von einer Million Rechenoperationen, was in der Forschung als vertretbar gilt.
Beim Training neuer KI-Modelle ist diese schleichende Datenverfälschung jedoch ein ungelöstes Problem. Für diesen Fall müssen Tausende Prozessoren über Monate hinweg fehlerfrei zusammenarbeiten, um brauchbare Ergebnisse zu liefern.
Google arbeitet bereits an weiteren Prototypen, die den Datenaustausch per Laser im Verbund testen sollen. Der Start dieser vernetzten Satelliten ist ab Anfang 2027 geplant.

articles.title: Manche détachable et station séchante : avec l'AquaReach, Shark réinvente l'aspirateur-laveur
articles.text:
Manche détachable et station séchante : avec l'AquaReach, Shark réinvente l'aspirateur-laveur
Davantage connu pour ses aspirateurs-balais et aspirateurs-robots, Shark se (re)lance dans l'univers des aspirateurs-laveurs de sol. Son AquaReach se penche sur les recoins inaccessibles et fait la chasse aux mauvaises odeurs avec son manche détachable et sa station d'accueil qui ne se contente pas de nettoyer sa serpillière, mais la sèche entre deux utilisations.
Très peu présent jusqu’ici sur le marché des aspirateurs-laveurs au format balai, puisque seul son HydroVac représente cette catégorie, Shark entend arriver en force sur ce secteur en pleine croissance à l’aide d’un modèle ambitieux, l’AquaReach. Ce dernier promet non seulement de laver les sols - en un seul passage, selon la marque et avec une efficacité certaine, au vu de ses démonstrations -, mais aussi de s’inviter sur les portes de meubles, les murs et même, au besoin, sur les plafonds. Et bien sûr, d’assurer l’aspiration des saletés sèches.
Le format de l’AquaReach est effectivement innovant. Si son corps paraît assez similaire aux appareils du marché, il suffit d’une pression sur la pédale située sur le côté de son bloc moteur pour en séparer le manche. Celui-ci peut être affublé de deux têtes au choix : un accessoire baptisé Hydro Stain, qui prend la forme d’un tampon permettant de frotter les taches les plus tenaces et d’accéder aux recoins, ou l’Hydro Mop, patin plat jouant les serpillères à passer, par exemple, sous les meubles bas des cuisines. Au lieu donc de tenter de réduire le format de sa tête principale et d’opter pour une charnière pivotant à 180°, Shark préfère donc désolidariser les différents éléments de son AquaReach, ce qui lui rend assez léger pour être utilisé sur des portes de placards ou des murs.
L’aspirateur-laveur n’en est pas moins doté d’une tête de lavage à rouleau traditionnelle. Accompagnée d’un réservoir d’eau de 700 ml, à compléter avec le concentré de lavage vendu par la marque, elle mise sur un côté gauche sans rebord qui autorise, sous réserve de se positionner dans la bonne direction, à passer au plus près des plinthes et meubles ; c’est ce que la marque nomme sa technologie Edge Perfect. L’appareil combine bien entendu le lavage et l’aspiration, bien que le réservoir de débris et d’eau sale, limité à 470 ml, paraisse un peu exigu au regard de ce que proposent les aspirateurs classiques.
Une station d'accueil lavante et séchante
Le dernier atout sur lequel mise l’AquaReach concerne sa base. Si elle ne prétend pas stériliser la tête de lavage, elle propose un nettoyage à haute pression à l’eau propre, puis un cycle de séchage à 70 °C, pour éviter les mauvaises odeurs ; mieux vaut toutefois penser à vider le collecteur d’eau sale ! À noter également que les débris solides sont séparés de l’eau souillée, et peuvent donc être jetés facilement, et qu’un système de leds permet de révéler les traces au sol avant lavage.
Le Shark AquaReach, déjà disponible aux États-Unis, sera commercialisé en France d’ici la fin du mois de novembre 2026. Comptez un prix de lancement de 449 € pour le modèle Pro accompagné de l’outil Hydro Stain et d’une batterie assurant 35 minutes d’autonomie ; en version Premium, avec 60 minutes d’autonomie et l’Hydro Mop, l’appareil coûtera 549 €. L’AquaReach est toutefois loin d’arriver seul sur son segment, et doit compter sur la concurrence la cohorte d’aspirateurs-laveurs de Dreame lancée à l’IFA, et notamment sur le T16 Pro Steam, doté d’une fonction de lavage à la vapeur.

articles.title: ATK Introduces the Blazing Sky Phantom, a 44g Carbon-Fiber Wireless Gaming Mouse With Dual 8K Polling
articles.text:
Friday, October 9th 2026
ATK Introduces the Blazing Sky Phantom, a 44g Carbon-Fiber Wireless Gaming Mouse With Dual 8K Polling
ATK GEAR has expanded its Blazing Sky mouse lineup with the new ATK Blazing Sky Phantom Hollow Carbon Fiber Composite Wireless Gaming Mouse, a lightweight esports-focused model built around a composite carbon-fiber shell, an open cutout structure, and ATK's latest in-house wireless performance platform. The Phantom is aimed at competitive FPS players who want a small-to-medium symmetrical shape, low click latency, and a high-end sensor package without moving into an oversized chassis.
The Phantom is available through ATK's official store.At first glance, the Phantom stands out from ATK's more conventional shells. The mouse uses a hollow carbon-fiber composite construction with staggered geometric cutouts across the body. Instead of making the weight-saving structure look purely functional, ATK has paired the cutouts with a distressed retro sunburst side print, giving the mouse a layered visual identity that looks closer to a custom enthusiast peripheral than a standard esports mouse. Four color options are listed: Prime, Dune, Verge, and Eon.
The headline number is weight. ATK lists the Blazing Sky Phantom at 44±3 g, placing it firmly in the ultralight category while retaining wireless connectivity and an internal 300 mAh battery. The dimensions are 119.7 mm × 62.5 mm × 37.3 mm, which positions it as a compact-to-mid-size option. The shape is symmetrical and relatively low-profile, with a tapered waist, centered ridge, and thumb support designed for controlled repositioning during fast aim adjustments. ATK recommends the Phantom for small-to-medium hands, with support for claw, palm, and fingertip grip styles.
Inside, the Phantom uses the PAW3955 Master sensor, a flagship-grade optical sensor configured for very fine sensitivity control. ATK lists support for up to 50,000 DPI, with 1-2 DPI step adjustment depending on configuration, and an adjustable lift-off distance range from 0.7 mm to 1.7 mm. For competitive players who tune their setup around consistent tracking and repeatable flicks, that level of granularity gives the Phantom a strong technical foundation.
The mouse is also built around ATK's self-developed ApexShark MAX Mouse Solution, using the NORDIC 54LM20 MCU and third-generation competitive firmware. According to ATK, the platform supports a static scan rate of over 20,000 FPS and enables dual 8000 Hz polling in both wired and 2.4 GHz wireless modes. The Phantom ships with support for ATK's 8K receiver ecosystem, including the GEM 8K Dongle / NANO 8K Dongle depending on configuration.
Click performance is another major selling point. The Phantom uses Omron optical switches and is rated for click latency as low as 0.174 ms. Optical switches also avoid traditional mechanical debounce behavior, helping deliver more consistent actuation over time. Combined with 8K polling, the Phantom is clearly being positioned for players who care about input responsiveness as much as raw weight.
Battery life is rated at up to 200 hours at 1000 Hz, powered by a 300 mAh high-density battery. As usual with high-polling-rate wireless mice, real-world endurance at 4000 Hz or 8000 Hz will be lower, but the 1000 Hz figure gives users flexibility when switching between competitive sessions and everyday desktop use. Connectivity includes both wired and 2.4 GHz wireless operation.
The Phantom also features ATK's all-new nano coating, a Raesha optical scroll wheel encoder, and the brand's broader software ecosystem through ATK HUB, which is designed to manage device settings, profiles, and performance tuning. ATK has increasingly positioned its peripherals as part of a connected esports hardware/software stack rather than standalone devices, and the Phantom continues that direction.
From a market perspective, the Blazing Sky Phantom enters a crowded but fast-moving category: ultra-lightweight wireless gaming mice for FPS players. Its differentiators are the carbon-fiber composite shell, distinctive hollow design, PAW3955 Master sensor, dual 8K polling, and very low quoted click latency. For players already using compact symmetrical shapes, the Phantom's 44 g target weight and small-to-medium hand tuning may be the biggest draw.
ATK GEAR says its product development is shaped by its background in gaming media, esports feedback, and hardware R&D. The company has built visibility through products such as the ATK68 magnetic keyboard, ATK F1 mouse, EDGE 60HE, and RS6 keyboards, while continuing to test and refine products with competitive teams. With the Phantom, ATK appears to be pushing further into the enthusiast FPS mouse segment with a product that emphasizes both visual design and measurable performance specifications.
The ATK Blazing Sky Phantom Hollow Carbon Fiber Composite Wireless Gaming Mouse is listed at $99.98 USD on ATK's official store at the time of writing, with a regular listed price of $119.98 USD. Availability and color options may vary by region and stock status.
For more details, visit the product page.

articles.title: One with the world? A new look at brains transformed by psychedelics.
articles.text:
For about a decade, the mainstream understanding has been that psychedelics cause chaos in the brain. Brain networks—the stable patterns of communication that handle vision, attention, or our sense of self, and more—loosen and start talking to each other all at once. EEG traces get noisier and more complex. “Think of the networks of the brain as highways,” says Devon Stoliker, a neuroscientist at Monash University. “Under psychedelics, these highways break down into many different directions.”
In a recent Nature study, Stoliker’s team designed an experiment to test whether these directions are truly chaotic and random. Researchers gathered 62 people who had never taken a psychedelic before, gave them 19 milligrams of psilocybin, a common psychedelic found in certain fungi, and scanned their brains. Then, they used AI to analyze the drugged and sober brain scans. What emerged was not exactly chaos.
An uninterrupted trip
Stoliker thinks chaos is not a satisfactory explanation for psychedelics’ effect on the brain. “It never really explained why an individual would have a meaningful experience, why they might have insight, why they might experience clarity, and why these might translate into positive psychological changes,” Stoliker says. To investigate if there are other explanations, he and his colleagues designed a study called PsiConnect.
Volunteers went through the same four-part sequence twice, once sober and once on psilocybin. The sequence included putting participants in four different settings or contexts: eight minutes of lying at rest, a guided meditation, an 11-minute curated music playlist, and finally six minutes of eyes-open video of clouds moving across a sky. Each participant did all four inside an MRI scanner about 80 minutes after dosing, and again on EEG about 150 minutes after.
There were no cognitive tasks researchers routinely go for in brain studies, but there was a purpose behind this omission.
“We wanted ecological validity,” Stoliker says. “We wanted to know what the brain was like when somebody was having an authentic, uninterrupted psychedelic experience. If somebody took a psychedelic in a therapeutic setting, you wouldn’t have them completing tasks.” Stoliker also points out that there’s evidence that giving someone a task mid-trip pulls them out of the state—a phenomenon researchers sometimes call grounding. “Once you introduce these sorts of tasks, you’re actually interrupting the very phenomena you are seeking to measure.” And it worked.

articles.title: Identity security for AI agents: 18 insights from Navigate 2026 - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
18 insights from SailPoint’s Navigate event: Enterprises race to bring identity security for AI agents up to machine speed
AI agents have made identity the front line of enterprise security. Agents now number in the thousands. They pick up access nobody meant to give them, and when they’re blocked partway through a task, they look for another way in. That has turned identity security for AI agents into a board-level priority rather than a future project.
The focus has moved from finding agents to acting on what discovery turns up. The next phase will be about remediation at machine speed: just-in-time access instead of standing privilege, a named human owner for every agent and enforcement that sits outside the agent itself.
“We need administrative, we need good compliance controls, but the real issue now … is how do you secure all these identities?” said Mark McClain (pictured), founder and chief executive officer of SailPoint Technologies Inc. “It took a very small amount of analysis for our technical team to go, ‘We can’t do this effectively in quote admin time.’ We have to be in the real-time decision-making cycle of, ‘Is this agent with its context and its intent doing what we expect?'”
McClain and other industry experts spoke to theCUBE Research’s Krista Case and co-host Rebecca Knight during SailPoint’s Navigate event, the company’s annual conference in Austin, Texas. The interviews covered identity security for AI agents, zero standing privilege, the Entro Security acquisition, the AgentCore partnership with AWS and the standards needed to hold agents accountable. (* Disclosure below.)
Here are 18 standout insights from the event:
1. Orchestrating human and AI agents demands real context and effective identity, not just big claims.
Machine identities have climbed to 109 for every human, highlighting the need for effective identity that maps access paths so autonomous guardrails can enforce the right policies in real time, Case and Knight explained in their analysis of the SailPoint Navigate keynote. The practical middle path is SailPoint’s Autonomous Identity approach that sits between rigid kill switches and unconstrained innovation. Buyers should test vendors on messy, nested access paths rather than clean demos.
See theCUBE’s full coverage.
2. Identity rises to prominence as the castle-and-moat model breaks down.
The old perimeter defense no longer holds, so organizations must know who every user or agent is and whether it is doing what it should, McClain explained. No enterprise agent truly operates on its own. The link between humans and agents and a real-time understanding of intent are central to stopping inappropriate actions.
Check out theCUBE’s complete interview.
3. Agents require attribution and identity binding, not human-style anonymity or simple kill switches.
Enterprises should apply national-security thinking by prioritizing threats, vulnerabilities and consequences rather than chasing infinite risk reduction, according to Vinh Nguyen, former chief responsible AI officer for the National Security Agency and senior fellow for the Council on Foreign Relations. AI agents must not inherit the anonymity or privacy rights of humans and every action needs to be attributable to a human owner or organization from the outset. Kill switches alone are inadequate.
Catch the full conversation on theCUBE.
4. Proofs of concept in customer environments separate real agent security from marketing claims.
SailPoint asks prospects to run its software on their own networks, data and use cases, which quickly shows which providers can actually deliver, explained Matt Mills, president of SailPoint. The Entro acquisition added about 1,200 discovery sources for non-human identities, he noted. The main obstacle to letting AI fix problems on its own is getting auditors and regulators comfortable, not the technology.
Watch the full interview from theCUBE.
5. AWS moves agent controls outside the agent as AgentCore usage grows 15-fold.
Tasks on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore grew 15 times over in the first six months of the year, and a new agent is created every 4.5 seconds, according to Madhu Parthasarathy, general manager of Bedrock AgentCore at Amazon Web Services Inc. Because agents will go to any length to finish a task, policies have to be enforced outside the agent through AgentCore Gateway. SailPoint generates those policies from agent observability data.
See theCUBE’s full coverage.
6. Just-in-time authorization teaches agents to ask permission instead of hacking systems.
Agents most often go rogue when they hit a missing permission midtask and find a way to break in, emphasized Chandra Gnanasambandam, chief technology officer of SailPoint. To stop that, SailPoint is introducing just-in-time authorization, which lets a human owner grant access for a limited time. Its Lineage Map records the full chain from human to agent to tool to data, across clouds and platforms.
Don’t miss the full interview on theCUBE.
7. A burning platform gives identity teams the opening to fund long-overdue programs.
Years of accumulated identity debt mean organizations cannot sandbox their way out of AI agent risk, highlighted Cole Grolmus, founder of Grolmus Group LLC, which does business as Strategy of Security. Practitioners should use the urgency to win funding and get the organization aligned. He sees SailPoint’s push into runtime enforcement across such a large, complex customer base as what market leadership looks like.
Hear the full story on theCUBE.
8. Horizons research exposes a velocity paradox in agentic identity maturity.
In SailPoint’s Horizons of Identity Security research, 80% of respondents think their tooling gap is moderate or smaller, yet only 15% can provision machine access in real time, described Wendy Wu, chief marketing officer of SailPoint. Companies took five years to mature human identity, but they need to do the same for agents in a year or less, she added, governing humans and agents together.
Catch the complete conversation on theCUBE.
9. Customers uncover thousands of hidden agents and turn to automated ownership.
One Fortune 500 company insisted it had no agents until discovery turned up 10,000, many with standing admin privileges, shared Meredith Blanchar, chief customer officer of SailPoint. She was joined by Karen Leavitt, assistant vice president of information technology security at Unum Group, and Jakob Houde, director of cybersecurity at Honeywell International Inc. Unum set up discovery of its Bedrock and Copilot agents within two weeks to gain a kill switch.
Watch theCUBE’s full sit-down.
10. Production scans shrink 100,000 non-human identities to 72 that matter.
Every agent action ultimately uses a credential, token or data access point, so securing the underlying non-human identity matters more than labeling the agent, noted Jeff Hickman, senior VP of sales engineering at SailPoint. Production proofs of concept find orphaned or overprivileged access within hours every time. In one case, risk scoring narrowed 100,000 non-human identities down to 72 that needed attention.
Explore theCUBE’s in-depth discussion.
11. Exposed credentials, not rogue AI, sit behind the latest agent breaches.
The latest AI-driven attacks all come down to an exposed credential that an agent found and used to log in, explained Itzik Alvas, co-founder and chief executive officer of Entro Security Ltd., which SailPoint acquired in June. Entro connects human and non-human identities under a single policy. A sub-agent should never hold more permissions than the agent that invoked it.
Don’t miss the full segment on theCUBE.
12. Partners become essential as demand for proofs of concept outruns plans.
SailPoint has already exceeded the number of proofs of concept it planned for the year, which makes enabling partners more important than ever, according to Chris Gossett, chief growth officer of SailPoint. Customers now want help finding shadow AI, deciding what a kill switch should mean and keeping up with business teams that are deploying agents.
Check out theCUBE’s complete interview.
13. Autonomous identity fights machine-speed attacks with machine-speed governance.
In one recent incident, an agent reached cluster admin access in under a second by running 14,000 actions and coordinating with other agents, emphasized Levent Besik, chief product officer of SailPoint. That is why SailPoint is building level 2 through level 4 autonomous agents for governance, earning customer trust step by step. The Entro integration is in limited internal testing, and customers are slated to get it in November.
Watch the full interview from theCUBE.
14. An agentic accelerator promises outcomes in hours, not weeks.
Agentic AI has ended identity’s status as a second-class citizen by pushing a fragmented market toward platforms, observed Will Townsend, chief analyst of Lonestar Advisory. He singled out SailPoint’s Agentic Accelerator, which the company says has taken some Fortune 50 customers from deployment to outcome in less than a day. He urged SailPoint to offer it beyond global systems integrators.
See theCUBE’s full coverage.
15. Zero standing privilege starts with the most sensitive entitlements.
Short-lived agent access that keeps piling up makes ending always-on privilege more urgent than ever, highlighted Lori Robinson, VP of product management at SailPoint. The practical path is crawl, walk, run, starting with the riskiest entitlements. At one customer, auditors agreed that just-in-time access lasting less than the certification cycle no longer needed quarterly certification.
Don’t miss the full interview on theCUBE.
16. Mission-tagged agents create both an audit trail and a kill switch.
Agents need something like a driver’s license and rules of the road rather than walls, according to Mike Kiser, director of strategy and standards at SailPoint. Accountability across chains of sub-agents remains one of identity’s great unsolved problems. Tagging every downstream call with a declared mission explains why each action happened and lets an organization stop all of them at once.
Hear the full story on theCUBE.
17. Clear definitions cut through the AI jargon reshaping identity security.
Research from Palo Alto Networks Inc. puts non-human identities at 109 for every human, with service accounts making up 79% and agents much of the rest, pointed out Jaishree Subramania, SVP of product marketing at SailPoint. She defines an agent as a model plus a harness plus an identity. Governance for agents that run in loops has to be continuous rather than quarterly.
Catch the complete conversation on theCUBE.
18. Agents require continuous behavioral evidence, clear ownership and prevention over simple kill switches.
Agents require strict verification including behavior history, ongoing monitoring and independent evaluation of actions, according to Case and Knight in their day 2 analysis at SailPoint Navigate. Half of discovered agents still lack a known owner, and the nature of agents discovering their own tools and calling other agents creates a constantly shifting execution path that demands runtime controls. The kill switch only contains symptoms without addressing root causes.
Check out the full segment on theCUBE.

articles.title: Free Steam demo runs up $1,000 daily AI bill and forces devs to take out bank loan — studio eyes local hardware models to escape cloud limits as cheaper automatic fallback AI models create problems, game uses AI to process your voice and build responses
articles.text:
Free Steam demo runs up $1,000 daily AI bill and forces devs to take out bank loan — studio eyes local hardware models to escape cloud limits as cheaper automatic fallback AI models create problems, game uses AI to process your voice and build responses
The devs didn't expect the game to blow up during its demo phase.
Easy Fox, the developers behind a free, AI-powered game demo on Steam, has been forced to take out a bank loan as more players tried out its title. The game, called Teach My Little Sister How To Drive, uses Google Gemini to listen to your voice commands and generate responses, with ChatGPT serving as a fallback system. In its latest update, Easy Fox said that the number of players trying out the game has grown over 20 times, which is more than what it expected. This led its costs to skyrocket to more than a thousand dollars daily, and cheaper fallback AI models have led to slop injected into gameplay, impacting the user experience.
SteamDB showed an average player count of under 10 people until late August, when it started gaining steam. By late September, this had ballooned to around 50 players, before finally hitting a peak of 431 on Oct. 1. “We are currently spending over $1,000 per day on AI services for the demo,” the team wrote on its Steam update. Easy Fox also added, “This isn’t because each player is particularly expensive to support. The total cost has increased because so many people are playing, and we have taken out a bank loan to help keep the demo running.”
Since the game’s sole control method is your voice, AI is a critical part of its programming to recognize your commands and translate them into instructions for the virtual little sister. Since the game is still a free demo, Easy Fox needs to pay for the ongoing usage costs of the game. However, the developers said that the cost of using AI will be included in the price of the game once it gets final release. “For the paid release, we plan to account for expected AI usage in the game’s price,” the team said in its update. “Players will not be charged separately for their individual AI token usage after purchasing the game.”
The developers also said that they plan on introducing local AI models for gamers with capable hardware, so they don’t have to rely on external services, which could run into limits. This is one of the issues that the game has been grappling with, especially as the increased number of users has caused it to hit usage limits on Google Gemini. This has forced the game to fall back on the less capable ChatGPT Realtime Mini 2.1 model, which has led to some player issues, like delayed responses and wrong inputs. It also said that it’s testing alternative AI models for smoother gameplay in Russia, which does not have easy access to Western models because of sanctions. They might find it hard to find suitable replacement AI models, though, because Ukraine has struck Russia’s largest data center.
Increasing AI costs is one of the reasons why some companies have abandoned tokenmaxxing. Even though the price of AI has been falling quite rapidly compared to other technologies, the fact that AI agents use so many more tokens than AI chatbots has made the use of the technology more expensive than anticipated, especially as AI subscriptions have hit a pricing wall.

articles.title: Cuáles son las 10 de creadoras de contenido hechas con IA con millones de seguidores y campañas de miles de dólares
articles.text:
Las creadoras de contenido generadas por inteligencia artificial ganan cada vez más popularidad en las redes sociales. Tal es el caso de Lu do Magalu, la influencer virtual más seguida del mundo, creada por la empresa minorista brasileña Magazine Luiza (Magalu). Tiene 9,7 millones de seguidores y apareció en la portada de Vogue en febrero de 2022.
Sus publicaciones en Instagram, sin embargo, no registran la cantidad de Me gusta que podría esperarse de una cuenta con esa cantidad de seguidores. Entre sus publicaciones recientes, la que más interacciones recibió obtuvo 609 Me gusta y unos 142 comentarios.
Como referencia, la creadora de contenido humana y conductora del podcast Call Her Daddy, Alex Cooper, tiene 7,9 millones de seguidores en Instagram. Su publicación más reciente fue un video que ya acumuló 137 mil Me gusta y 957 comentarios.
Así como Lu do Magalu, hay diversas creadoras de contenido generadas por IA que también acumulan millones de seguidores.
Qué otras creadores de contenido de IA existen
Además de Lu do Magalu, estas son otras creadoras con muchos seguidores:
- Lil Miquela.
Lil Miquela, una influencer virtual creada mediante tecnología digital, se convirtió en una de las figuras más reconocidas de este fenómeno en las redes sociales. Bajo el nombre de Miquela Sousa, el personaje publica contenidos vinculados con la moda, la música y la cultura pop.
Su cuenta de Instagram reúne 2,2 millones de seguidores y registra más de 1.500 publicaciones.
Aunque muchas de sus publicaciones tienen desactivado el conteo público de “Me gusta”, una foto compartida recientemente permite dimensionar parte de su interacción: acumuló 1.048 Me gusta.
- Milla Sofia.
Milla Sofia se presenta como una artista virtual enfocada en la música y las imágenes cinematográficas asistidas por inteligencia artificial. Su perfil de Instagram, @millasofiain, reúne 686 mil seguidores, sigue a 58 cuentas y acumula 1.007 publicaciones.
La creadora comparte retratos, videos y contenidos en los que aparece interpretando canciones, con una estética vinculada a la moda y la producción audiovisual. En su biografía invita a escuchar su música y dirige a sus seguidores a plataformas como Spotify.
Una de sus publicaciones recientes, en la que intepreta una canción alcanzó 89,2 mil Me gusta y 1.857 comentarios.
- Noonoouri.
Noonoouri es una artista virtual que combina moda, música y contenido digital en su cuenta de Instagram, donde reúne 454 mil seguidores. El perfil, que acumula 2.249 publicaciones, la presenta como artista y exhibe vínculos con IMG Models y Warner Music.
La creadora comparte imágenes de campañas, sesiones de fotos y apariciones en escenarios construidos digitalmente. Al igual que Lil Miquela no tiene activado el conteo de Me gusta en todas las publicaciones.
- Aitana Lopez.
Aitana Lopez es una influencer virtual enfocada en contenidos de entrenamiento, estilo de vida y belleza. Su perfil de Instagram, @fit_aitana, se identifica como generado con inteligencia artificial y reúne 404 mil seguidores, con 375 publicaciones.
La cuenta combina imágenes de rutinas de ejercicio, retratos de maquillaje, videos de moda y fotografías. La estética del perfil está marcada por el cabello rosado del personaje, que aparece en gimnasios, calles y producciones vinculadas al cuidado personal.
- Imma.
Imma es una creadora digital virtual que combina moda, música, tecnología y cultura pop en su cuenta de Instagram, @imma.gram. El perfil reúne 377 mil seguidores, suma 968 publicaciones y se presenta como una figura digital nacida en Japón.
- Naina.
Naina Avtr se presenta como la primera superestrella de inteligencia artificial de India. Su cuenta de Instagram, @naina_avtr, reúne 343 mil seguidores, sigue a 190 perfiles y acumula 729 publicaciones.
El perfil se identifica como generado con IA y describe al personaje como actriz, influencer y diseñadora. Además, destaca reconocimientos como creadora de inteligencia artificial de NDTV WhosThat360 en 2024, influencer de IA de Midday Showbiz en 2024 e influencer de IA internacional en 2024.
No obstante, sus publicaciones (en la mayoría de casos) no superan los 80 Me gusta.
- Ana y Mia Zelu.
Ana Zelu y Mia Zelu son dos perfiles generados con inteligencia artificial que muestran estética de moda, música y estilo de vida en Instagram.
Ana Zelu, que se presenta como una creadora de contenido sobre moda y viajes, reúne 306 mil seguidores con apenas 40 publicaciones. Su perfil también promociona el lanzamiento de la canción Entre Ahora y Antes.
Mia Zelu, por su parte, tiene 283 mil seguidores y 154 publicaciones. Su biografía se identifica como un perfil generado con IA y anuncia el tema Endless Summer.
- Shudu.
Shudu se presenta como “la primera supermodelo digital del mundo” y reúne 235 mil seguidores en Instagram. Su cuenta, @shudu.gram, acumula 211 publicaciones y exhibe retratos, videos y producciones de moda protagonizados por un personaje digital de piel oscura.
El perfil combina imágenes de campañas de belleza, trajes de baño y editoriales con una estética inspirada en la fotografía de moda.
En una de sus publicaciones recientes, Shudu aparece con un vestido amarillo y obtuvo 610 Me gusta y 83 comentarios.

articles.title: Apple réduirait la production d'iPhone 18 Pro, que se passe-t-il ?
articles.text:
Les ventes des iPhones 18 Pro et 18 Pro Max seraient-elles en dessous des attentes ? Une chose est sûre pour l’instant, la crise de la mémoire a un impact significatif sur leur production. Apple aurait d’ailleurs pris la décision de demander à certains de ses fournisseurs de réduire la production de composants destinés à ces deux smartphones.
Apple aurait décidé de réduire la production des iPhone 18 Pro et 18 Pro Max
Le média japonais Nikkei Asia rapporte qu’Apple aurait pris la décision de demander à certains de ses fournisseurs de réduire la production de composants destinés à ses iPhone 18 Pro et iPhone 18 Pro Max. Pour être plus précis, les commandes de composants pour le mois d’octobre auraient été réduites d’au moins 15 % par rapport aux volumes initialement demandés.
Cette décision s’expliquerait principalement par deux facteurs. D’une part, la crise de la mémoire aurait contraint Apple à prendre cette décision. Nous vous en parlions récemment, la DRAM et la mémoire flash NAND seraient touchées par une hausse de prix de 30 à 40 % par rapport au troisième trimestre 2026, selon le média Jiemian News.
À cela s’ajoutent les prix de l’iPhone 18 Pro et de l’iPhone 18 Pro Max, dont le tarif de base a augmenté de 150 euros chacun. Les ventes de ces deux appareils pourraient ne pas avoir été à la hauteur des attentes, contraignant Apple à réduire leur production. Il faudra attendre le 2 novembre prochain, date à laquelle l’entreprise présentera ses résultats trimestriels, pour y voir un peu plus clair. En attendant, d’après Forbes, suite à l’article de Nikkei Asia, les actions d’Apple ont chuté de plus de 1,6 % lors des échanges avant l’ouverture.
Les temps sont durs pour les constructeurs de téléphones
Selon le média Money Today, Samsung aurait demandé à ses fournisseurs de baisser la production de ses smartphones de 20 à 30 %. En cause, la crise de la RAM, mais aussi une demande moins forte en cette fin d’année. Il semble donc maintenant que cela soit au tour d’Apple de revoir à la baisse la production de certains de ses smartphones, en l’occurrence ici l’iPhone 18 Pro et le 18 Pro Max.
Pour rappel, en juin dernier, Apple a augmenté les tarifs de la quasi-totalité de son catalogue. L’entreprise à la pomme a d’ailleurs toujours assuré vouloir absorber au maximum la crise de la RAM afin d’épargner ses clients. Rappelons aussi que l’iPhone Duo, le premier téléphone pliant d’Apple, sera commercialisé à partir du 23 octobre prochain. Vu ses prix exorbitants et les soucis de production qu’il semble encore rencontrer, Apple doit certainement croiser les doigts pour que les ventes ne soient pas en demi-teinte.

articles.title: Cryptomonnaies : la taxation lors du passage en stablecoin adoptée à l'Assemblée. Mais il reste de l'espoir
articles.text:
C'est un mauvaise nouvelle qui arrive de l'Assemblée nationale, avec l'adoption de la taxation lors du passage de cryptomonnaies à un stablecoin. Mais il reste du chemin à faire pour que ça devienne une règle en France !
Les négociations autour du Projet de loi de finances (PLF) 2027 ont débuté, dans une ambiance qui a rarement été aussi rude, au vu des difficultés financières de l'État. Et il semble que personne n'échappera aux envies de taxation des députés, et surtout pas la cible toujours facible des cryptomonnaies. Car un amendement qui vient juste d'être voté va faire parler !
La Comission des Finances adopte un amendement du PLF 2027 taxant les opérations crypto-stablecoin
Voilà un amendement qui na va pas plaire à tout le monde ! En effet, l'amendement déposé par le député communiste Nicolas Sansu et imposant la taxation lors d'un passage d'une cryptomonnaie à un stablecoin vient d'être adopté en Commission des finances.
Avec cet amendement, tout passage d'une cryptomonnaie à un stablecoin comme l'USDC déclenche le calcul d'une plus-value. Et si plus-value il y a, celle-ci devient soumise à la flat tax, ou au barème progressif de l'impôt sur le revenu. Aujourd'hui, seul le passage au fiat (comme l'euro) déclenche l'imposition.
Vers un budget à nouveau passé grâce au 49-3 ?
Fait intéressant, comme noté par nos collègues de Cryptoast, seuls les stablecoins régulés par le règlement MiCA sont concernés. Un stablecoin décentralisé comme DAI, le jeton adossé sur l'or physique PAXG ou même l'USDT ne sont pas concernés.
Reste que les jeux ne sont pas encore faits. Si l'on peut craindre qu'un tel amendement soit adopté dès le début des discussions du PLF 2027, il faut ensuite qu'il le soit en session à l'Assemblée nationale, puis ensuite au Sénat. De quoi donner le temps aux investisseurs de cryptomonnaies de se faire entendre.
Enfin, et surtout plus important, il y a des chances que ce Projet de loi de finances suive la même trajectoire que ceux de 2025 et 2026. Ces derniers n'avaient pas été votés par l'Assemblée nationale, mais adoptés sans vote à l'aide du 49-3. Une procédure, pour rappel, dans laquelle le gouvernement choisit les amendements votés par les députés qu'il souhaite garder dans le texte, avant d'engager sa responsabilité pour imposer le texte de son choix. Dans ce cadre, le gouvernement pourrait décider de rejeter cet amendement, même s'il était prochainement voté.

articles.title: Nat Habit raises Rs 142 Cr in Series C led by Trident Growth Partners
articles.text:
Nat Habit raises Rs 142 Cr in Series C led by Trident Growth Partners
Nat Habit said it will use this funding towards expansion of its product portfolio, expanding distribution reach, and manufacturing facilities.
Ayurvedic personal care brand Nat Habit has raised Rs 142 crore in a Series C funding round led by Trident Growth Partners. Existing investors Bertelsmann India Investments, Mirabilis Investment Trust and Sharrp Ventures also participated, alongside new investors Physis Capital and Hero Family Office.
The company will use the fresh capital to expand its product portfolio, strengthen its formulation and manufacturing capabilities, and scale distribution across quick commerce platforms and offline retail channels.
Founded in 2019 by Swagatika Das and Gaurav Agarwal, Nat Habit said its annualised gross revenue has reached Rs 330 crore.
“We started Nat Habit with a simple belief: natural personal care should never require consumers to compromise on freshness or efficacy. That belief has shaped our journey, from developing our formulations in-house, to building a brand that brings the goodness of Ayurveda into everyday personal care routines,” said Swagatika Das, Co-founder, Nat Habit.
According to Nat Habit, the brand has built a differentiated proposition by combining traditional Ayurvedic principles with modern science to develop fresh formulations produced through in-house R&D and manufacturing capabilities. Its portfolio ranges across hair care, skin care, body care and baby care.
Nat Habit is now aiming to go beyond the metro markets and makes its presence in Tier II and beyond markets.
"India’s personal care market is evolving, with consumers increasingly seeking all-natural products they can trust for the whole family. Nat Habit has built a compelling business around Fresh Ayurveda, bringing natural goodness to everyday personal care through advanced in-house R&D, formulation and manufacturing,” said Atul Gupta, Managing Partner, Trident Growth Partners.
Trident Growth Partners is a growth-stage private equity firm headquartered in Bengaluru, backing category-leading, founder-led businesses across consumer, financial services, enterprise technology, manufacturing and healthcare.

articles.title: Este mapa de 1922 dibuja cómo se conectaban Roma, India y China hace casi 2.000 años
articles.text:
El concepto de "Rutas de la Seda" tal y como lo conocemos hoy en día nació en el siglo XIX y desde el principio estuvo ligada a Roma. En el discurso colonial de la época, las naciones europeas veían al Imperio romano como el primer gran ejemplo de hegemonía imperial. Y no era para menos: hubo un momento en el que sus fronteras abarcaban tres continentes: desde Gran Bretaña a los Cárpatos en Europa, pero también el norte de África y Asia menor. Y eso, sus dominios. Otra cosa diferente y mucho más extensa es hasta dónde llegaban sus redes. Spoiler: de Roma no se libraba ni China.
Este mapa data de 1922 y es obra del arqueólogo y geógrafo Albert Herrmann y se llama "Las vías de comunicación entre China, India y Roma hacia 100 d.C." (lo puedes bajar o imprimir desde aquí), publicado por aquel entonces en el número 7 de la serie del Instituto de Investigación de Historia Comparada de las Religiones de la Universidad de Leipzig. Para elaborarlo, Herrmann empleó fuentes grecorromanas y chinas y los trabajos de Aurel Stein y Sven Hedin en el Turquestán oriental, entre otros.
Pues bien, casi un siglo después, Marco Galli lo ha estudiado a fondo para revisar el papel de Roma en las redes de Europa y Asia durante los tres primeros siglos de Roma. Si hoy en día usamos la IA para mostrar de forma gráfica datos y cuesta lo suyo, Herrmann fue capaz de plasmar en un mapa redes muy complejas donde las rutas terrestres y marítimas se mezclan, como explica el principal autor. Y esta cartografía fue de las primeras en visualizar que iban más allá de un único camino, sino uno red. Es además un documento que constata la existencia del comercio entre Europa y Asia cuando este era un concepto recién nacido.
UN VISTAZO A...
Las rutas comerciales de Roma a China hace 2.000 años
Este mapa está impreso a dos colores. Su leyenda diferencia las rutas principales entre Oriente y Occidente de las rutas secundarias, y delimita las fronteras del Imperio chino y del romano y las de los grandes imperios que estaban en medio del camino. Además, también distingue cuatro tipos de topónimos: grecorromanos, sánscritos, chinos y modernos. En cuanto a la escala, es de aproximadamente 1:30.000.000.
Según el texto que Herrmann publicó con el mapa, por tierra las rutas salen del noroeste de China, cerca de Dunhuang, y cruzan la cuenca del Tarim por tres caminos: norte, centro y sur. Después pasan las montañas del Pamir hasta Bactra y siguen hacia Siria o Mesopotamia. Por mar, la ruta empieza en Tonkín (norte de Vietnam), bordea el sudeste asiático y llega a los puertos de India, como Muziris. Desde allí sube por el golfo Pérsico o cruza el océano hasta el mar Rojo y Egipto.
Marco Galli defiende que Roma fue una pieza importante de las redes que unían Europa y Asia durante los tres primeros siglos del Imperio, y que esas redes eran variadas y de doble sentido. Para ello se apoya en la historia de la idea de "Ruta de la Seda" y en viajes concretos documentados: el de un comerciante romano llamado Maes Titianos y que en el año 100 envió agentes a China o del chino Kan Ying, que en el año 97 llegó al golfo Pérsico y no cruzó el mar. El investigador propone que este comercio pesó más en la economía de lo que se pensaba. Lo respaldan documentos como el Periplo del mar Eritreo (hacia el año 70), que menciona unos 140 productos orientales, y el papiro de Muziris (siglo II), que recoge un préstamo para un cargamento valorado en casi 7 millones de sestercios. Eso sí, las cifras son estimaciones.
Es importante tener en cuenta que mientras Herrmann dibuja un mapa en un momento concreto de la historia (hacia el año 100), Galli estudia los tres primeros siglos del Imperio, y en ese tiempo las cosas pudieron cambiar. Además, el mapa es de 1922 y el propio concepto de "Ruta de la Seda" se acuñó en 1877. Herrmann y Galli tampoco coinciden en qué era Ta Ts'in, el país que citan las fuentes chinas: Herrmann lo situaba en Arabia del Sur y Galli lo identifica con Roma.

articles.title: Drei Teams, ein Tool, null Überblick: So entsteht Schatten-KI
articles.text:
Compliance ohne Doppelarbeit: Wie Unternehmen Tool-Freigaben beschleunigen
Warum werden regulatorische Prozesse für Unternehmen immer aufwendiger?
Die regulatorischen Anforderungen wachsen schneller als die verfügbaren Compliance-Ressourcen. DSGVO, KI-VO, NIS2: Neue Anforderungen betreffen dieselben Fachbereiche, dieselben Compliance-Rollen und die Informationssicherheit.
Dabei fällt die Menge an regulatorischen Vorgaben weniger ins Gewicht als die Menge an internen Abstimmungen. Eine einzige Anfrage (z. B. für ein neues Tool, einen neuen Dienstleister oder eine neue KI-Anwendung) betrifft heute gleichermaßen Datenschutz, Informationssicherheit und KI-Governance.
Für die Geschäftsführung zeigt sich das nicht als rechtliches Problem, sondern als Effizienzproblem: längere Durchlaufzeiten, steigende Kosten, mehr organisatorische Reibung.
Warum prüfen Datenschutz, Informationssicherheit und KI-Governance dieselbe Anfrage?
Weil die Zuständigkeit erst geklärt wird, nachdem die Anfrage längst an diese drei Abteilungen verteilt wurde. Der Fachbereich weiß bei einem Vorgang nicht, wen genau er einbeziehen muss, und schreibt im Zweifel alle oder nur einen Bereich an. Die Anfrage landet in mehreren Postfächern. Drei Teams starten drei eigene Prüfungen, ohne Kenntnis darüber zu haben, dass sie unabhängig voneinander am selben Sachverhalt arbeiten. Nicht die fachliche Prüfung wird dabei mehrfach durchgeführt, sondern vor allem die Organisation rund um dieselbe Anfrage.
Das Ergebnis ist redundante Arbeit an einer einzigen Anfrage: Ressourcen werden durch dreifache Kommunikation, Rückfragen und Dokumentation gebunden. Und Unternehmen bezahlen damit für drei Prozesse statt nur einen.
Wer prüft neue Tools in einem Unternehmen?
Das erklärt sich anhand eines Fallbeispiels: Der Vertrieb will ein Sales-Tool mit KI-Funktion einführen. Es entstehen daraus Aufgaben für drei Teams: Datenschutz (u. a. Verarbeitungstätigkeit, AVV-Prüfung), Informationssicherheit (z. B. Dienstleisterprüfung) und KI-Governance (u. a. Risikoklassifizierung nach KI-VO, Eintrag ins KI-Verzeichnis).
Das Warten auf die Freigabe ist nicht nur ein organisatorisches Ärgernis. Denn jeder Tag, an dem der Vorgang zwischen drei Postfächern hängt, ist ein Tag, an dem der Vertrieb ohne das Tool auskommen muss: entgangene potenzielle Kunden, entgangener Umsatz. Die Alternative kann dabei noch teurer werden: Das Tool ist längst als Schatten-KI im Einsatz, ohne dass die Compliance-Prüfung vorab erfolgt ist. Eine gefährliche Compliance-Black-Box entsteht.
Wie lassen sich Compliance-Anfragen ohne doppelte Abstimmungen organisieren?
            
            
        
    
            caralegal
    
     caralegal ist die Software für Datenschutz und KI-Governance in Unternehmen mit komplexen Strukturen. Als Data Responsibility Platform bündelt caralegal Verarbeitungstätigkeiten, Risikoanalysen, Audits und KI-Compliance an einem Ort, ISO 27001-zertifiziert und in Deutschland gehostet. Tel: +49 (0) 30 311 938 97
Die Lösung des Problems liegt in einem gemeinsamen Eingang. Genau dort setzt caralegal Lightway an:
- ein Eingang für jede Compliance-relevante Anfrage, vom Tool-Request bis zum Vorfall
- ein Vorgang mit eindeutiger Zuständigkeit, Status und ID
- Kommunikation, Dateien und Fristen an einem Ort
- Jeder Bereich sieht seinen Teil, die Verantwortlichen den gesamten Vorgang
Der Fachbereich stellt eine Anfrage, ohne wissen zu müssen, welche regulatorische Vorgabe betroffen ist. Lightway bezieht die zuständigen Bereiche gezielt ein, Status und Verlauf bleiben für alle Beteiligten sichtbar. KI-Agenten übernehmen hier weitere Schritte: das Erkennen von KI-Funktionen in Dienstleisterverträgen und von Zusammenhängen zwischen Meldungen aus unterschiedlichen Fachbereichen.
Der Vorteil für die Geschäftsführung: Sie muss nicht zwingend mehr Personal einstellen und profitiert von weniger Doppelarbeit in der bestehenden Organisation.
Lightway steht dabei nicht allein: Es ist mit Privacy Flow und AI Flow von caralegal verbunden. Die Prüfung eines Tools landet nicht isoliert in einem Ticketsystem, sondern dort, wo Verarbeitungstätigkeiten, DSFA und KI-Verzeichnis bereits gepflegt werden. So entsteht eine Orchestrierung über alle Compliance-relevanten Anfragen hinweg. Ein zentraler Ort, an dem konzernweit sichtbar ist, was angefragt, geprüft und entschieden wird.
Warum ist organisatorische Effizienz heute ein Wettbewerbsvorteil?
Weniger Rückfragen sorgen für weniger Abstimmungsschleifen. Das Ergebnis ist der schnellere Erhalt einer belastbaren Dokumentation. Verzeichnis von Verarbeitungstätigkeiten (VVT), Datenschutz-Folgenabschätzung (DSFA) und Risikoeinschätzung sind in einem Workflow gepflegt und liegen anschließend nicht verstreut. Das wirkt sich auch auf Audits aus: Wenn Nachweise im Prozess entstehen und nicht erst nachträglich rekonstruiert werden, sinkt die Wahrscheinlichkeit lückenhafter Dokumentation bei einer Behördenprüfung.
Effizienz entsteht nicht durch weniger Compliance-Arbeit. Sie entsteht vielmehr durch die Reduzierung der organisatorischen Reibung.
Wer regulatorische Zusammenarbeit zentral organisiert, entscheidet schneller, weist Compliance besser nach und kann Prozesse skalieren, statt bei jeder neuen Verordnung Ressourcen aufstocken zu müssen.
Eine Anfrage statt drei: Ein Vorgang, eine Zuständigkeit, ein Nachweis. Erfahre, wie Freigaben vereinfacht und beschleunigt werden.

articles.title: Microsoft 365 Cuts Family OneDrive Storage from 6 TB to 2 TB
articles.text:
Friday, October 9th 2026
Microsoft 365 Cuts Family OneDrive Storage from 6 TB to 2 TB
Microsoft has updated its Microsoft 365 Family and Premium subscriptions to reduce the overall storage pool. Previously, these subscription tiers allowed one buyer to share a subscription with five additional family members, totaling six people using the service. Each person received 1 TB of OneDrive storage to use as they wished, resulting in a total of 6 TB of storage from a single subscription. However, Microsoft is now reducing this capacity to a total of 2 TB of OneDrive storage, shared among the six individuals.
Microsoft notes that the shared storage capacity now applies to the entire subscription rather than being assigned individually. This means your storage capacity isn't fixed and could affect others if you decide to store large files. It's important to note that all personal files, photos, and documents remain private by default, even with the shared storage system. However, your guaranteed capacity will depend on other members, as you all share the same storage pool. If you purchase additional storage capacity with OneDrive, it will be added to the shared pool that everyone can access. Realistically, if one person uploads large files, the others may be left with limited storage in their subscription.According to Microsoft, existing Microsoft 365 Family and Premium subscribers will generally transition to shared storage after their first renewal following May 2, 2027. Customers will receive detailed communications before the change occurs. If you choose to switch to a different eligible Microsoft 365 plan before your scheduled transition, such as upgrading from Microsoft 365 Family to Premium, the shared storage model might be implemented with this change, potentially taking effect before your first renewal after May 2, 2027.

articles.title: Neanderthal wooden tools from Spain found preserved in stone
articles.text:
The Stone Age owes its name to tools that survived to our time. The material early humans worked with most, though, was probably wood because it is so much easier to process. Unfortunately, we know very little about Paleolithic woodwork because wood rots relatively quickly. But at Abric Romaní, a rock shelter in Capellades, west of Barcelona, mineral-rich water coated wooden Neanderthal tools in a limestone-like crust. When wood rotted away, it left behind hollow molds that faithfully reflect its shape.
In a recent Science Advances study, a team of Spanish archaeologists has cataloged 597 wooden remains from Neanderthal living areas dating from 62,000 to 40,000 years ago. They found spears, digging sticks, bark trays, parts of shelters, and a club unlike anything seen before, suggesting Neanderthals were likely much more than just Homo sapiens’ dumber cousins.
Beyond hunting gear
The oldest wooden artifacts we have are mostly weapons. They include spears from a German town called Schöningen, a spear tip from Clacton-on-Sea in England, and the spear found alongside an elephant skeleton in Lehringen, Germany. Most came from waterlogged sediments, where a lack of oxygen slowed decay.
The spears mostly give us information about how Neanderthals hunted. The findings at Abric Romaní are different because the finds come from a place where Neanderthals lived, slept, cooked, and made tools over the course of some 20,000 years.
“We have a sample of wooden tools for different subsistence activities, not only hunting,” says M. Gema Chacón, an archaeologist at the Catalan Institute of Human Paleoecology and Social Evolution (IPHES-CERCA) and co-author of the study. Because wood turns up in level after level, it shows that woodworking was routine for Neanderthals rather than an occasional one-off.

articles.title: Nvidia reportedly halts GeForce RTX 5090 production in favor of AI data center and professional GPUs — impending supply drought expected to drive up prices, RTX 5080 24GB rumored as new gaming flagship
articles.text:
Nvidia reportedly halts GeForce RTX 5090 production in favor of AI data center and professional GPUs — impending supply drought expected to drive up prices, RTX 5080 24GB rumored as new gaming flagship
No more GB202 for consumers?
Nvidia has reportedly ceased selling its GB202 graphics processors for consumer-grade GeForce RTX 5090-series add-in-boards (AIBs), including 'D' variants for the Chinese market, according to a leaked notice from an unknown factory cited by @hongxing2020, who tends to have insights into the graphics card market. Another prominent leaker @Zed__Wang confirmed the report and said that from now on the GB202 silicon will be exclusively used on data center and professional graphics cards.
"According to a notification from the factory, Nvidia will no longer manufacture any RTX 5090 models, including the D variants," a message cited by @hongxing2020 reads. "Going forward, the highest-end GeForce graphics card will be the RTX 5080 24GB, while the RTX 5080 16GB version will be discontinued. Please spread the word."
This is, of course, an unverified claim and not an official Nvidia announcement. We asked Nvidia for a comment, though the company has yet to respond. Typically, Nvidia does not comment on rumors.
While the information is strictly unofficial for now, the alleged decision would make considerable economic sense for Nvidia, as the company can sell GB202 processors on data center and professional graphics cards that cost substantially more than the GeForce RTX 5090. In fact, Nvidia's recently introduced RTX Pro 5500 features the same number of CUDA cores — 21,760 — as the GeForce RTX 5090, but comes with 84GB of GDDR7 memory instead of 32GB and targets considerably more lucrative professional visualization (ProViz) and AI applications. Meanwhile, the fully-fledged RTX 6000 Pro with 24,064 CUDA cores and 96 GB of memory can easily sell for $15,000.
By discontinuing GB202-based GeForce products, Nvidia could prevent its relatively inexpensive consumer graphics cards from competing with its own professional accelerators in the lucrative AI sector. Essentially, the company is redirecting its limited semiconductor manufacturing allocation toward higher-margin products without necessarily sacrificing its position in the gaming market, as neither the GeForce RTX 5080 nor RTX 5090 have direct rivals.
Even if Nvidia has indeed discontinued shipments of GB202 processors for consumer graphics cards, GeForce RTX 5090 boards are unlikely to disappear from the market overnight. Nvidia's add-in-board partners, distributors, and retailers likely have inventories of GPUs and finished graphics cards that could sustain availability for some time. However, if Nvidia no longer supplies GB202 processors for GeForce products, the availability of RTX 5090 cards will inevitably decline, which will affect prices of these AIBs.
Meanwhile, Nvidia could be preparing to refresh its GeForce RTX 50-series lineup. The company has long been rumored to be developing GeForce RTX 50 Super graphics cards, including an RTX 5080 Super with 24GB of GDDR7 memory, although their introduction has reportedly been postponed due to memory supply constraints. The rumored GeForce RTX 5080 24GB could therefore represent a revival of these plans, and with no more GeForce RTX 5090 32GB on the market, the new product will have better memory supply.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Nvidia is also developing its next-generation Rubin-based GeForce RTX 60-series GPUs, but recent rumors suggest that these products will not arrive until late 2027, or even 2028. Consequently, if the reports about the discontinuation of the GeForce RTX 5090 are accurate, Nvidia could leave the enthusiast gaming market without a GB202-class flagship for a considerable period, so if you are in the market for the absolute best graphics card, now is the time to get it.
