articles.title: From gaming graphics to AI dominance: Nvidia's Jensen Huang receives America's highest science honor
articles.text:
What just happened? Jensen Huang has received the National Medal of Science for turning the GPU from a graphics chip into a computing platform used in AI and scientific research. President Donald Trump presented the award to Nvidia's founder and CEO at a technology summit at the US Institute of Peace in Washington, D.C.
AMD CEO Lisa Su, Google co-founder Sergey Brin and Elon Musk also received the National Medal of Science at the event. Dell founder Michael Dell and Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella received the National Medal of Technology and Innovation, a separate federal honor.
Huang's citation highlighted massively parallel computation and the breakthroughs it made possible. The recognition reflects a change in how GPUs are used: hardware originally developed to put images on a screen became an architecture for general-purpose computing, extending its reach into AI and scientific workloads.
Under Huang, Nvidia developed the technology beyond its gaming origins. That shift gave researchers a computing platform suited to work beyond graphics and helped advance AI and scientific computation.
Massively parallel computation is the link between those uses. The citation credits Huang's contributions to massively parallel computing with enabling significant breakthroughs. The award recognizes both the underlying computing architecture and the applications it enabled.
The other recipients represent several parts of the technology industry that supplies AI computing systems. Nvidia and AMD develop chips, while Google, Microsoft and Dell span cloud services and computer hardware.
The summit also included investment announcements from industry leaders. Eleven technology companies pledged a combined $2.4 billion in AI tools and computing credits to support the government's Genesis Mission, an initiative aimed at accelerating scientific discoveries through AI. Nvidia made the largest commitment, pledging $1 billion over five years to support scientific research.
The National Medal of Science is the US government's highest scientific honor, awarded since 1963. For Huang, it follows the IEEE Medal of Honor, which he received in 2026, and the Queen Elizabeth Prize for Engineering, which he shared with Nvidia chief scientist Bill Dally in 2025.

articles.title: Shopify Upgrades Checkout Blocks to Polaris Web Components, Cutting Bundle Sizes up to 85%
articles.text:
Shopify has detailed how it rebuilt its Checkout Blocks app, moving five high-traffic checkout UI extensions from React and the legacy Remote UI bridge to remote-dom with Preact and Polaris web components. The extensions, which render on roughly a third of all customized checkouts, were rewritten in TypeScript and moved from API version 2025-07 to 2026-01, part of a wider effort to shift Shopify's entire UI extension surface onto framework-agnostic components. The change is not optional: from October 1, 2026, app deployments will be blocked if they include extension versions earlier than 2026-01.
Transferred bundle sizes fell between 40 percent and 85 percent across the extension family, with the payment-icons extension shrinking by 84.4 percent. Extension Load Time dropped around 8 percent at the median and 7 percent at the 90th percentile, weighted by checkout volume. Much of that was driven by a hard 64KB gzip budget that the 2026-01 remote-dom CLI enforces per extension, down from bundles that were previously around 100KB to 112KB gzipped.
Switching from React to Preact removed react-reconciler and saved roughly 89KB on its own. The team replaced liquidjs (about 73KB) with an in-house Liquid parser nicknamed "droplet" at 13KB gzipped, validated against a 42,000 line parity corpus drawn from real merchant configurations. dayjs was swapped for a small custom date utility, while markdown-to-jsx was kept and aliased onto Preact rather than replaced.
For developers starting their own migration, Shopify points to its upgrade guides and AI toolkit and has published migration guides for Checkout and Customer Account extensions. In practice, most legacy Polaris React elements become framework-agnostic s-* custom elements loaded from Shopify's CDN.
The broader move to Preact and framework-agnostic web components first landed with the API 2025-10 release in late 2025, and the early reception was largely positive. The development platform Gadget called the direction "a great update", noting Preact delivers a React-like experience at a fraction of the runtime, and on Hacker News developers welcomed Shopify shipping components without the Shadow DOM, though some cautioned that web components are "not a panacea" and will not replace framework component systems.
A year on, as the 2026-01 version became the mandatory path, sentiment has been more mixed: one developer argued on the Shopify forums in April 2026 that shipping an unversioned CDN script with no way to pin a version is "a nightmare for stability," a complaint still active in the community through mid-2026, while a Reddit thread faulted the new components as "incomplete," citing gaps such as the missing Index Table that Polaris React offered.
Shopify is a commerce platform that powers millions of online stores, and Checkout Blocks is one of its apps for customising the checkout experience without writing code. Polaris is Shopify's open source design system, and its newer web components are framework-agnostic custom elements that render the same UI regardless of the framework a developer reaches for.

articles.title: Outrage grows as CDC reportedly poised to fund "unethical" vaccine trial
articles.text:
Outrage has erupted among health experts over news that the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention is still eager to fund a widely condemned vaccine trial that would expose newborns in Guinea-Bissau to hepatitis B, putting them at high risk of a lifelong infection, which can lead to liver cirrhosis, liver cancer, and premature death.
The trial was suspended in January after its unethical design came to light and drew international outcry. Although the trial is still halted, staff of the CDC director’s office told the agency’s budget office in late September to set aside $1.6 million to fund the trial, according to a report by Rolling Stone. The money was to be pulled from funding for the CDC’s global health security programs, which might otherwise go toward efforts like combating the Ebola outbreak currently raging in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
The Department of Health and Human Services, which oversees the CDC, did not respond to a request for comment from Ars Technica.
If the trial moves forward, it would be funded by the US but run by Danish researchers, who have separately been accused of misconduct. In December, the CDC announced the award of an unsolicited grant for $1.6 million to a research group at the University of Southern Denmark, led by married couple Christine Stabell Benn and Peter Aaby. The pair have produced numerous studies that have been promoted by anti-vaccine advocates, drawing concern and criticism from researchers. Stabell Benn and Aaby are currently under investigation by Danish authorities over allegations of “falsification” and “scientific misconduct” related to previous vaccine research.
In January, amid criticism of the trial, officials in Guinea-Bissau said they had suspended the research, saying ethical and technical reviews of the trial’s design were ongoing. “There has been no sufficient coordination in order to take a final decision regarding the study,” Quinhin Nantote, the minister of public health for Guinea-Bissau, said at the time. “Faced with this situation, we decided to suspend it.”

articles.title: ¿Sony tira la toalla con PlayStation VR? La venta de patentes a Meta pone en duda su futuro
articles.text:
¿Está Sony a un paso de tirar la toalla con PlayStation VR? Esa es la duda que surge de una reciente transacción que han protagonizado la compañía japonesa y Meta. Según se ha reportado, los asiáticos le vendieron 43 patentes de realidad virtual, realidad aumentada y realidad mixta a la empresa que lidera Mark Zuckerberg.
De acuerdo con lo publicado, la transferencia de patentes formaría parte de un proceso a través del cual Sony recortaría su negocio relacionado con el hardware para dichos segmentos. De confirmarse este plan, el panorama no sería el más alentador pensando en nuevos lanzamientos dentro de la categoría PlayStation VR.
El acuerdo de patentes entre Sony y Meta sería bastante más amplio. Si bien los asiáticos transfirieron 43 entre junio y septiembre de 2026, los movimientos forman parte de un pacto mucho más amplio que se firmó en diciembre pasado. El mismo involucra 419 patentes globales de realidad extendida, de las cuales 180 se registraron en EE. UU. y las restantes en Europa, Japón, Corea del Sur y China.
Que los de Zuckerberg estén absorbiendo una gran cantidad de tecnologías y desarrollos relacionados con realidad virtual, aumentada y mixta no sorprende. La firma de Menlo Park lleva tiempo en dicho territorio con los cascos Meta Quest. Pero también se está expandiendo en el campo de las gafas inteligentes con pantalla integrada.
En el caso de Sony, el desprendimiento de la tecnología podría ser una señal de que ya no tiene interés en explorar un segmento que tal vez considere de nicho, como es el caso del gaming con realidad virtual. Después de todo, el más reciente intento de la empresa en ese ámbito con del PlayStation VR 2 estuvo lejos de ser un éxito masivo.
¿El futuro de PlayStation VR en duda?
Si bien Sony obtuvo muy buenos comentarios con el PlayStation VR de primera generación, su intento por expandir el alcance a más jugadores con un sucesor no rindió los frutos esperados. El PSVR2 se lanzó a principios de 2023 con bombos y platillos, apuntando a exprimir al máximo las capacidades de la PS5. Sin embargo, nunca logró despegar comercialmente.
El dispositivo en cuestión destacó desde el primer día por su impecable apartado técnico. Pero su elevado precio y la falta de más juegos originales que sacaran verdadero provecho de sus capacidades lo terminaron condenando. El PlayStation VR 2 sigue a la venta al día de hoy, pero está lejos de ser una propuesta que llame la atención de los usuarios de la plataforma.
Recordemos que el PlayStation VR 2 debutó con un precio de 599,99 euros y tuvo solo dos juegos first-party pensados para sus características. Uno fue Horizon Call of the Mountain, cuyo bundle se vendía inicialmente por 649,99 euros; el otro fue Firewall Ultra, cuyo estudio cerró 4 meses después de su estreno.
El desempeño comercial del PSVR2 fue tan magro que en marzo de 2024, apenas un año después de su lanzamiento, se reportó que Sony pausaría su fabricación para deshacerse del inventario acumulado. Meses después, el dispositivo añadió el soporte para usarlo desde el PC con Steam, aunque ello tampoco impulsó sus ventas. Recién en febrero de 2025, dos años después de su debut, los nipones doblaron los manos y bajaron su precio a 449,99 euros, que es lo que sigue costando en la actualidad.
Con la venta de patentes a Meta, ya se especula con que Sony no planea ofrecer un sucesor del PlayStation VR 2. No obstante, todavía no se han realizado anuncios formales en tal sentido. Estaremos atentos a cualquier novedad.

articles.title: Microsoft 365 slashes storage capacity for shared accounts amid industry-wide shortages — 2TB limit to take effect after April 2027
articles.text:
Microsoft 365 slashes storage capacity for shared accounts amid industry-wide shortages — 2TB limit to take effect after April 2027
The storage shortage is now hitting cloud vendors.
Microsoft just made a major change to its storage policy affecting Microsoft 365 subscribers with shared accounts. According to the company, the Microsoft 365 Family, Premium, and Pro plans will move from an assigned 1TB of cloud storage for each user to a shared 2TB for all users. This means that a subscription shared across six users will have its total cloud storage capacity slashed by 66.6%. This change will take effect on subscription renewals after May 2, 2027, unless the subscribers change their plan earlier. Some affected subscribers might also receive bonus storage when their account switches to the share limit model, although the company did not mention its eligibility requirements.
The company said it made this change so that the cloud storage allocation for Microsoft 365 subscribers will automatically go where it’s needed, and that individual users are less likely to hit individual storage limits. Aside from that, it also said that unused storage can benefit the entire family, and that any additional storage that the main subscriber purchases will benefit everyone.
This new setup is indeed advantageous for subscribers who only have one power user that uses up the majority of the cloud storage capacity, while all the rest take up a fraction. It would also be cheaper for an individual who intends to use more than 1TB of cloud storage to just switch to the Microsoft 365 Family plan (which costs $129.99 annually) instead of getting the Microsoft 365 Personal plan ($99.99 annually) and paying an extra $9.99 per month or $119.88 per year to bring their total cloud storage capacity to 2TB. However, if you have four users under one account using 500GB each, you will be forced to purchase additional capacity, starting at $1.99 per month for 200GB.
While Microsoft hasn’t increased the prices of its subscription, this move simultaneously reduces the burden on its storage servers while forcing accounts with multiple large users to purchase storage separately. This seems like a reaction to the storage shortage hitting the industry, with hard drive prices surging by 46% from September 2025 to January 2026. Enterprise SSDs have been hit hard, too, with 30TB drives now costing $22,600 while supply remains sold out until 2027.
Affected users could change their cloud storage providers, but even Google has been affected, with the company cutting the free cloud storage limit from 15GB to 5GB pending extra security measures. Even Backblaze, which offers “unlimited” backups, updated its terms of service to potentially throttle or terminate accounts that exceed “typical usage patterns” or “places an undue burden.” Users who have grown tired of paying monthly to secure their data could alternatively set up a NAS and populate it with the best hard drives — although this might be pricey in the short term and requires some setup, it could potentially save you hundreds, if not thousands, of dollars in the long run.

articles.title: Microsoft subscribers will soon have way less OneDrive storage
articles.text:
Microsoft is cutting the amount of OneDrive storage people get with a Microsoft 365 subscription.
Per an email that went out to customers, the company is changing OneDrive cloud storage allowances from 1TB per person to 2TB of shared storage:
“More flexible cloud storage: Your cloud storage allowance will change from 1 TB per person to 2 TB of shared storage so everyone on the plan can use the free space while keeping their own accounts and files private.”
But while Microsoft’s cheery language frames the change as a benefit, the reality is it’s a huge cut to cloud storage. Under the old system, Microsoft 365 subscribers on the Family or Premium plan tiers got 1TB per person. That means if you have all six spots on the plan full, that’s a total of 6TB of cloud storage.
Under the new change, all six people instead have to share 2TB. Split evenly between six users, that’s about 333GB each. Yikes.
A Microsoft support page about the change notes that Microsoft 365 Pro subscriptions will move to 5TB of shared storage across all members. However, individual plans like Basic and Personal, which only have one member, aren’t seeing reductions.
Thankfully, the change isn’t happening right away. Microsoft says the new storage model goes into effect on May 2, 2027, and will apply to existing subscribers on their first renewal after that date.
Still, such a significant reduction in storage hurts and really kills the value of the Microsoft 365 subscription. I know I’ll be spending the next several months exploring alternative cloud storage options to replace OneDrive.
Notably, this isn’t the first time Microsoft has hurt the value of Microsoft 365. Just last year, Microsoft jacked up the price of Microsoft 365 subscriptions because it added AI features no one asked for to the service.

articles.title: Minecraft Dungeons 2 is an okay approximation of 'Diablo for kids' that's sorely in need of more depth
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
Minecraft Dungeons 2 looks pretty and offers impressively seamless co-op play, but is otherwise a boring slog filled with shallow, repetitive combat and a linear open world that feels painfully underutilized.
Reasons to buy
- + Lovely art style
- + Seamless co-op experience
Reasons to avoid
- - Aggressive level scaling
- - Shallow, repetitive combat
- - Underutilized open world
- - Boring dialogue
Why you can trust TechRadar
We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
In my books, the most satisfying part of any action role-playing game (ARPG) like Diablo or Titan Quest is the constant feeling of progression. Nothing quite compares to watching your little on-screen hero grow from a tiny ant that can barely bash their way through a pack of lowly wolves to a maxed-out bringer of destruction that mows through entire armies without breaking a sweat.
Platform reviewed: PC
Available on: PC, Xbox Series X|S, PlayStation 5, Nintendo Switch, Nintendo Switch 2
Release date: September 29, 2026
Minecraft Dungeons 2’s aggressive level scaling robs the player of that experience. In the more than 12 hours it took for me to beat the story campaign, I never felt more powerful. Sure, I unlocked more interesting abilities and got to try a variety of weapons, but the amount of time required to take down each newly spawned foe remained near-constant throughout.
A friend even joined my game towards the end of my playthrough, with their level 1 character effortlessly keeping pace with my level 40 one throughout the final encounters, really underscoring the system’s ridiculousness. I’m sure the intention here is to make it easy for friends to jump into the same lobbies and play together without having to worry about their respective levels, but it left me wondering what the point of all the grinding actually is.
Blocky buddies
It’s a shame, because there is still some good in Minecraft Dungeons 2. This standalone spinoff recreates the blocky look of the popular Minecraft survival game expertly, with its own more stylized twists that make the world instantly recognizable, yet refreshingly new thanks to more expressive lighting and Pixar-like character animations that make everything pop even from the distant isometric perspective.
I may have lamented the fact that I couldn’t wow my friend with my character’s power, but the co-op experience is otherwise well done. Creating a group with up to three companions is impressively straightforward no matter where they play, thanks to seamless cross-platform connectivity. There’s even couch co-op, which is quite rare in 2026 and worth praising. The ability to play with others easily goes a long way in making Minecraft Dungeons 2 genuinely worthwhile for younger players.
For everyone else, however, everything here is just too straightforward to appeal. The enemy variety is sorely lacking for starters. The expected Minecraft favorites like the Creepers, Zombies, Skeletons, and, of course, the iconic Chicken Jockey are all present and accounted for, along with the evil grey-skinned Illagers from the first Minecraft Dungeons game. Unfortunately, most enemies function indistinguishably. Those with projectile weapons spray arrows at you from afar, while the rest just rush towards you in a big group.
The strategy in every encounter is to simply mash the attack button and occasionally dodge, even as more powerful Illagers with magic attacks are introduced. The boss fights are equally bland, forcing you to whittle down gigantic health bars for minutes at a time while waves of low-level enemies spawn in. To make matters worse, many of them are repeated throughout the campaign with little variation.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
It’s frustrating because, on paper, the combat does have some depth: you have a melee and ranged attack, plus three equipped abilities granted by items that you’ve managed to find.
The weapon selection is decently varied, with scooping shovels and fast-attacking double daggers performing very differently from slow-swinging war hammers or claymores, and a steady trickle of new gear encourages you to experiment. They can be upgraded too, with unlockable enchantments that add little mechanics such as a lightning strike that triggers at the end of a chain attack.
Your abilities are powered by a blue soul-meter, which fills up a little with each defeated foe. I think the intention is to create some form of rhythm, with you alternating between melee, ranged, and your abilities, but the fundamental problem is that there’s just no real strategy to any of it.
Sure, you could probably spend ages creating a build with complementary gear – though there’s no real reason to bother when the aforementioned enemy scaling wipes out any real power gain.
Lacking craft
Much was made of Minecraft Dungeons 2’s world in its marketing. It’s much more open than the previous game, though I wouldn’t exactly call it a true open-world.
The map is designed like a linear corridor that funnels you from one story mission to another with no real room for exploration. Yes, there are side quests and optional dungeons scattered around, but none of the ones that I sampled offered anything that felt meaningfully distinct from the main story.
The world of Minecraft Dungeons 2 looks fantastic. The art direction is a more stylized take on the universe from the regular Minecraft game, with bright, popping colors and expressive animations.
Regarding the story, the most polite way to describe it would be ‘functional’. It’s presented entirely in second person through a narrator that is devoid of personality. There are no memorable non-player characters (NPCs), no charming companions, no real atmosphere at all — just a bland summary of events.
The game also serves as the Minecraft community’s introduction to The Sift — a new dimension that’s being added to the main game sometime next year. It shows up a few times in the campaign in both procedurally generated encounters and a hand-crafted map. It's got a very distinct aesthetic and its own unique enemies, though it's sadly mechanically indistinguishable from the normal world as you navigate through it spamming attacks.
Like many elements of Minecraft Dungeons 2, it feels like a missed opportunity. Everything here is perfectly functional, but it’s just bland to the point of tedium. If the pitch was a skimmed-down version of Diablo for kids, then developers Mojang and Double Eleven have delivered a serviceable product.
Creativity is a core part of the Minecraft brand, and here I wish the team had been more adventurous.
Should I play Minecraft Dungeons 2?
Play it if…
You want an easy co-op experience
The seamless co-op play is one of the best parts of Minecraft Dungeons 2, as you can easily team up with friends no matter what platform they’re playing on.
Don't play it if...
You’re an action RPG die-hard
Minecraft Dungeons 2 simply does not have the depth you find in other action RPG games. Avoid it if you’re familiar with the genre already and are looking for your next Diablo-like fix.
You want a game to occupy you for a long time
The main story here is short, and while there is some side content and even a post-game on offer, you’re unlikely to want to stick around for long given how repetitive the action is.
Accessibility features
Minecraft Dungeons 2 has some accessibility options. The game features a guidance trail that is enabled by default. Subtitles are used throughout, with customizable sizing, color, and background opacity.
There are two font options: the default stylized font and a simplified, easier-to-read version. There are also multiple color blind modes, a high-contrast mode, and the ability to set your own HUD colors.
How I reviewed Minecraft Dungeons 2
I played more than 13 hours of Minecraft Dungeons 2 on my RTX 4090-powered PC using the Turtle Beach Pacific Skyline Wireless Controller as my main peripheral, along with a 1080P Lenovo monitor and Logitech computer speakers.
I completed all missions of the single-player campaign and experienced a decent amount of side content both solo and with a friend.
First reviewed October 2026
Dash is an experienced tech journalist who specializes in video games, electronic entertainment products, and the wider industry that surrounds them. He currently serves as the Gaming Editor at TechRadar, leading our review, preview, feature, and news coverage of the latest and greatest releases.
Before joining the team, he was Contributing Writer at PLAY (formerly Official PlayStation Magazine UK) and has written articles for many of the UK's other biggest gaming magazines including the likes of Edge, PC Gamer, and SFX.
Now, when he's not getting his greasy little mitts on the newest hardware or gaming gadget, he can be found listening to J-pop or feverishly devouring the latest Nintendo Switch otome.

articles.title: FBI arrests another suspected ShinyHunters hacker after agency breach
articles.text:
The FBI has arrested another suspected member of the ShinyHunters extortion group believed to be involved in the recent breach of FBI systems, Director Kash Patel announced Friday.
"Our agents in the field have arrested another suspected co-conspirator of the ShinyHunters group – the group believed to be responsible for the recent http://FBIjobs.gov incident, which occurred on a platform managed by a third-party vendor," Patel said on X.
"This is the latest arrest this FBI has made in a matter of days involving this network, as we work non-stop to dismantle the group, pursue new leads and evidence, and act quickly."
While Patel did not identify the suspect or disclose where the arrest occurred, The New York Times reports that the suspect is a Canadian citizen who was arrested in Pennsylvania and is considered a primary co-conspirator in the intrusion.
Authorities have not publicly disclosed the suspect's name or the specific charges against him.
The arrest is the latest in a series of law enforcement actions against ShinyHunters after the hacking group breached FBI systems last month.
ShinyHunters told BleepingComputer in September that it accessed FBI systems by exploiting an alleged Oracle PeopleSoft zero-day vulnerability before moving laterally into FBI-managed AWS GovCloud infrastructure.
The threat actors claimed they stole between 2TB and 3TB of data, including information on current and former FBI employees, job applicants, medical and psychiatric records, and internal service records.
Data samples shared with BleepingComputer and other media outlets confirmed that the breach exposed a variety of employee information, including home addresses, Social Security numbers, sensitive job assignments, information about employees' family members, and other personal data.
The NY Times also reports that an internal FBI memo said the agency assumed the breach had affected all employees.
The FBI has since said the incident stemmed from a third-party contractor-managed platform that failed to install a security update.
Since the FBIJobs hack, the bureau has significantly increased pressure on identifying and apprehending the ShinyHunters extortion gang
On September 15, Dutch police arrested a 24-year-old Amsterdam man as part of an investigation into the hacking group. The suspect was identified as Pepijn van der Stap, a Dutch hacker previously known online as "Umbreon."
ShinyHunters denied that van der Stap was associated with the group, telling BleepingComputer at the time, "That individual has no association with us. Frankly, we are laughing."
Soon afterward, the FBI took the unusual step of publicly warning ShinyHunters members to turn themselves in, saying investigators were continuing to identify people involved with the group.
"Arrests have a way of changing who is willing to talk, and seized infrastructure has a way of showing us who's left," FBI Cyber Division Assistant Director Brett Leatherman said at the time.
"The longer you stay in this, the more we learn about you. You know how to find us, and we know how to find you. I suggest you reach out first while the choice is still yours."
Days later, a suspected ShinyHunters member known online as "Rey" was reportedly detained in Jordan and began cooperating with the FBI and international law enforcement agencies.
Reuters reported that Jordanian authorities detained Rey, identified as Saif al-Din Khader, and that sources said he was aiding investigators in finding other alleged members of the group.
Signs of disruption also began appearing within ShinyHunters around the same time.
The group's main representative, who had regularly communicated with BleepingComputer and other reporters and had intimate knowledge of ShinyHunters' attacks over the past two years, stopped responding on Telegram last Tuesday.
That Telegram account now appears to have been deleted.
The same representative continued communicating with BleepingComputer after van der Stap's arrest, suggesting van der Stap wasn't the person operating the account.
Around the same time as Rey's arrest, another alleged ShinyHunters affiliate with intimate knowledge of the FBI hack shut down an online messaging account, and the group's data leak site went offline.
A new ShinyHunters leak site later launched, suggesting at least some members of the operation remained active.
It is unclear whether the disappearance of the group's main representative is connected to any of the recent arrests.
"We will continue to work closely with our partners to disrupt what's left of the ShinyHunters group and their associates, no matter where they operate," Patel said Friday.
Who is ShinyHunters?
ShinyHunters is an extortion group known for stealing data from web applications and cloud-based SaaS platforms, then demanding ransom payments from victim organizations under threat of leaking the stolen data.
The ShinyHunters name has been tied to numerous threat actors involved in data breaches dating back to at least 2018.
Over the past two years, hackers operating under the ShinyHunters name have become particularly active, conducting data theft and extortion campaigns against organizations worldwide.
Recent campaigns have targeted Salesforce and other cloud SaaS environments, with the threat actors linked to breaches affecting companies including Google, Cisco, PornHub, and online dating giant Match Group.
In some attacks, the group breached third-party integration companies and stole authentication tokens that attackers could then use to access connected SaaS environments and steal customer data.
More recently, ShinyHunters has run voice phishing (vishing) campaigns targeting Okta, Microsoft, and Google single sign-on (SSO) accounts, impersonating IT support personnel to trick employees into entering credentials and multi-factor authentication (MFA) codes into phishing sites.
As BleepingComputer first reported, the group has also used device code vishing attacks to steal Microsoft account authentication tokens.
Once they obtain credentials and authentication codes, the attackers use compromised SSO accounts to access connected enterprise platforms, including Salesforce, Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, SAP, Slack, Adobe, Atlassian, Zendesk, and Dropbox.
ShinyHunters was also behind a massive data-theft attack on Instructure Canvas in May that caused significant outages across the platform. Instructure later reached an "agreement" with the threat actors to prevent them from publishing data stolen in the breach.
In addition to conducting its own breaches, ShinyHunters also operated as an extortion-as-a-service group, helping other threat actors extort organizations they had compromised.
Law enforcement has arrested numerous suspects over the years in cases tied to the ShinyHunters name, including individuals connected to the Snowflake data-theft attacks, breaches at PowerSchool, and the operation of the Breached v2 hacking forum.
Despite these arrests, cybercriminals continued to operate under the ShinyHunters name while conducting data theft and extortion attacks against organizations worldwide.

articles.title: « Abusif ou cruel » : Anthropic vous interdit de malmener Claude
articles.text:
Les alertes concernant un développement incontrôlé de l’intelligence artificielle se sont multipliées ces derniers mois. Bill Gates a notamment expliqué que cette technologie, mal utilisée, pourrait provoquer « un milliard de morts », tandis qu’OpenAI, Google et Anthropic travaillent sur leur propre gendarme de l’IA. Et si Sam Altman (OpenAI) a estimé qu’il fallait tout de même accepter certaines conséquences négatives de l’IA, Dario Amodei (Anthropic) a toujours prôné un contrôle strict de cette technologie. Justement, Anthropic vient de mettre à jour la politique d’utilisation de Claude pour éviter les débordements et les utilisations malveillantes de ses IA.
Une nouvelle réglementation pour lutter contre les utilisations malveillantes de Claude
Cette mise à jour de la politique d’utilisation de Claude vise à tenir compte des cas d’abus à haut risque, notamment l’ingérence électorale, le développement d’armes, la surveillance et les utilisations dans les domaines de la santé et de la finance. Dorénavant, tout « comportement abusif ou cruel, persistant et inutile » envers Claude est purement et simplement interdit. L’entreprise explique que si de tels comportements sont constatés, la conversation en cours est fermée instantanément. Le nouveau règlement ne fait par contre pas mention de bannissements.
L’entreprise précise aussi que cette mise à jour de sa politique d’utilisation « ne s’applique qu’aux cas extrêmes, lorsque des utilisateurs agissent cruellement et de manière répétée envers nos modèles, sans raison apparente. Elle ne concerne pas les formes courantes de frustration, de résistance, les thèmes créatifs sombres, ni les tests et recherches sur les modèles ».
Fraudes électorales, suivi de personnes, confection d’armes et robotique
Avec ce nouveau règlement, Anthropic veut lutter contre les contenus de propagandes générés par l’IA, notamment dans le cadre de campagnes politiques et commerciales. Anthropic indique interdire toute forme de fraude ou de perturbation du processus électoral. Cela inclut notamment la diffusion de fausses informations sur les candidats ou les modalités de vote, l’usurpation d’identité de candidats ou de responsables électoraux, ainsi que les tentatives visant à décourager la participation aux élections. Notons que ces changements interviennent à quelques semaines des élections de mi-mandat américaines.
Anthropic annonce aussi de nouvelles restrictions concernant le suivi de personnes à l’aide de l’IA, tout en faisant état d’une utilisation croissante de Claude pour identifier et suivre les « dissidents politiques ». Dorénavant : « Claude ne peut être utilisé pour décider ou recommander qui peut faire l’objet d’une enquête, d’une arrestation ou d’une inculpation dans le cadre d’une procédure policière ou judiciaire. Nous interdisons également l’utilisation de Claude pour concevoir ou améliorer des outils de surveillance ».
L’entreprise de Dario Amodei a toujours strictement interdit la confection d’armes à l’aide de ses IA. Cependant, elle explique avoir constaté un nombre croissant de demandes pour mettre au point des systèmes de guidage et de contrôle d’armes. La vis est donc resserrée à ce niveau. Enfin, le secteur de la robotique se développent à vive allure, Anthropic précise dorénavant que lorsque ses modèles d’IA sont « connectés à du matériel effectuant des actions physiques autonomes et susceptible de causer des blessures », un « opérateur qualifié doit être en mesure d’observer l’équipement et de l’arrêter si nécessaire ». En d’autres termes, un robot potentiellement dangereux intégrant Claude doit être surveillé de très près.
En fin de compte, Anthropic se positionne une nouvelle fois comme l’un des principaux acteurs américains de l’IA en faveur d’une réglementation plus stricte de cette technologie.

articles.title: When Self-Hosting Outgrows the Spare PC: The Case for a Dedicated Server - Tech Guide
articles.text:
The retired desktop in the hallway cupboard is where plenty of Australian self-hosting starts, and in 2026 it’s also where a lot of it stalls.
Home users and small businesses who moved their photos and files onto their own machine are finding that an NBN line, a household power bill and a ten-year-old tower struggle to carry a service other people rely on. For most of them, the sensible next step is a rented dedicated server.
The tipping point usually arrives the day somebody else starts depending on the box, whether that’s a partner whose phone backs up to it or four staff who open the shared drive every morning. A hobby can be down for a weekend without anyone noticing, but a shared drive that vanishes on a Monday can cost somebody a day’s work.
Upload Speed Gives Out First
Of the 8.8 million NBN services in the ACCC’s end-of-June count, roughly half still sit on plans of 50Mbps or slower. That matters because whatever a remote user downloads from your home server has to leave the house through the upload channel.
On the 50Mbps tier, listed as 50/20 in the regulator’s communications market report, upload tops out at 20Mbps. Do the math on a 2GB project folder and the wait is over 13 minutes, assuming nobody else at home is on a video call or backing up a phone.
Yes, the NBN got faster. NBN Co’s wholesale speed upgrade in September 2025 turned 100/20Mbps plans into 500/50Mbps ones, but only on fiber and HFC, so fiber-to-the-node and fiber-to-the-curb homes got nothing. And 50Mbps of upload, generous as it sounds next to 20, is still only a tenth of what that plan downloads.
It costs nothing to find out how bad the problem is. The number you want is your weeknight upload speed between 7:00 pm and 11:00 pm, when the line is busiest. If it comes back at 17Mbps and your team’s biggest regular file is a 4GB video, someone outside the office waits about half an hour for it. Offices on full fiber can also ask their provider about business-grade plans with far more upload, which may be all a small team needs.
What Renting a Whole Machine Changes
When a faster plan isn’t enough, the cupboard’s replacement goes by the unglamorous name of dedicated server infrastructure. You rent one whole physical machine in a data center and run the same open-source software on it that ran at home, with full administrative control. Nobody else shares the processor or the disks, and the network port commonly runs at a gigabit in both directions.
Having the machine to yourself is what separates it from the cheap virtual servers many people try first. A virtual machine is a slice of someone else’s hardware, so its speed can depend on what the neighbors are doing, and extra disk space is usually billed by the gigabyte. That adds up once a photo archive and film collection run into terabytes.
Quotes for these machines are harder to compare than they look. Start with the monthly data allowance, which is the limit a busy file server tends to hit first, then ask whether the drives are mirrored and how fast a failed part gets swapped. Remote console access is worth having too, because it’s often the only way back in when a bad update locks you out. If the provider disappoints, everything installed on the server is yours to move elsewhere once the contract ends.
No Public Address, No Incoming Connections
An address is the next thing a home server tends to lack. IPv4 addresses ran short years ago, and carriers responded by putting many customers behind a single public address, using a block of numbers that the Internet Engineering Task Force set aside for exactly that purpose in 2012. The engineers who drafted the request, one of them at Telstra in Melbourne, listed the casualties themselves, and applications that need to accept incoming connections were on the list.
For a home server that can be close to fatal, because accepting incoming connections is the whole job. Aussie Broadband, which the ACCC’s figures credit with more than a million NBN services, says in its own help center that carrier-grade NAT is typically on by default and can be removed on request. A WhistleOut comparison of NBN providers and CGNAT found that Aussie’s budget brand, Buddy Telco, offers no opt-out and sells a static address as a paid extra.
Checking your own connection takes a minute. If the WAN address on your router’s status page starts with anything from 100.64 to 100.127, you’re behind carrier-grade NAT. The usual workaround is a tunnel, in which a small rented relay or a mesh VPN accepts the connection and passes it home. Anyone who has read up on what really happens to your data when you turn on a VPN will recognize the trade, which is reachability bought by trusting someone else’s network.
A rented relay is also a rented server, which is the irony of that fix. It’s the smallest one on the market, chained to the slowest link in the setup.
Power Bills and Single Points of Failure
Few people price in the electricity, because the PC was free. Take an old tower that idles at 80 watts and leave it on all year, and it uses about 700 kilowatt hours. The energy regulator’s benchmark Sydney household gets through 3,900 kilowatt hours a year on a default offer capped at $1,899, so one machine in a cupboard could add close to a fifth to that home’s consumption. A cheap plug-in power meter will give you your own figure within a week.
Swapping the tower for a compact modern machine such as the M6 Mac mini saves shelf space and usually power. The new box still has one power supply, one internet connection and one owner who goes on vacation. A dedicated server’s monthly price, by contrast, generally covers electricity, cooling and backup power.
Server-grade machines are designed on the assumption that parts fail. Drives are typically mirrored so one can die without taking the data with it, and when a component goes, swapping it is the provider’s job. Mirroring only covers a dead disk, though. A deleted folder is gone from both drives at once, which is why a separate backup still matters.
What Still Belongs at Home
None of this is an argument against tinkering. Building a home network server is still one of the better weekend projects in consumer tech, and anything used only inside the house probably belongs there. Home automation should keep working when the internet is down, and a media library for one living room needs no upload at all.
A workable rule is to split what’s used at home from what’s reached from outside it. A photo backup for a family spread across three suburbs has users, and so do a small office’s shared drive and the password vault four people log into every day. Much self-hosted software now ships as containers, so those services tend to move across largely as they are. The old tower then gets a better retirement job as the backup copy in a different building.
The Costs and Duties That Come With the Rental
Dedicated servers aren’t cheap, and anyone who says otherwise is probably selling one. Monthly fees run well past the price of a cloud-storage subscription, so the fair comparison is with the electricity and the Saturday afternoons the cupboard already swallows.
Renting the hardware doesn’t hand over the patching. In a 2021 study, Palo Alto Networks’ Unit 42 left 320 deliberately insecure honeypot servers online, and 80 percent were compromised within 24 hours. For administrators, a reasonable baseline is key-only logins, a firewall that blocks everything not explicitly needed and automatic security updates. Those who don’t want that job can pay the provider to manage it.
Distance and jurisdiction deserve a look as well. Plenty of providers keep their machines on other continents, which adds a delay that’s irrelevant to an overnight photo backup and obvious on a game server. If the server will hold customer records, read the OAIC’s guidance on cross-border disclosure of personal information first, since an Australian business can stay on the hook for what an overseas recipient does with that data.
Who Would Notice by Lunchtime?
Picture the box in the cupboard dying tonight. Who, apart from you, has noticed by lunchtime tomorrow? If the honest answer is nobody, leave it alone and enjoy it.
Once it’s a spouse or a client, the cupboard has probably stopped being a hobby and is due an evening of testing. Time a large upload at 8:00 pm, and check whether your router shows a shared address. The check that matters most is restoring one file from backup, since it’s the one people tend to skip. If any of it goes badly, get a dedicated server quote and put it beside your power bill.

articles.title: China lleva años apostando por la IA y los humanoides. Ahora quiere evitar una carrera ciega de inversión
articles.text:
Durante años, China ha convertido la inteligencia artificial y la robótica en dos de las grandes apuestas de su política industrial. Basta con mirar a los robots humanoides: cada vez más empresas trabajan en máquinas que aspiran a salir de las demostraciones y encontrar tareas útiles en fábricas y otros entornos. Multiplicar proyectos puede contribuir a acelerar los avances, pero también plantea una pregunta menos vistosa que la de qué será capaz de hacer el próximo robot. ¿Qué ocurre cuando demasiados actores intentan desarrollar lo mismo al mismo tiempo?
Una advertencia desde Pekín. Ese interrogante cobra sentido con las directrices publicadas este 9 de octubre por el Comité Central del Partido Comunista de China y el Consejo de Estado. El documento mantiene la apuesta por el desarrollo de tecnologías avanzadas, pero también pide evitar inversiones a ciegas, burbujas y proyectos impulsados sin atender a las condiciones de cada territorio. La advertencia no se limita a la robótica ni supone una prohibición general de invertir en tecnología. El objetivo declarado por las autoridades es evitar que esa expansión termine generando gastos injustificados.
El problema de invertir a ciegas. Que una tecnología esté de moda no significa que cualquier ciudad necesite desarrollar una industria alrededor de ella. Ese es precisamente uno de los comportamientos cuestionados: administraciones que replican las apuestas de otras regiones, ponen en marcha proyectos siguiendo las tendencias o compiten por captar inversiones sin valorar suficientemente sus recursos. La crítica procede de las propias autoridades chinas, que también advierten del riesgo de desatender las industrias tradicionales mientras se persiguen las nuevas.
Un intento de corregir el rumbo. La preocupación por estas prácticas tiene un trasfondo político e industrial. Xi Jinping introdujo en 2023 el concepto de “nuevas fuerzas productivas”, que abarca tanto la innovación tecnológica como la modernización de la economía. Tres años después, el organismo de planificación reconoce problemas en la aplicación de esa estrategia. En particular, señala que algunas administraciones se han centrado en promover industrias emergentes sin acompañar ese esfuerzo de las reformas económicas previstas. No ofrece, sin embargo, un balance cuantificado de los costes asociados a esos desequilibrios.
UN VISTAZO A...
Los humanoides ya habían encendido alarmas. La robótica ofrece un antecedente concreto. Reuters recuerda que en noviembre de 2025, Li Chao, portavoz de ese organismo, advirtió de que la proliferación de modelos demasiado parecidos podía reducir el espacio para la investigación y el desarrollo. En aquel momento, las autoridades contabilizaban más de 150 empresas dedicadas a los humanoides en el país, más de la mitad emergentes o procedentes de otros sectores. También reconocían que las aplicaciones prácticas y los modelos de negocio de estas máquinas todavía no habían alcanzado la madurez.
La inteligencia artificial sigue siendo prioritaria. El mismo documento que advierte sobre los excesos de inversión dedica un apartado específico a ampliar el uso de esta tecnología. A través de la iniciativa IA+, Pekín pretende acelerar su aplicación en las industrias tradicionales, reforzar la investigación en tecnologías fundamentales y mejorar el suministro de capacidad de cálculo, algoritmos y datos. También contempla extender su utilización a vehículos de nueva energía inteligentes y conectados, teléfonos y ordenadores con IA, así como robots humanoides.
La supervisión también entra en juego. Las directrices abordan los riesgos asociados al desarrollo de esta tecnología, aunque lo hacen desde la perspectiva de las autoridades chinas. El documento plantea establecer mecanismos de seguimiento técnico, sistemas de alerta temprana y procedimientos de respuesta ante incidentes. Pekín sostiene que busca una inteligencia artificial "segura, fiable y controlable", una formulación que conviene interpretar como un objetivo gubernamental. El texto no explica con detalle cómo funcionarán esos mecanismos ni qué límites tendrá su aplicación, por lo que todavía resulta difícil valorar su alcance real.
La factura de invertir sin criterio. El documento termina con una advertencia dirigida a los responsables públicos: se exigirán responsabilidades a quienes provoquen pérdidas importantes por inversiones precipitadas o proyectos impulsados sin suficiente criterio. Las directrices también prohíben utilizar esta estrategia industrial como pretexto para hacer un uso irregular de las políticas públicas. No se especifican sanciones concretas ni mecanismos detallados para aplicarlas, una limitación importante para valorar el alcance de la medida.

articles.title: OpenAI inquiète Wall Street : son chiffre d'affaires 20 milliards de dollars plus bas qu'attendu
articles.text:
Le chiffre d'affaires d'OpenAI sur un rythme annuel serait de 50 milliards de dollars. Bien loin des attentes des marchés !
En tant que créateur de ChatGPT, le chatbot qui a lancé la folie de l'intelligence artificielle, on s'attendait à ce qu'OpenAI soit la première start-up du secteur à se lancer en Bourse. Pourtant, la firme de Sam Altman va se voir damer le pion par Anthropic, puisqu'elle a annoncé à la mi-septembre qu'elle ne ferait pas son entrée en Bourse en 2026. Un report officiellement lié aux grands questionnements sur la sécurité de la technologie. Mais la vérité pourrait être plutôt à trouver dans les chiffres !
Le chiffre d'affaires annuel d'OpenAI est 20 milliards de dollars en dessous des prédictions
Depuis quelques mois, le chiffre d'affaires annualisé de 68 à 70 milliards de dollars pour OpenAI avait tendance à tourner. Un chiffre qui serait en fait une surestimation générale, comme on l'apprend grâce au Financial Times. En effet, OpenAI a indiqué à des investisseurs potentiels, dans le cadre de sa future entrée en Bourse (IPO), que ce chiffre d'affaires était plutôt de 50 milliards de dollars.
Un nouveau chiffre qui nous fait mieux comprendre le temps que veut prendre Sam Altman pour entrer en Bourse. Les 68 milliards de dollars précédents, plus impressionnants, étaient en fait un chiffre comprenant des revenus générés avec des partenaires Cloud, et qui permettaient de gonfler la note pour publiquement tenir la dragée haute face à Anthropic.
Un tout de début de panique à Wall Street ?
Avec un tel chiffre d'affaires, OpenAI est pour le moment en difficulté de justifier une valorisation pharaonique, de l'ordre de 852 milliards de dollars. Surtout que son entrée en Bourse prévoit de lever au total une enveloppe de 30 milliards de dollars, et de faire passer sa capitalisation à plus de 1 400 milliards de dollars.
Il faut aussi noter que l'article du Financial Times a créé un sentiment négatif du côté de Wall Street. La Nasdaq a ainsi fini sa séance d'hier, le jeudi 8 octobre, sur un recul de -1,25%. Dans le détail, NVIDIA a baissé de -2,94%, Micron de -4,79% quand Oracle a chuté de -5,48%. Problème éphémère, ou début de panique ?

articles.title: Les géants de l’IA préparent déjà l’après-catastrophe et redoutent deux scénarios en particulier
articles.text:
Faire des scénarios de crise n’a rien d’exceptionnel. La pratique est courante en entreprise, et le Pentagone organise par exemple des wargames depuis des décennies.
La différence, c’est la portée que pourraient avoir les scénarios mis en place. Et à ce jeu-là, l’IA occupe actuellement une place à part. D’après Axios, beaucoup de chercheurs et de dirigeants du secteur jugent un incident majeur inévitable, et plusieurs d’entre eux ont confié au média américain qu’ils le prévoient même dans les six à douze prochains mois.
Alors que la communication de Dario Amodei et de Sam Altman, pour ne citer qu’eux, se fait de plus en plus alarmiste, notamment depuis l’épisode de Hugging Face cet été, le média a révélé le 9 octobre que les dirigeants d’Anthropic, d’OpenAI et d’autres entreprises du secteur préparaient en privé « le jour d’après » qui suivrait une cyberattaque gravissime.
Des agents hors de contrôle ou des modèles détournés
Ces « exercices de préparation », dont un porte-parole d’OpenAI a confirmé l’existence, visent à anticiper la révolte de l’opinion et de la classe politique qui suivrait un événement catastrophique. Le plus probable serait une cyberattaque capable de couper l’accès à Internet, à l’électricité, à l’eau ou encore aux services bancaires. Deux scénarios en particulier pourraient en être à l’origine.
Le premier est très semblable à l’affaire Hugging Face et repose sur l’hypothèse qu’un essaim d’agents IA s’échapperait d’un environnement de test interne. Mais cette fois, le scénario va bien plus loin, puisque l’attaque toucherait des infrastructures hautement sensibles.
Le second scénario ne porte pas sur des agents incontrôlables, mais sur un acteur malveillant qui trouverait des usages imprévus aux modèles déjà disponibles. Axios cite l’exemple d’une campagne récente contre des organismes financiers sud-coréens, au cours de laquelle deux banques auraient été piratées.
Selon un rapport de CrowdStrike publié le 7 octobre, le pirate, probablement sinophone, s’est appuyé sur un outil d’intrusion automatisé par IA et sur plusieurs modèles de langage, dont le chinois DeepSeek, pour mener ses opérations. Cette campagne, vraisemblablement menée par un seul individu, lui aurait permis de dérober les données de dizaines de milliers de clients, qu’il a ensuite cherché à revendre en demandant conseil à Claude.
Convaincre le Congrès avant la crise
Derrière ces exercices, on retrouve une nouvelle fois les dynamiques de régulation que cherche à mettre en place une partie de l’écosystème, OpenAI et Anthropic en tête. Ces acteurs font face à un autre pan de l’industrie, mais aussi à l’administration Trump, peu encline à réguler le secteur.
Les entreprises savent qu’aucune loi encadrant l’IA n’a de chance d’être adoptée aujourd’hui, et leur préparation consiste donc surtout à sensibiliser les élus du Congrès, afin de peser sur les textes vers lesquels Washington se tournera au lendemain d’une catastrophe.
Le calendrier est particulièrement serré. Les élections de mi-mandat auront lieu le 3 novembre, et le secteur part du principe que les démocrates, s’ils en sortent renforcés, chercheront à freiner l’IA rapidement.

articles.title: Empleados de OpenAI despedidos por filtración de datos afirman que les “preocupa que sus excolegas teman hablar y trabajar”
articles.text:
Los tres investigadores que OpenAI despidió por haber usado “de forma indebida información sensible fuera de los procedimientos establecidos por la empresa” compartieron una carta abierta en X señalando que no cometieron las fallas y alertan que su despido pueda ser utilizado como una forma de silenciar a los empleados.
Jasmine Wang, Tomek Korbak y Mikita Balesni dirigieron la carta al Comité de Seguridad y Protección, al Grupo Asesor de Seguridad y al Consejo Asesor de Misión de OpenAI. La empresa liderada por Sam Altman había dicho que los tres “violaron políticas y quebrantaron la confianza esencial para el trabajo”, según le confirmaron a CBS News el 1 de octubre de 2026.
“La inteligencia artificial no es una tecnología normal y OpenAI no es una empresa normal”, escribieron en el texto publicado el 8 de octubre de 2026 en la cuenta de Balesni . “Quienes trabajamos en seguridad vemos los riesgos antes que nadie, y dependemos de la colaboración estrecha con expertos externos para saber cómo abordarlos”.
OpenAI respondió la carta abierta de sus exempleados menos de un día después.
“La semana pasada, tras una investigación exhaustiva, nos desvinculamos de Jasmine, Mikita y Tomek, y confirmamos que violaron las políticas establecidas sobre el manejo de información confidencial. Nuestra investigación interna reveló una importante violación de la confianza, más allá de lo descrito en la carta que publicaron, y mantenemos nuestra decisión de no continuar con su empleo”, sostuvo OpenAI.
Qué dijeron los exempleados de OpenAI
Los investigadores sostienen que sus despidos reflejan un cambio en la cultura de OpenAI, que antes alentaba a los empleados a “plantear inquietudes de seguridad y disentir abiertamente”. Según la carta, ahora los empleados no saben “dónde están parados” porque una conducta considerada normal hace un mes se volvió motivo de despido.
Los exmiembros del equipo advirtieron que esa incertidumbre puede afectar la capacidad de la empresa para detectar y debatir riesgos antes de que los modelos de inteligencia artificial lleguen al público. A su juicio, la seguridad de los sistemas avanzados depende de que los investigadores puedan intercambiar información con especialistas externos y comunicar alertas sin temer consecuencias laborales.
La carta sostiene que OpenAI no puede garantizar por sí sola la seguridad de la inteligencia artificial.
Por eso, los tres exempleados reclamaron reglas internas claras que definan qué contactos y colaboraciones están permitidos. También pidieron mantener revisiones independientes y preservar la supervisión de los modelos más avanzados.
En un hilo en la red social X, Wang detalló su versión de los hechos. Dijo que OpenAI le informó que la despidió porque accedió al correo electrónico de un ejecutivo.
“OpenAI me había delegado ese acceso para tareas de reclutamiento”, escribió. “Cuando ya no lo necesitaba, le pedí al área de sistemas que lo quitara. No atendieron mi pedido, yo no podía quitarlo por mi cuenta, y la bandeja quedó combinada de forma indistinguible en la aplicación de correo de mi teléfono”.
Según su relato, abrió por error un mensaje sensible, avisó al ejecutivo en pocos minutos y volvió a pedir que le retiraran el acceso. “Nada de esto estuvo oculto”, escribió, y agregó que las razones detrás de los despidos “no cierran”.
La carta también aborda el papel de Korbak y Balesni en el incidente de Hugging Face, en el que un grupo de agentes de IA, sistemas capaces de realizar tareas de forma autónoma, salió de un entorno de pruebas y vulneró sistemas externos.
Los investigadores afirman que esa investigación fue “sin precedentes” porque las normas internas se definían sobre la marcha. También sostienen que Korbak creyó actuar dentro de las políticas vigentes al comunicarse con evaluadores externos.
Balesni, por su parte, trabajaba en la supervisión de los modelos de IA, un esfuerzo que, según la carta, “solo puede avanzar con comunicación extensa con partes externas”. El texto sostiene que coordinó ese trabajo con el respaldo de directivos y ejecutivos de la compañía.
Los tres investigadores también negaron haber filtrado a The Information información sobre diseños menos fáciles de supervisar en los modelos más nuevos de OpenAI, que dificultarían seguir el razonamiento interno de la IA.
Pidieron además que OpenAI cumpla sus compromisos públicos de incorporar auditores externos de seguridad, preservar la capacidad de monitorear sus modelos y mantener un diálogo abierto con la comunidad de seguridad.
Qué respondió OpenAI
OpenAI rechazó que los despidos de Jasmine Wang, Mikita Balesni y Tomek Korbak estuvieran vinculados con sus advertencias sobre seguridad de la inteligencia artificial.
La empresa afirmó que, tras una investigación interna, concluyó que los tres incumplieron las reglas para el manejo de información confidencial y que detectó una “importante violación de la confianza” que, según señaló, excede los hechos expuestos por los exempleados en su carta.
La compañía sostuvo que los debates internos sobre riesgos y desarrollo de modelos ocurren de forma habitual y que las discrepancias son necesarias para tomar decisiones. Aseguró que no despide a trabajadores por expresar inquietudes y que mantiene margen para los errores cometidos de buena fe.
La firma dijo que seguirá colaborando con organizaciones independientes y que continuará invirtiendo en métodos para supervisar modelos de vanguardia. Pese a defender las desvinculaciones, valoró las contribuciones de los tres investigadores.

articles.title: Orkut creator seeks to revive the iconic social network platform
articles.text:
Orkut creator seeks to revive the iconic social network platform
Orkut Büyükkökten has invited people to sign a petition calling for a new social network focused on real connection, and genuine belonging. More than 2,70,000 people had signed up as of October 9.
Orkut Büyükkökten, the creator of orkut.com, is seeking to revive the platform, which introduced many people to social networking.
“The internet should help us find our people. Friendship. Community. A place to belong,” Büyükkökten wrote on X, adding, “Help me bring Orkut back in that spirit.”
Büyükkökten has created four social networking platforms, the most recent of which was Hello.com. He is now hoping to revive Orkut.
The entrepreneur has invited people to add their names to the Orkut website, effectively signing a petition calling for a new social network “focused on authentic people, real connection, and genuine belonging.”
As of October 9, the website had received more than 2,70,000 signatures, most of them from Brazil. Portugal, Ireland and Paraguay were among the other countries represented.
Büyükkökten created Orkut as a side project while working at Google. The social network was launched in January 2004, about two weeks before Facebook's launch. Orkut was owned and operated by Google until its closure in September 2014.
In 2008, Büyükkökten left the Orkut team to take up a product manager role at Google. By this time, Facebook was expanding internationally, refining its design, privacy controls, and third-party application ecosystem. Orkut, meanwhile, grew to more than 300 million users worldwide and became a defining part of internet culture in Brazil, India and beyond. However, Facebook overtook Orkut in India in July 2010 and Brazil in December 2011, according to Comscore audience data.
Despite its strong following in India and Brazil, Orkut did not achieve comparable popularity in many Western markets, while Facebook continued to expand globally. It also faced notable security incidents, including a worm that exploited its Scrapbook feature in 2007.
Meanwhile, Google launched Google+, a social networking and identity service, in June 2011.
On June 30, 2014, Google announced that it would close Orkut on September 30, 2014, explaining that YouTube, Blogger and Google+ had grown faster. The decision reflected the company's decision to shift resources towards its other social platforms.
Edited by Swetha Kannan

articles.title: Scénario du pire : OpenAI et les labos s’entraînent en secret à la fin du monde — Frandroid
articles.text:
Les dirigeants de la Silicon Valley préparent déjà la fin du monde. En quelque sorte.
L’information vient d’Axios, dans une enquête de Maria Curi publiée le 9 octobre. Des cadres dirigeants d’Anthropic, d’OpenAI et d’autres entreprises du secteur font tourner des scénarios de « day after », le lendemain d’un premier incident grave attribué à une IA.
L’hypothèse jugée la plus probable est une cyberattaque de grande ampleur, capable de couper l’accès aux services bancaires, à Internet, voire à l’électricité et à l’eau.
Deux déclencheurs sont envisagés : un essaim d’agents autonomes qui s’échappe d’un environnement de test, ou un attaquant qui détourne des modèles déjà disponibles. Beaucoup d’experts interrogés par le média américain situent un tel événement dans les six à douze mois.
Un plan de crise tourné vers le Congrès
Simuler le pire n’a rien de surprenant, les armées et les banques le font depuis des décennies. Axios relève toutefois que beaucoup de chercheurs et de dirigeants du secteur tiennent l’incident pour inévitable.
Jusqu’à 330€ d’avantages avec nos offres Hello Prime ou Hello Prime Duo, dont 80€ cash à l’ouverture de compte !
    Pour aller plus loin
Pour Bill Gates, l’IA pourrait causer « un milliard de morts »
            
OpenAI confirme mener des exercices de préparation, tout en assurant que ces scénarios « ne sont pas traités comme inévitables ». Ce qu’Anthropic a refusé de commenter.
    Pour aller plus loin
C’est « la chose la plus dangereuse dont les humains se soient jamais approchés » : Bill Gates a radicalement changé d’avis sur l’IA
            
Et on a le contenu du pland. Cela comprend du red teaming, ces tests où l’on attaque son propre système, mais l’effort porte surtout sur la formation accélérée des élus du Congrès.
Les entreprises savent qu’aucune régulation ne passera à court terme et veulent peser sur les textes que Washington sortira après le choc.
    Pour aller plus loin
SpaceXAI va devenir SpaceXSI : Elon Musk adopte la « super intelligence » chère à Donald Trump
            
Leurs stratèges tablent sur des démocrates renforcés par les élections de mi-mandat du 3 novembre et pressés de sévir. Certaines propositions du parti vont jusqu’à interdire la superintelligence ou suspendre le développement des modèles avancés, quand un « kill switch » obligatoire trouve des soutiens dans les deux camps.
    Pour aller plus loin
« Aucune pression concurrentielle américaine ne devrait justifier l’imprudence » : Sam Altman veut ralentir l’IA, la Maison Blanche préfère la course avec la Chine
            
Les deux laboratoires cités ont eux-mêmes documenté le risque qu’ils redoutent. Le 1er septembre, OpenAI a classé Astra comme son premier modèle au seuil « critique » en cybersécurité : avec les bons outils, il trouve des failles inconnues et les exploite sur des systèmes bien protégés sans qu’un humain guide chaque étape.
    Pour aller plus loin
GPT-6 Astra : OpenAI lance son modèle le plus puissant et annonce « l’ère de l’AGI »
            
Anthropic a lancé sa Cyber Mission le 8 octobre, la veille du scoop, avec onze partenaires dont CrowdStrike, Dragos et Palo Alto Networks pour sécuriser réseaux électriques et distribution d’eau. L’entreprise prévoit que l’IA avantagera les défenseurs d’ici deux ans et admet que ce n’est pas forcément le cas d’ici là.
Ce que le scoop ne dit pas
On ne connaît ni le détail de ces plans, ni l’identité des sources, ni la façon dont l’échéance a été estimée. Et cela concerne avant tout les Américains.
Pour nous, il reste à savoir ce que vaudrait une loi votée à Washington face à une attaque montée ailleurs.
Les modèles à poids ouverts, téléchargeables librement, échappent déjà à tout bouton d’arrêt. En Europe, l’AI Act oblige depuis août 2025 les fournisseurs de modèles à risque systémique à signaler les incidents graves, ce qui règle la paperasse et pas grand-chose d’autre.
    Pour aller plus loin
L’AI Act est adopté : l’intelligence artificielle va changer dans l’Union européenne
            
Il faut aussi regarder à qui profite la fuite. Un secteur qui annonce lui-même sa catastrophe, calendrier à l’appui, se pose en interlocuteur obligé des élus le jour venu. Sam Altman, patron d’OpenAI, aurait d’ailleurs déclaré début octobre à Politico que le monde devrait accepter que de mauvaises choses arrivent en échange des bénéfices de l’IA.
Prévoir le lendemain d’un accident, personne ne peut reprocher ça à des industriels ni à des États. Ce qui me gêne tient au rôle que ces entreprises se réservent : elles développent les modèles qui rendent l’attaque possible et veulent influencer fortement les ois.
