articles.title: Apple's touchscreen MacBook could arrive later this month
articles.text:
What we know so far: The event that Apple just announced for next week might be only the first of two this month. While the company is expected to unveil its HomeKit refresh on October 13, another event just two weeks later might introduce a new iPad and multiple Mac devices.
Sources have told Bloomberg's Mark Gurman that Apple is planning an event near the end of October to mark what would be its fourth hardware launch of the fall. The star would be the long-rumored touchscreen-equipped MacBook, but other devices are also expected to appear.
Apple has long resisted the laptop touchscreen trend, but rumors of a touchscreen MacBook have circulated for some time. Earlier this year, observers claimed the device's launch was almost guaranteed after testers discovered full touchscreen support in a macOS 27 preview build.
Earlier macOS versions only supported the Apple Pencil and a few touch gestures, so expanding touch support suggests touchscreen Mac devices are on the horizon. Furthermore, giving the iPad a more macOS-like interface likely laid the groundwork for a full-blown touch-enabled macOS interface.
Other hardware details about the new MacBook remain scarce, but it might introduce a new "Ultra" tier to the product line. However, rumors said the same thing about the iPhone Duo before Apple chose its unique name, so nothing is certain. MacBook users also shouldn't hold their breath for a MacBook 2-in-1, as Apple is still expected to keep the lineup separate from iPads.
Speaking of iPads, the October 27 event might also introduce an upgraded iPad mini with an OLED panel. The device would mark the start of a broad iPad overhaul, with updates to the standard iPad, OLED iPad Air, and iPad Pro expected early next year. A budget-priced iPad for kids is also rumored. Additionally, the late-October presentation could introduce M6 updates for the iMac and the 14-inch MacBook Pro.
 – Greg Joswiak (@gregjoz) October 8, 2026
Apple has already announced one hardware launch presentation for this month, scheduled for October 13. The home-themed messaging in the company's announcement supports prior rumors that a HomeKit relaunch is on the horizon.
To compete with the Amazon Echo Show and Google Nest, Apple is expected to unveil an iPad-like stationary display that incorporates some HomePod features to manage Bluetooth speakers and other smart home devices. These might include a refreshed HomePod, a new HomePod mini, and eventually smart locks, cameras, and thermostats from LG.

articles.title: CircleCI Makes Machine Runner Orchestrator Generally Available
articles.text:
CircleCI has made its Machine Runner Orchestrator 1.0.0 generally available, providing automated scaling of self-hosted machine runner virtual machines according to CI workload demand. The release expands the earlier Runner Provisioner preview with support for CPU, GPU, and ARM workloads from a single deployment, as well as Kubernetes environments running on GKE, AKS, and EKS, alongside KubeVirt-based clusters.
The release is aimed at a common challenge with self-hosted CI infrastructure: maintaining enough runner capacity for bursts of build and test activity without permanently provisioning machines for peak demand. The orchestrator monitors CircleCI workload requirements and provisions and removes machine runners accordingly, allowing organisations to retain control over the underlying compute environment while making runner capacity more dynamic. CircleCI says the capability is included with self-hosted runners across its plans at no additional cost.
Earlier versions were focused on provisioning machine runners, but the new orchestrator can manage several resource classes from a single deployment. That matters in environments where CI workloads are no longer homogeneous: conventional CPU builds can coexist with GPU-intensive workloads and ARM-based builds without requiring separate orchestration installations for each class.
The underlying architecture also reflects the increasing use of Kubernetes as the control plane for CI infrastructure. Rather than requiring a particular Kubernetes distribution, Machine Runner Orchestrator now supports the three major managed Kubernetes platforms - Google Kubernetes Engine, Azure Kubernetes Service, and Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service - as well as KubeVirt environments. This gives platform teams more flexibility over where the orchestration layer runs while the actual CI runners remain machine-based
Machine Runner Orchestrator occupies a different layer from Kubernetes node autoscalers such as Karpenter and Cluster Autoscaler. Kubernetes node autoscaling primarily responds to unschedulable Pods and adjusts the underlying cluster capacity. Karpenter, for example, provisions nodes based on pending workloads and can also consolidate or otherwise manage node lifecycle.
CircleCI's orchestrator instead operates at the CI runner layer. Its purpose is to ensure that the machines registered as CircleCI runners scale with the demand for CI jobs. In a Kubernetes-based architecture, the two approaches can therefore potentially operate together: Kubernetes manages the infrastructure hosting the orchestration components, while CircleCI manages the machine capacity available to execute CI workloads.
CircleCI is not alone in moving self-hosted CI execution toward Kubernetes-native autoscaling. GitHub's Actions Runner Controller (ARC) provides a Kubernetes operator for orchestrating and scaling self-hosted GitHub Actions runners. Its runner scale sets can automatically increase or decrease runner capacity based on workflow demand, creating and removing ephemeral runners as jobs are processed.
The difference is largely in the execution model. GitHub ARC primarily creates ephemeral runner environments as Kubernetes-managed workloads, whereas CircleCI's Machine Runner Orchestrator is specifically concerned with machine runner virtual machines. This makes CircleCI's approach particularly relevant for CI workloads that require VM-level isolation or capabilities that are hard to reproduce in standard runner containers, while still using Kubernetes as the orchestration control plane.
The transition to 1.0 is not completely transparent for existing preview users. CircleCI has formally renamed the product from runner-provisioner to machine-runner-orchestrator, changing the associated Helm chart, container image repository, and Packagecloud repository. Existing installations cannot simply be upgraded in place: CircleCI instructs users to uninstall the previous deployment and install the new 1.0.0 package.
That creates a short operational gap during migration. CircleCI warns that runners associated with the configured resource classes will be offline between removal of the old deployment and installation of the new one. Organisations therefore need to account for this when upgrading production CI infrastructure rather than treating the release as a conventional in-place software update.
Version 1.0.0 also addresses two high-severity vulnerabilities in the Go gRPC implementation. The fixes cover CVE-2026-84304, involving heap memory exhaustion through HTTP/2 frame fragmentation, and CVE-2026-84445, which could cause a crash when requests were missing the :authority or Host header.
The 1.0 release moves CircleCI further toward the model of combining multiple resource classes with Kubernetes-based orchestration and support for major managed Kubernetes platforms. For platform engineering teams, the interesting shift is therefore not simply another runner feature, but the emergence of CI execution capacity as an independently scalable infrastructure layer; one that can respond to software delivery demand in much the same way that modern platforms already scale application workloads

articles.title: Monte Carlo Capital raises €13 million for Fund II to invest in early-stage DeepTech, AI and SpaceTech | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Monte Carlo Capital (MCC), the Monaco-based early-stage venture firm investing at Seed in DeepTech and tech-enabled innovators, today announced a €13 million ($15 million) first close of Fund II, with a target of €26 million ($30 million).
This comes after the close of Fund I at over €11 million in 2025 – as reported by EU-Startups. Most Fund I LPs have recommitted, and Fund II has already made five investments.
“Reaching a $15 million first close on Fund II is a strong vote of confidence from our investors, and we have already put that capital to work in five companies. Our approach hasn’t changed: get onto outstanding cap tables early, invest alongside the world’s leading VCs, and keep backing our best companies as they scale through our SPVs. We only invest where we see a credible path to a multi-billion-dollar outcome,” says Ian Sosso, founder and Managing Partner, Monte Carlo Capital.
Monte Carlo Capital’s Fund II first close comes amid continued fundraising activity among European venture capital firms targeting DeepTech, AI and other emerging technologies in 2026.
Recent EU-Startups coverage includes Munich-based Vanagon Ventures’ €20 million fund for pre-Seed DeepTech and AI startups, London-based Project Ventures’ €5.8 million vehicle targeting university-linked ventures, and Ruya Ventures’ €43 million DeepTech fund.
Larger vehicles include Paris-based 360 Capital’s €85 million Poli360 2 fund, Berlin-based Merantix Capital’s €103 million AI fund, London-based Transition Ventures’ €128 million Fund II and French VC Elaia’s €134 million DeepTech Seed fund.
Together, these announcements represent approximately €519 million in disclosed fund capital, rising to €532 million when including MCC’s latest first close.
Founded in 2009 by Ian Sosso, MCC combines a lean fund with co-investment SPVs. Before launching MCC’s funds, Ian built a track record as an angel investor, leading over 50 syndicates and acting as lead investor up to Series B.
He is a board member of the European Business Angels Network (EBAN), which named him Best European Early-Stage Investor in 2019.
Today’s announcement comes 3 years after MCC’s launch of its first fund in 2023. Fund II invests primarily at Seed, and selectively at pre-Seed and Series A, with a focus on sectors such as DeepTech, AI, SpaceTech, and enterprise software.
Current portfolio companies include:
- StarCloud – Fastest YC company ever to reach unicorn status. Now valued at €2 billion ($2.3 billion).
- Scout AI – Reportedly, the largest DefenceTech Series A in US history, at €357 million ($400 million).

articles.title: AI disqualification yields new Nikon Small World in Motion winner
articles.text:
Last month we covered the winner of Nikon’s Small World in Motion video: Ning Xu of Tsinghua University in China, whose video captured tiny cilia beating in the airways of a child with a rare respiratory disorder. But allegations surfaced about Xu’s use of AI while making the video. Nikon launched an investigation and concluded that Xu’s entry did not comply with competition rules. The new winner is Nguyen Nam Nhat of Vietnam with a video of a tiny roundworm and a single-celled organism (above).
According to a BBC report, some researchers expressed concern that Xu’s video had structural abnormalities and that cell features appeared and disappeared in a way one would not see in actual cellular biology. Others spotted what looked like AI watermarks embedded within the source files. Xu said he used AI “to distinguish and visualize features in the reconstructed grayscale images”; however, he denied that AI was used “to generate the experimental movie, the cilia, or their motion.”
Founded in 2011, the Nikon Small World in Motion competition is a spinoff of the company’s Small World Photomicrography Competition, which has been around since 1974. Both are meant “to showcase the beauty and complexity of things seen through the light microscope”—one through still photographs, the other through photovideography, taking advantage of all the technological advances that now allow users to make movies or time-lapse images through the microscope.
The other winners also moved up a notch with Xu’s disqualification. Benedikt Pleyer of Bavaria, Germany, placed second with a video of jellyfish larvae suspended in water droplets; Andrew Moore of Howard Hughes Medical Institute in the US placed third with a video of synchronized cell division in neighboring cells; Patrick Hickey of Hypha Research Ltd. in Edinburgh, Scotland, placed fourth with a video of the dynamics of mitochondria and chloroplasts in Turtle Vine leaf cells; and Igor Adameyko placed fifth with a video of a tiny, colorful sea slug (Cyerce kikutarobabai) on the move.

articles.title: Así funciona ViVeTool, la herramienta gratuita que permite activar funciones ocultas de Windows
articles.text:
Qué tiempos aquellos en los que para encontrar nuevas características en Windows tenías que esperar a que Microsoft lanzase una nueva versión. Y, para ello, debías esperar varios años. Pero con Windows 10, todo esto cambió. Desde entonces, cada actualización de Windows 11 es una caja de sorpresas en la que puedes encontrar nuevas funciones, apps que aparecen y otras que desaparecen. Y algún que otro bug y error de funcionamiento. El caso es que esas novedades no siempre son malas. A veces mejoran Windows. Pero como no siempre vienen activadas desde el primer día, surgen soluciones como ViVeTool, una app para curiosos e impacientes.
Antes de Windows 10, las actualizaciones servían para corregir problemas del sistema, mejorar la seguridad y poco más. Y de vez en cuando se lanzaba una actualización mayor que recopilaba todos esos parches y, en ocasiones los acompañaban de alguna mejora o novedad. Pero, en la actualidad, Windows 11 recibe constantes cambios que afectan a la interfaz, las aplicaciones oficiales y, en definitiva, cualquier aspecto que Microsoft cree conveniente cambiar a media partida. Te guste o no. Y no siempre la cosa sale bien.
Sin embargo, los cambios constantes no siempre son malos. Sirva de ejemplo la enésima actualización de Windows 11, que activa cambios que se incorporaron en actualizaciones anteriores y que todavía no estaban activos. Algunos de estos cambios ya los vimos, como maximizar las apps, el menú de Inicio rediseñado, una función oculta de búsqueda o mejoras de rendimiento. Y si quieres ser de los primeros en disfrutar estas novedades, te interesará conocer ViVeTool.
Qué es ViVeTool y para qué sirve
ViVeTool es una aplicación gratuita y de código abierto que sirve para activar, desactivar o consultar funciones internas que Microsoft ha incluido en el sistema a través de actualizaciones, pero que todavía no ha habilitado para todos los usuarios. El motivo es que prefiere que un grupo limitado de personas prueben esos cambios antes de activarlos para todo el mundo. Normalmente, desarrolladores, expertos o entusiastas que están suscritos al programa Windows Insider de Microsoft. Pero esto no te impide activarlos tú mismo. Aunque si lo haces, es por tu cuenta y riesgo.
Uno de los inconvenientes de esta herramienta es que funciona desde la línea de comandos. Pero esto no debería ser un problema ya que la aplicación es muy fácil de utilizar. La propia app te muestra una lista de comandos disponibles y apenas necesitarás dos o tres para saber qué parches están disponibles y activarlos. O desactivarlos si no te terminan de gustar o te dan problemas en vez de soluciones. Es otra de sus ventajas.
Por lo demás, ViveTool es compatible con Windows 10 (build 18963 o posterior) y Windows 11 (incluyendo 24H2 y 25H2), aunque por razones obvias, Windows 11 es el sistema que más actualizaciones con cambios recibe actualmente. Y funciona en ordenadores Intel o AMD (x86/x64) y en ARM64. También hay que dejar claro que no es una herramienta oficial de Microsoft, como sí ocurre con PowerToys. Y si quieres descargar e instalar ViveTool, puedes hacerlo desde su repositorio de GitHub.
Otro detalle a tener en cuenta de esta herramienta es que dependerá de la versión de Windows que tengas instalada que puedas activar o desactivar las funciones ocultas. Así que conviene mantener actualizado Windows, si es posible, para tener más oportunidades de que esas novedades estén ya instaladas aunque no visibles.
Cómo usar ViVeTool y sus comandos
Como suele ser habitual, antes de utilizar ViveTool necesitarás descargarlo en tu ordenador. En su página oficial encontrarás la versión Intel y la versión ARM. Van por separado. Una vez descargado el archivo correspondiente a tu computadora, ábrelo desde el Explorador de archivos de Windows y extrae el contenido a una carpeta cualquiera.
Para abrir ViVeTool deberás abrir primero la línea de comandos en modo administrador. Esto puedes hacerlo de varias maneras. En el buscador de Windows encontrarás Símbolo del sistema o Windows PowerShell. Desde el menú de resultados, te aparecerá la opción Ejecutar como administrador cuando selecciones una de las dos aplicaciones.
Y ya está. Con la línea de comandos en modo administrador, ve a la ruta en la que está ViVeTool. Y, una ve dentro, ejecuta el comando vivetool. Aparecerá una lista de comandos disponibles. Por ejemplo, con vivetool /query verás los cambios y funciones de Windows disponibles. Algunos ya estarán activados (enabled), pero otros no (disabled). Y con vivetool /appupdate puedes comprobar si hay actualizaciones para la app ViVeTool.
Otro inconveniente de ViVeTool es que te muestra los códigos de las funciones ocultas de Windows pero no te explica para qué sirven. Para obtener la respuesta, tendrás que buscar en Internet. Y, una vez sepas si ese cambio te convence, para activarlo deberás ejecutar el comando vivetool /enable /id:12345678 donde “12345678” es el código del cambio. Por ejemplo, con el código 61754985 se activan las nuevas opciones para personalizar el menú de Inicio de Windows 11. Y si no te convence esa novedad, puedes desactivarla con el comando vivetool /disable /id:12345678 donde “12345678” es el código del cambio.
Y, para terminar, conviene recordar que herramientas como ViVeTool deben manejarse con precaución. Es decir, puede que al activar alguna función oculta de Windows, esa función no esté del todo madura, por lo que te puedes encontrar con errores de funcionamiento o inestabilidad en las aplicaciones. Si es así, desactiva la función para volver a la normalidad.

articles.title: Rockstar revela dos nuevas canciones de GTA 6: Cardi B y Fuerza Regida se unen a la banda sonora del juego
articles.text:
El videojuego Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6) tendrá una banda sonora de 34 canciones, algunas originales. Ya se conocían temas de Travis Scott, Rauw Alejandro y CA7RIEL & Paco Amoroso. Rockstar reveló dos nuevas canciones.
Se trata de Suzuki, de Fuerza Regida, y Don’t Chart, de Cardi B. Ambas canciones ya están disponibles en plataformas de música como Spotify.
Suzuki sigue el género regional mexicano, con influencias de corridos tumbados, música sierreña y sonidos urbanos de raíces tradicionales.
Por su parte, Don’t Chart mantiene el estilo característico de Cardi B: rap, una base minimalista y letras desafiantes.
A pesar de que el juego no contará con su propio CD físico, la banda sonora, sí, además de una versión vinilo.

Bad Bunny se une a las estaciones de radio de GTA 6
Rockstar Games presentó las primeras seis estaciones de radio de Grand Theft Auto VI y confirmó una novedad que modificará la experiencia sonora de la saga: los jugadores podrán escuchar radio y pódcast bajo demanda fuera de los vehículos.
Jason y Lucía usarán auriculares conectados a sus teléfonos móviles para acceder a esos contenidos mientras recorren Leonida a pie, sin perder la opción tradicional de oírlos dentro de los automóviles.
El juego, cuyo lanzamiento está previsto para el 19 de noviembre de 2026 en PlayStation 5 y Xbox Series, contará con una oferta musical más amplia que las entregas anteriores.
Las emisoras anunciadas son Flash FM, Cocoteo FM, Back Country Radio, AfroBank FM, The Chamber 106.6 y Dirty South Classics. Sus programaciones abarcarán pop, música latina, country alternativo, música afro, metal, rap y hip-hop regional.
Flash FM incluirá canciones de Charli xcx, MGMT y Zara Larsson junto a PinkPantheress. Cocoteo FM reunirá música de Bad Bunny, Axel Rulay con Farruko y El Alfa, y Romeo Santos con El Chaval de la Bachata.
CD y vinilo de la banda sonora original de GTA 6
Rockstar Games anunció Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album, una banda sonora oficial de 34 canciones inéditas que se publicará el 20 de noviembre de 2026, un día después del lanzamiento de GTA 6.
El proyecto, realizado junto a Atlantic Records, incluye a artistas como Travis Scott, Keith Richards, Rauw Alejandro y CA7RIEL & Paco Amoroso. Aunque el videojuego no tendrá edición física, el álbum se venderá de forma independiente en CD y vinilo.
Rockstar ya lanzó varios sencillos en plataformas digitales y habilitó preventas en tres versiones. Además, anticipó novedades sobre una banda sonora interactiva y la evolución del sistema de radio del juego.

articles.title: Amazon and others are done keeping data center deals secret. Is it enough to build trust? | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Amazon says it will stop using NDAs when negotiating data center deals with local governments, following a similar move from Microsoft earlier this year. Secrecy has fueled community backlash against AI infrastructure, with opposition leading to hundreds of proposed and enacted moratoriums from New York to San Francisco. Meanwhile, a wave of startups is betting that consumers will hand AI agents access to their inboxes, files, and credit cards — if they can get websites to let them in.
On this episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast, Anthony Ha, Sean O’Kane, and Rebecca Bellan dig into whether ditching NDAs will change how data center deals get done, why trust may be the real product for personal AI startups, plus a couple of deals of the week.
Subscribe to Equity on YouTube, Apple Podcasts, Overcast, Spotify and all the casts. You can also follow Equity on X and Threads, at @EquityPod.

articles.title: Mistral’s new Large 4 trails some Chinese open models in independent tests
articles.text:
Independent tests rank Mistral’s new trillion-parameter Large 4 the best AI model outside the U.S. and China — but Chinese open-weights still overcome Europe's best efforts
Its best result is a cyber test, but it falls behind on the index.
Mistral launched its trillion-parameter Large 4 (ML4) model this week, saying it “pushes the frontier of open-weight performance.” Artificial Analysis (AA), an independent AI benchmarking firm, ranked Mistral's Large 4 as the best model available from outside the U.S. and China in its index. The mixture-of-experts model, trained on Nvidia’s Grace Blackwell GPUs, scored its personal best in AA’s CyberGym-E2E-AA end-to-end cybersecurity measure, although several Chinese open models beat it overall.
ML4 scored 38 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.3.2, which AA says makes it the “most intelligent model from outside the US and China." At least five Chinese open models scored higher on the index: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (max) at 39, GLM-5.3-Flash at 42, Kimi K3 (max) at 44, GLM-5.3 (max) at 45, and MiMo-V2.6-Pro at 46. While MiMo-V2.6-Pro is comparable in total size to ML4, GLM-5.3-Flash is about one-third the size at 320B parameters total and 18B versus ML4’s 49B–52B active. Unlike the rest, ML4 isn’t open yet: Mistral says its weights are due “by the end of the month.”
| Mistral Large 4 vs. Chinese open models on Artificial Analysis' Intelligence Index (Oct. 6) |  |  |  |  | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Model | Index score | Parameters, total / active | Cost per index task | Weights | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Xiaomi MiMo-V2.6-Pro | 46 | 1.0T / 42B | $0.13 | Open | 
| Z.ai GLM-5.3 (max) | 45 | 753B / 40B | $2.01 | Open | 
| Moonshot Kimi K3 (max) | 44 | 2.8T / 104B | $2.00 | Open | 
| Z.ai GLM-5.3-Flash | 42 | 320B / 18B | $0.25 | Open | 
| DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (max) | 39 | 552B / 16B | $0.27 | Open | 
| Mistral Large 4 Preview | 38 | 1.05T / 49B–52B | $1.13 ($0.57 at launch pricing) | Due by end of October | 
| DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813 (max) | 36 | 1.6T / 49B | $0.67 | Open | 
Cost is a different story. ML4 comes in at $1.13 per AA task at list price, or $0.57 at the 50% discounted launch price. This compares to $0.13 for MiMo-V2.6-Pro and $0.25 for GLM-5.3-Flash. Although comparatively expensive, ML4 scored what AA calls its “strongest result” and Mistral calls “the highest of any model” with an 81.7% score on CyberGym-E2E-AA, compared with GLM-5.3-Flash’s 74%, from a model whose post-training run Mistral claims is “still in flight.”
While the score is impressive, it is only one of three tests in the Cyber Index; ML4 only scores 16% in DeepsecBench-AA and 51% in CWE-Bench-AA. However, AA’s projection is that, once the weights ship, it “will rank among the top three open weights models on the Cyber Index.” This leaves the door open for ML4 to apply to narrower tasks.
| Mistral Large 4 on Artificial Analysis' Cyber Index and its three tests (Oct. 6) |  |  |  |  | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Model | Cyber Index | CWE-Bench-AA | DeepsecBench-AA | CyberGym-E2E-AA | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Grok 4.7 (xhigh) | 56 | 68% | 27% | 74% | 
| Xiaomi MiMo-V2.6-Pro | 56 | 63% | 26% | 79% | 
| OpenAI GPT-6 Luna (max) | 53 | 57% | 24% | 78% | 
| Z.ai GLM-5.3-Flash | 50 | 56% | 20% | 74% | 
| Mistral Large 4 Preview | 50 | 51% | 16% | 82% | 
| OpenAI GPT-6 Astra (max; declined some tasks) | 33 | 63% | 37% | 0% | 
| Anthropic Claude Opus 5.5 (max with fallback; declined some tasks) | 29 | 58% | 27% | 1% | 
Mistral bets on this, saying ML4 is “state-of-the-art among open models” on enterprise workloads such as “cybersecurity, finance and law,” and that in visual grounding, where its 1.6B-parameter vision encoder comes in, it can go as far as “surpassing even frontier closed models.” On AA’s Cyber Index, Mistral says, ML4 ranks “among the top five models globally,” and it solves 93% of Cybench, a set of 40 challenges drawn from security competitions.
CEO Arthur Mensch went further in Abu Dhabi, saying the model is “above the Chinese models on certain aspects, including cyber,” Reuters reported. Mistral’s other figures include DeepSWE v1.1 at 61.7%, Coding Agent Index at 49.8%, AutomationBench at 59.9%, and Dense 200 at 42%; AA’s own chart puts ML4 at 27% on Terminal-Bench 4.0.
ML4 does, in fact, beat OpenAI’s closed GPT-6 Luna (max) on CyberGym-E2E-AA, but Luna matches ML4’s 38 on AA’s index at about one-sixteenth of the cost per task ($0.07). Mistral says frontier models such as Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra “score near zero on the same test because they refuse to perform the task,” and AA’s chart marks both as declining some tasks on safety grounds.
Outside of that test, Mistral says ML4 also beats DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813 and Qwen3.8 Max on the Coding Agent Index; per AA, it is cheaper than the latter. Overall, AA’s index-vs.-cost chart puts ML4 below the Pareto line and just outside the “Most attractive quadrant.”
The cost comes from needing 200 million output tokens to run AA’s index, against a median of 81 million. As for speed, ML4 generated 116.1 tokens per second, with 1.46 seconds to the first token. This puts ML4 at about 33% faster than its tier median and 2.6x faster to the first token. AA’s speed is measured on Mistral’s own API, which Mistral says runs on the same hardware the model used for training.
ML4 was “trained from scratch on 3,800 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs in Mistral’s own datacenters in Europe,” the company said. This is up from 3,000 Nvidia H200s used to train Large 3, released last year, which was smaller at 675B total parameters with 41B active. The training occurred over “roughly two months,” as reported by VentureBeat.
Mistral raised a €3 billion Series D in what the company calls “the largest equity round ever raised by a European technology company” in its post. Mistral Compute has planned for 18,000 Grace Blackwell chips, as announced with Nvidia last year. Mistral says it is “significantly scaling up our compute capacity in our own European datacenters,” and that ML4 will become the base for “a new generation of specialized and optimized Mistral models.” The model’s open weights, once released, will be able to run on a private cloud or on-premises.
The weights, architecture details, and additional benchmarks are expected before the end of October. Artificial Analysis lists the preview as proprietary until the weights arrive. Once it does, the model may be re-scored, and Mistral’s claims will be held to task. For the first two weeks following release, ML4 can be used via API at a discounted rate.
While European models still have a lot to prove, based on previous performance and ML4’s showing with an 8-point gap versus a similar-size Chinese model that’s also a lot less expensive, Mistral has demonstrated resolve and produced a model with, at least, niche application, as the basis to eventually close that gap.
Shane Downing is a Contributing Writer for Tom’s Hardware, covering consumer storage, PC hardware, and AI.

articles.title: How to keep AI agents within their permissions
articles.text:
Written by: Ido Shlomo Co-Founder and CTO of Token Security
AI agents should do more on their own. Who has the time or attention span to approve every command? And watching agents do the work they’re asked to do is mind-numbingly boring.
But agents do need boundaries, especially in corporate environments. Without a clear limit on what they can do, agentic flows tend to use all available access.
Here's a real-world example: A developer asks their agent to figure out why a nightly export job is failing. The team's rule for agents is simple: they work through read-only roles. But the developer also holds admin for on-call work, and both profiles sit in the same ~/.aws/config.
The agent hits AccessDenied when it tries to rerun the job, so it switches to the admin profile, assumes the role, and runs aws s3 rm against the production bucket to clear out the half-written export first.
The credential is valid. The developer may assume admin privileges, and the admin can delete S3 objects. AWS checks the signature, not who is holding the key, so as far as AWS knows, the developer did this. The violation is that an agent used a role that agents aren't allowed to use. Unlike intent, you can check that on every request.
Who’s to blame? The developer who shouldn’t have handed the agent their credentials and let it auto-approve actions? The harness maker? That’s the wrong question. Again, agents should do more on their own, speaking both as a developer and as a manager of developers who work with AI.
Instead of assigning blame, we need to know where this deletion attempt can actually be stopped. There are several possible enforcement points, and each depends on what the control can see, what it can block, and whether the agent has another path to the same action.
We want autonomy with limits we can actually enforce
First, we need to scope the problem. There’s constant pressure to expand agentic access, and usually, the reason makes sense in isolation. A task gets stuck, for example. Or there’s a new integration for a service that holds some of the organizational context.
The result is always the same: the next task starts with more access than the previous one.
A second source of pressure is the agent itself. Agents look for new credentials when the ones they have are blocked, without asking the human in charge whether they can have that access.
This behavior is agnostic to the source of the instructions. A malicious prompt injection can cause overreach attempts, but so can mistaken assumptions during an authorized task.
Valid Key, Wrong Hands
AWS checks the signature, not who holds the key. When an agent grabs an admin profile, the request appears to come from the developer.
Token Security maps every agent to its owner, identities, and permissions, so your controls block actions outside the assigned task and allow the rest to run.
See where it stops
Be specific about what you are enforcing
Agents use tool calls to retrieve data or take action, so that’s where the enforcement matters most. That said, "control tool calls" is a very coarse rule. What if the tool is a shell that can run an SDK? It can also be a browser with an authenticated session. When you allow the tool, you also allow what’s behind it.
To properly understand what’s happening, we need the operation, its arguments, the account and resource accessed, and the identity in use. For data operations, we also need to understand what the output is and where this output is routed.
There’s a lot that goes into a proper decision about the validity of an action.
In most agent harnesses, local commands, file operations, skills, and delegation are also tool calls. They matter because of where they lead. For example, reading ~/.aws/config is how the agent finds an admin profile to use.
So enforcement at the tool call is critical, and so is deciding on the action inside it.
Where enforcement can happen
Some of the damage can be prevented through reasoning checks that assess a plan or action against the task at hand. But this is a probabilistic control, and some malicious instructions will pass through. There’s no good alternative to having proper mitigation controls that can stop an action.
| Method | What it’s useful for | What I would check before relying on it | Risk it removes | Autonomy cost | 
| Managed agent settings | Restricting tools, permissions, approval modes, and allowed integrations close to the agent. | Which clients honor the settings? Can a user, project, or agent override them? Model and effort settings can attempt to restrict access, but they’re behavioral choices by nature. | Broad when the app enforces it; little for behavioral settings | Low, except approval modes, which cost the most | 
| Runtime hooks | Checking a supported operation before it runs, with context from the agent's session. | Can the user or agent change or disable it? Does it cover alternate tools and subagents? Does it block before execution, including on errors and timeouts? | Per operation, for the events it sees | Low if automated, high if it asks a person | 
| Gateways | Inspecting and blocking the requests routed through them, with a shared policy across connected agents. | Which traffic do they actually see: model requests, MCP tools, direct APIs, or network traffic? Can the agent reach the same system another way? | High for routed traffic, none for the rest | Low, since only the blocked call stops | 
| Sandboxes | Limiting the files, processes, network routes, and credentials available to an agent. | What can the agent still do inside those limits? Are reachable services restricted to the right account and operations, or just an allowed domain? | Caps reach, not what happens inside | Medium, as tasks needing outside access break | 
| Endpoint enforcement | Governing local agent use through endpoint software or the EDR that’s already deployed. | Can it stop a particular operation, or only a process or host? What is visible inside containers or VMs? Which hosted agents sit outside its reach? | Local agents only | High if it kills a process or host | 
| Credential and target-service authorization | Reducing the authority granted to an agent and enforcing access at the system that holds the resource. | Are credentials specific to the agent and task? Are there alternate credentials? Can the service distinguish the agent from the person or shared account behind it? | High, wherever the request comes from | Medium, as narrow access stalls tasks and sends agents looking for more | 
| API-based management | Changing agent settings, removing permissions, revoking credentials or sessions, and disabling access where platforms expose those actions. | When does the change take effect? What happens to existing sessions and cached tokens? Is it the prevention of future access or a response after the action? | Mostly after the action | None until it fires | 
These methods overlap and complement each other. A hook that calls a policy service and a gateway that consults an identity graph do a better job because the enforcement and decision points are in the locations best suited to them.
This table is far from exhaustive, and there are more considerations for some of these methods. Take managed settings, for example. Model and effort settings are behavioral in nature, but with some harnesses, permissions are much more than a prompt saying “please don’t flip out”.
In Claude Code, for example, permission rules are enforced by the application itself, and managed settings can restrict user overrides. In that case, control lives in a settings file, but that doesn’t make it less effective.
With hooks, the basic premise depends entirely on their placement in the execution chain. You can’t stop an event that’s already happened, and failure behavior varies by hook types and events.
Gateways have their own complexities, as they must base their authorization decisions on what they see. Look at AWS AgentCore, which demonstrates policy checks for connected tools. Note which calls it sees.
Sandboxes and scoped credentials solve different problems. Proper isolation can remove access capabilities, whereas a scoped credential limits what happens after access is granted. See Cloudflare's sandbox authentication design, which shows a way to add credentials outside the sandbox, so the agent doesn't need to possess the secret. Its operations, though, will still require authorization.
Apply the same policy to a hosted agent
Consider a support agent that’s asked to summarize open cases. Its connector uses a service account built for agents that edit and close cases. The agent decides that some cases look resolved and tries to close them.
Again, the capability comes with the credential, and the agent is within its grant. The place where the action is disallowed is the agent’s approved read-only policy.
To enforce it, the policy must be something a control can check, such as: “This agent may read cases, and any call that edits or closes one is denied, regardless of the service account it holds.”
If that agent lives in a hosted environment, an endpoint control on the employee’s laptop might have no opportunity to stop the action, since it’s all server-side.
Here, you’ll need cooperation from the SaaS platform’s own controls, rely on a tool gateway, or have a narrower service identity. And again, it depends on what the platform exposes and where the calls run.
Which brings us to coverage gaps in our controls. There’s no one perfect control here. Hooks aren’t better than endpoint enforcement, which isn’t better than a sandbox. It’s all about what you deploy and where.
| Method | Coding agent on a laptop | Support agent in a SaaS platform | 
| Managed agent settings | Works if the client honors them | Only what the vendor exposes | 
| Runtime hooks | On the events the runtime exposes | Only if the platform offers hooks | 
| Sandboxes | Limit files, network, and credentials | The agent runs on the vendor's servers | 
| Endpoint enforcement | In reach | Out of reach | 
| Gateways | Catch the admin calls, if AWS traffic routes through them | A tool gateway in front of the connector | 
| Credential and target-service authorization | Keep admin out of the agent's reach | A read-only service account for summaries | 
| API-based management | Revoke the session after the fact | Disable the connector after the fact | 
Two methods can stop both of these examples before the action reaches the target: a gateway that sees the relevant traffic and credential scoping at the target. The other methods depend more heavily on where the agent runs and what the runtime exposes.
Above all, you want the agent to keep working within its approved policy. Read-only is not complete. It can still expose sensitive data, depending on where the output goes. Anthropic's containment analysis explains why.
Choose what’s practical, then test the ways around your control
You’ll likely be deciding what’s practical based on your deployment. Managed settings require supported clients and central administration, for example. And you won’t have hooks without a runtime that exposes the right events. Gateways force you to route traffic through them, and endpoint controls mandate software installation and maintenance.
None of these is free. The controls introduce trade-offs, require maintenance, and must account for an ever-growing volume of AI-driven work.
Take the AWS example from the beginning of the article. Blocking the literal command is a start, but what if the same request comes through an SDK? With a different credential? Through delegation?
The security requirement to block deletion remains the same, but there are many different paths to it.
Then there’s the question of value, and you have to consider it as much as the control capabilities. How much delay do the controls add? How often does someone need to unblock a false positive? Are we reducing risk or introducing problems?
SACR's ARISE report centers on runtime intervention, delegated authority, and action-level decisions. This should be brought down to a concrete request, a policy, and evidence of what happened when the agent tried it.
A short guide, based on where your agents run and what you control there:
| Where your agents run | What you usually control | Start with | Then add | 
| Developer laptops and IDEs | The endpoint, agent settings, local credential files | Managed settings, plus hooks where the client supports them | A gateway for cloud API traffic, and endpoint enforcement for clients you can't configure | 
| Your own cloud, CI or containers | The runtime, network egress, and workload identity | A sandbox and per-agent workload credentials | A gateway on egress | 
| SaaS platforms | Connector credentials and the platform's admin settings | A narrow service identity per agent | Platform controls through the API, and a tool gateway in front of connectors, where the platform allows it | 
It probably isn’t one or the other. Instead, most organizations have all of the above, mixed together, with controls spread around different teams as well. Across these environments, the one common denominator is identity. So start with credential scoping at the target, as this dictates the reach wherever the agent is running. Then, add one policy source that every enforcement point reads from.
Do this, and you’re in a good starting position.
Where Token fits
At Token Security, we are building around the identity intelligence graph and the decisions it can support across the different enforcement points. Our current focus spans agent settings, gateways, endpoint enforcement, and APIs into identity and agent platforms.
The broader vision is to build or connect to the enforcement capability the customer needs. We don't need to build everything ourselves.
The graph connects an agent to its owner, the identities it consumes, the permissions associated with those identities, and the resources it can access. That’s the kind of context that policy engines can use to decide what an agent may do, rather than assuming that the credential's full authority is appropriate.
In a recent gateway demo, we demonstrated this exact idea: same developer, same session, and the agent’s call is denied on admin and allowed on readonly. Other controls can enforce read-only access, too.
Supplying the right identity context and applying the policy across the different places agents work is paramount, yet complex, as this process requires reliable attribution. If we cannot distinguish the agent's request from a human using the same credentials, the graph doesn't magically fix it.
What about baselines? Keep in mind that past behavior can only be used as an input, not the policy itself. The fact that an agent usually just reads data does not prove that a write is forbidden. That’s the job of the rule that pins agents to readonly. Missing or stale context also requires an explicit decision, as with hook timeouts.
I want an agent to complete the investigation or the support summary without requiring approval for every step. I also want to know exactly where an action outside that task will stop. That's what I would ask of every enforcement method, including Token Security.
Check us out or book a demo if you’re also solving these AI security problems in your organization.

articles.title: Sony veut tourner la page du disque, mais les joueurs français ne semblent pas prêts à l’abandonner
articles.text:
Alors que Sony prévoit d’abandonner progressivement les jeux PlayStation sur disque à partir de 2028, les ventes de Marvel’s Wolverine racontent une histoire quelque peu différente. En France, plus de deux exemplaires sur trois se sont vendus en version physique.
Exclusivité PlayStation 5, Marvel’s Wolverine constitue un assez bon révélateur des habitudes d’achat sur la console de Sony. Les chiffres de septembre montrent que le passage au tout-numérique avance à des vitesses très différentes selon les pays. Selon des données d’Ampere Analysis et de GSD relayées par The Game Business, 35 % des ventes mondiales de Marvel’s Wolverine ont été réalisées en version physique. En Europe, cette proportion grimpe à 51 %. En France, le phénomène est encore plus marqué : plus des deux tiers des ventes ont été réalisées sur disque.
La France reste très attachée au jeu physique
Le contraste avec le Royaume-Uni est frappant. Outre-Manche, environ deux tiers des ventes de Wolverine ont été numériques. En France, c’est donc presque exactement l’inverse. Et le jeu d’Insomniac n’est pas un cas isolé. Plus de 45 % des ventes de Silent Hill: Townfall ont été réalisées en boîte. Sur PS5, la part du physique atteint également 36 % pour The Blood of the Dawnwalker, tandis qu’Onimusha affiche 30 % de ventes physiques.
Ces chiffres ne signifient évidemment pas que le disque reprend partout du terrain. Ils montrent en revanche que certains jeux, souvent solo et narratifs, continuent de se vendre en grande partie en boîte.
« L’industrie est prête à passer à autre chose, mais pas aussi vite »
Le timing est particulièrement intéressant puisque Sony prévoit d’abandonner progressivement les jeux PlayStation sur disque à partir de janvier 2028. Une décision qui a déjà ravivé les débats autour de la propriété des jeux, de leur revente, du marché de l’occasion et de leur conservation à long terme.
Comme nous l’expliquions cet été dans un billet consacré à la fin annoncée du support physique sur PlayStation, le passage au tout-numérique revient aussi à troquer un objet que l’on possède réellement contre un droit d’accès dépendant des choix commerciaux des plateformes et des éditeurs.
Interrogé par The Game Business, l’analyste Joost van Dreunen résume assez bien la situation : les joueurs conservent un besoin de collectionner, ce qui maintient selon lui la pertinence du physique. Et si l’industrie est prête à passer à autre chose, elle ne peut pas le faire aussi vite.
Il serait risqué d’extrapoler les habitudes de tous les joueurs PlayStation à partir d’un seul titre. Mais lorsqu’une exclusivité PS5 comme Marvel’s Wolverine réalise plus des deux tiers de ses ventes françaises sur disque, le signal est difficile à ignorer : sur certains marchés, la transition vers le tout-numérique risque de prendre davantage de temps que ne le laisse penser la stratégie actuelle de Sony.

articles.title: Why Digital Convenience Hasn't Eliminated the Value of Physical Assets - Tech Guide
articles.text:
Ownership records, payments, and portfolios have largely moved to apps and online accounts. A balance can be viewed or transferred in seconds, and a digital record can make ownership easier to monitor. Yet speed and visibility do not determine what an asset is or why someone values it.
The persistence of physical holdings can therefore appear contradictory. Although records increasingly exist on screens, many assets remain objects that can be held, stored, moved, or inspected. Understanding this distinction requires separating the object itself from the records, rights, and prices attached to it. It also raises a broader question about which properties material ownership retains when access and record-keeping become digital.
What Counts as a Physical Asset
Before comparing physical and digital assets, the underlying definitions must be clear. In particular, an asset’s physical form, accounting classification, and stated value describe different qualities, even though those qualities can overlap.
Tangible, Intangible and Current Assets
A physical asset, also called a tangible asset, has material form and can be held, stored, moved, or inspected. By contrast, an intangible asset includes a trademark, licence, or software entitlement.
The value of an asset might mean its current market price, replacement cost, or balance-sheet figure, and those numbers rarely match.
Current assets are holdings expected to convert to cash within a year. They include cash, cash equivalents, marketable securities, accounts receivable, inventory, prepaid expenses, and short-term notes receivable. Physical and current assets are therefore overlapping classifications rather than competing ones.
Physical Assets You Can Actually Point To
Physical holdings include real property, machinery, equipment, vehicles, inventory, precious metals, collectibles, deeds, documents, and keys. A warehouse of inventory, a delivery van, and an American Buffalo gold coin are all tangible, although their uses and valuation methods differ.
These categories show why physical form must be considered separately from liquidity, accounting treatment, and the digital records connected to an asset.
What Digital Convenience Does Not Replicate
Digital systems make assets easier to record, monitor, and transfer. However, they do not reproduce every property of direct possession. The distinction becomes clearer when custody, access, and verification are treated as separate mechanisms rather than as a debate about technology’s trustworthiness.
Custody, Counterparty Risk and Account Access
Direct custody places possession and control with the holder. No account suspension, platform insolvency, or service shutdown stands between that holder and the physical object. However, this also transfers responsibility for protecting valuable belongings to the owner.
Counterparty risk is the possibility that another party will not honour a claim. Digital assets held through an account depend on the institution maintaining the record and permitting access. An object held directly does not carry that same claim against someone else, although its authenticity and legal ownership can still be disputed.
Account-access failure is more ordinary than institutional collapse. Lost credentials, locked profiles, frozen transfers, and service outages can temporarily separate a holder from an otherwise valid digital record. Direct custody avoids those access failures but introduces theft, loss, and damage instead.
Verifying Something Without a Platform
A physical asset can be weighed, measured, inspected, and authenticated without network connectivity or a functioning service provider. Its dimensions, condition, serial number, or material composition remain observable even when associated records are unavailable.
Still, that independence does not make physical holdings safer overall. It gives them a different failure profile. Diversification across physical and digital assets can reduce dependence on any single custody, access, or authentication system rather than eliminate risk altogether.
How Value Is Measured on Each Side of the Line
Digital and publicly listed holdings usually receive a continuous market price. This makes asset valuation quick and visible, but the displayed figure reflects the market at that moment. It does not necessarily show what a thinly traded holding would realise in a large sale or what replacement would cost later.
Physical holdings commonly carry several values at once. An appraisal estimates likely market value from comparable sales. Replacement cost asks what acquiring an equivalent item would require, while book value records an accounting figure after depreciation. A delivery van might have a modest book value but a much higher replacement cost.
Material content introduces another layer. An American Buffalo gold coin, a .9999 fine issue with an iconic design, has measurable content alongside any premium for condition, rarity, or design. According to the U.S. Mint, each official bullion issue contains one ounce of .9999 fine, 24-karat gold.
Appraisal and authentication cost money and take time. Consequently, physical valuation is less frequent and precise than a screen price, but it is not less real. What matters is whether the quoted figure represents market value, replacement cost, intrinsic value, or book value.
The Costs and Friction of Holding Something Real
The argument for physical ownership only holds if its costs are stated plainly. Material independence brings expenses and operational demands that a database entry does not, while physical transfers usually require more effort than changing a name in a digital ledger.
Storage, Insurance and Slow Liquidity
Storage and insurance are recurring costs. Valuable objects need secure locations, while machinery, vehicles, and buildings require maintenance. Some holdings also incur transport, specialist handling, inspection, and environmental-control expenses.
Liquidity is often the sharper constraint. Converting an object into cash means finding a buyer, establishing condition, agreeing on a price, and completing physical delivery. A listed holding might trade within seconds, whereas a vehicle, collectible, or property can take days or longer to transfer.
Condition also affects the result. Wear and depreciation reduce equipment values, while uncertain provenance increases authentication expenses for collectibles and bullion. Documentation, maintenance records, and a clear chain of ownership therefore influence valuation and saleability.
Digital Records Managing Physical Holdings
In practice, physical and digital systems increasingly operate together. Digital inventories connect photographs, serial numbers, purchase records, appraisal histories, maintenance schedules, and insurance documents to the tangible assets they describe.
These records support maximising asset performance by making maintenance intervals, condition changes, and ownership information easier to track. They can also show when insurance values no longer match replacement costs or equipment has become more expensive to maintain than replace.
Technology has changed how physical assets are catalogued, priced, insured, and transferred without altering the distinction between the record and the object. A database can document a machine’s location and condition, but it cannot perform the machine’s work. Likewise, a digital inventory can track bullion or property without becoming the material holding.
Convenience Changed Access, Not Ownership
Digitisation improved how assets are recorded, monitored, and moved between parties, but that differs from replacing what is held. A physical asset still provides direct custody, independence from account access, and material verifiability. Digital assets provide faster transfers, easier tracking, and more visible pricing.
Each arrangement carries different costs and failure modes. Physical ownership requires storage, insurance, authentication, and patience with slower liquidity. Digital convenience introduces dependence on accounts, counterparties, and operational systems. The useful distinction is therefore not physical versus digital, but which risks a holder accepts and which forms of diversification reduce exposure to any one system.

articles.title: GTA 6 suma a Lana Del Rey y dos músicos de Slayer para conducir emisoras de radio en Vice City
articles.text:
Grand Theft Auto VI prepara una experiencia musical que combinará artistas reconocidos, géneros de distintas regiones y nuevas formas de escuchar contenidos durante el juego. Según información publicada por Rolling Stone, Lana Del Rey, Bad Bunny y dos integrantes de Slayer estarán vinculados a emisoras de radio de GTA 6, aunque Rockstar Games todavía no confirmó oficialmente todas estas identidades.
La compañía presentó seis estaciones que formarán parte del mundo de Vice City y sus alrededores, con propuestas que van desde el reguetón y la bachata hasta el country, el hip-hop y el metal.
Entre las novedades también aparece la posibilidad de escuchar radio y pódcast mientras los protagonistas caminan por las calles, una función que amplía las opciones de entretenimiento fuera de los vehículos.
El videojuego tiene previsto su lanzamiento el 19 de noviembre para PlayStation 5 y Xbox Series X|S.
Las seis emisoras de radio que tendrá GTA 6
Rockstar reveló seis estaciones que estarán disponibles en Grand Theft Auto VI. Cada una tendrá una identidad musical propia y contribuirá a representar la diversidad cultural del estado ficticio de Leónida, donde transcurre la historia.
Estas son las emisoras presentadas hasta ahora:
- Flash FM: dedicada a la música pop, recupera una de las estaciones más reconocidas de la saga. Según Rolling Stone, estará conducida por la cantante Robyn y la modelo Alex Consani.
- Cocoteo FM: reúne música latina, desde reguetón y dembow hasta merengue y bachata. Bad Bunny y RaiNao figuran como sus conductores, de acuerdo con la publicación.
- Back Country Radio: enfocada en el country alternativo, contará con Morgan Wallen y Lana Del Rey, según la información difundida por Rolling Stone.
- AfroBank FM: ofrecerá música afro y combinará clásicos con artistas contemporáneos. Burna Boy estará al frente de la estación.
- The Chamber 106.6: será la opción para los seguidores del metal. Kerry King y Tom Araya, integrantes de Slayer, conducirán el espacio, según Rolling Stone.
- Dirty South Classics: estará dedicada al rap y al hip-hop del sur de Estados Unidos, con Trick Daddy y Trina como conductores.
Rockstar indicó que habrá más emisoras cuando el juego llegue al mercado. Por ahora, estas seis permiten anticipar la variedad musical que tendrá la nueva entrega.
Bad Bunny, Slayer y otros artistas en la banda sonora
Los adelantos oficiales ya permitieron conocer parte de la música que sonará durante las partidas. Entre los nombres y canciones anunciados aparecen Romeo Santos, Farruko, El Alfa, Loretta Lynn, Waylon Jennings, Black Sabbath, Pantera, Charli xcx, Zara Larsson, PinkPantheress, Asake, DJ Khaled, Rick Ross y Pitbull.
La selección combina artistas contemporáneos con referentes de diferentes épocas. En The Chamber 106.6, por ejemplo, se confirmó la presencia de canciones como I, de Black Sabbath; I’m Broken, de Pantera, y Raining Blood, de Slayer.
La música latina también tendrá un espacio importante en Cocoteo FM, donde figuran temas como EoO, de Bad Bunny; Si Es Trucho Es Trucho (Remix), de Axel Rulay junto a Farruko y El Alfa, y Canalla, de Romeo Santos y El Chaval de la Bachata.
Además, el repertorio oficial incluye a los argentinos CA7RIEL y Paco Amoroso, un dato que suma representación regional a la propuesta musical del videojuego.
GTA 6 permitirá escuchar radio y pódcast a pie
Otra de las novedades es que Jason y Lucía, los protagonistas de la historia, podrán escuchar radio y pódcast mientras recorren Leónida a pie, mediante auriculares vinculados a sus teléfonos.
Hasta ahora, la radio ha sido una parte característica de la experiencia de Grand Theft Auto, especialmente durante los desplazamientos en automóvil. La incorporación de contenidos para escuchar fuera de los vehículos amplía esa dinámica y permite mantener el componente musical durante otras actividades.
Rockstar todavía tiene pendiente revelar más detalles sobre las estaciones y los contenidos disponibles. Con su lanzamiento previsto para el 19 de noviembre, GTA 6 apunta a combinar una selección musical amplia con nuevas formas de integrar el sonido a la exploración de su mundo abierto.

articles.title: BYD au Mondial de l’Auto 2026 : le Great Tang serait-il la surprise du 12 octobre ? — Frandroid
articles.text:
Avec une Model Y, un arrêt au Superchargeur dure une trentaine de minutes. BYD vient de publier cette image à deux jours de l’ouverture du Mondial de l’Auto… qui pourrait nous surprendre.
Le message de BYD Europe : rendez-vous lundi 12 octobre à 10 h 55, sur le stand du Hall 6 de la Porte de Versailles, pour découvrir un nouveau modèle montré pour la première fois en Europe. Le communiqué officiel parle d’un « modèle inédit » et s’arrête là.
L’image montre la silhouette d’un SUV à contre-jour, garé devant un portique en T siglé BYD Flash. Le reste du stand de 1 000 m² est déjà connu, avec la citadine hybride rechargeable Dolphin G DM-i et le pick-up Shark de 5,46 mètres.
Le Great Tang, suspect numéro un
La silhouette évoque la famille Tang, et le calendrier va dans le même sens. En juin, Stella Li, vice-présidente exécutive de BYD, a annoncé l’arrivée du Great Tang en Europe pour la fin 2026 ou le début 2027.
    Pour aller plus loin
BYD Great Tang : plus imposant qu’un Tesla Model X, ce nouveau SUV électrique promet des caractéristiques totalement folles
            
Ce SUV de 5,30 mètres (c’est énorme) et sept places est le plus grand jamais vendu sous le logo BYD, avec une architecture 1 000 volts et des batteries de 105,8 ou 130,2 kWh.
La marque lui prête 800 à 950 km d’autonomie selon le cycle chinois CLTC, nettement plus généreux que notre cycle WLTP. D’autres candidats restent possibles, à commencer par le Sealion 08 de 5,11 mètres, lancé en Chine début septembre et lui aussi compatible Flash.
    Pour aller plus loin
Le BYD Great Tang est le 16° SUV de la marque : voici en quoi il se démarque des autres
            
Cinq minutes de recharge en théorie
La borne du teaser, on la connaît. Le système Flash Charging délivre jusqu’à 1 500 kW, quand les bornes rapides européennes plafonnent le plus souvent à 350 ou 400 kW. BYD annonce un passage de 10 à 70 % en cinq minutes, et de 10 à 97 % en neuf minutes.
Ces chiffres viennent du constructeur et supposent deux conditions réunies : une batterie Blade de deuxième génération dans la voiture, une borne BYD en face.
Sur une borne Ionity ou un Superchargeur, la voiture se contentera de ce que la borne sait fournir. Or le réseau européen débute à peine, avec de premières stations en Allemagne et au Royaume-Uni, et je n’ai trouvé aucune station publique ouverte en France pour le moment. L’objectif de 3 000 stations en Europe existe bien, avec une échéance qui glisse de fin 2026 à 2027 selon les prises de parole.
Un SUV sept places électrique capable de traverser la France avec deux pauses courtes intéresse d’abord les familles qui hésitent entre un Kia EV9, un Volvo EX90 et un Peugeot E-5008.
Pour quelqu’un qui recharge surtout à domicile et part deux fois par an, une borne à 1 500 kW ne changera rien au quotidien. La seule voiture compatible vendue en Europe jusqu’ici est la Denza Z9GT, facturée autour de 115 000 euros, donc l’arrivée d’une BYD tout court ferait descendre la technologie d’un étage.
Si on a confirmation, on aura certainement plus de détails pendant le Mondial de l’auto : le prix européen, l’autonomie WLTP, la date de livraison en France et la puissance réellement acceptée sur une prise CCS. Le tarif chinois, 239 900 yuans soit environ 30 000 euros, ne dit rien de la facture ici une fois les droits de douane ajoutés. Il faut ça, sans doute, au moins doubler ce tarif.

articles.title: La 'ley de nietos' acaba de convertirse en la gran grieta del 29-N y de momento nadie sabe a cuántos votantes afecta
articles.text:
Las convocatorias electorales (sobre todo las adelantadas, como es el caso) suelen elevar el tono del debate político. El 29-N lo que está recrudeciendo es el debate jurídico. Y todo a costa de una normativa de 2022. La conocida como 'ley de nietos' se ha convertido en una pieza clave del panorama preelectoral español, el foco de una espinosa controversia que, además de a los partidos, ha enredado al Tribunal Supremo, la Abogacía del Estado, la Fiscalía y la Junta Electoral. Es comprensible si se tiene en cuenta qué está en juego: quiénes podrán acudir a las urnas en noviembre.
Para los servicios jurídicos del Estado, el dilema es el siguiente: ¿Qué hacer con miles de españoles inscritos en el CERA, el censo de votantes que viven en el extranjero?
¿Qué es la 'ley de nietos'? El apodo popular de la Ley 20/2022 de Memoria Democrática. Para ser más precisos, el de su disposición octava, que dio un plazo de dos años (más tarde prorrogado hasta octubre de 2025) para que los descendientes de españoles nacidos en el extranjero pudieran solicitar la nacionalidad de sus ancestros.
¿A quién se abría esa puerta? A los hijos y nietos de españoles que, "como consecuencia de haber sufrido exilio por razones políticas, ideológicas o de creencia u orientación e identidad sexual, hubieran perdido o renunciado a la nacionalidad española".
La norma no acotaba ningún marco temporal, pero sí deslizó un concepto clave: "exilio". El pasaporte quedaba al alcance de los hijos o nietos de españoles a los que durante la dictadura no les quedó otra que hacer las maletas. El cómo ejercer ese derecho lo aclaró días después el Ministerio de Justicia a través de una instrucción dirigida a todos los interesados, los registros civiles y los consulados.
¿Es eso importante? Mucho. De hecho es la clave del embrollo judicial que está caldeando las semanas previas al 29-N. La instrucción diferencia entre dos perfiles. Por un lado están los descendientes de españoles que abandonaron el país entre el 18 de julio de 1936 y el 31 de diciembre de 1955, es decir, el período durante el que se prolongó la Guerra Civil y la fase de aislamiento del franquismo. Por otro lado, están los herederos de españoles que cruzaron las fronteras entre enero de 1956 y 1978, cuando se aprobó la Constitución.
A efectos de la aplicación de la Ley de Memoria Democrática esa distinción es fundamental. En el primer caso (quienes hicieron las maletas entre 1936 y 1955) el Estado "presume la condición de exiliado" general, aplicable a todos los españoles que cambiaron de país. Para reclamar la nacionalidad, sus descendientes solo deben acreditar que lo son y que sus padres o abuelos salieron de España.
En el segundo caso (1956-1978) la norma es bastante más estricta y exige a quienes quieran acogerse a la 'ley de nietos' que prueben que sus antepasados eran "exiliados".
¿Tan relevante es? Para Vox y Iustitia Europa sí. Ambas formaciones acudieron a la justicia con un argumento relevante: las instrucciones tienen un rango menor que las leyes, por lo que no pueden modificarlas. Y Vox opina que eso es precisamente lo que ocurrió en 2022 con la 'ley de nietos'. Si bien la norma habla de descendientes de "exiliados", en ningún caso contempla que todos los españoles que abandonaron el país entre 1936 y 1955 puedan considerarse como tal, algo que sí dice la instrucción ministerial.
Dicho de otro modo, la formación de Abascal argumenta que el Gobierno amplió las costuras de la ley sin pasar por las Cortes. "La Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública [el Ministerio de Justicia] dicta una Instrucción que extiende el acceso a la nacionalidad mucho más allá del texto legal", subrayaban.
Vox pidió que dejara de aplicarse de forma cautelar y llevó el tema al Supremo y la Junta Electoral Central (JEC). ¿Por qué acudió a este último organismo? Muy fácil. Porque la nacionalidad abre la puerta al derecho al voto y Vox solicitó auditar y controlar las altas en el censo de electores en el exterior (CERA).
¿Qué hizo el Tribunal Supremo? A principios de septiembre la Corte suspendió los efectos electorales de la 'ley de nietos'. Lo hizo de forma cautelar, a la espera de dictar una sentencia y centrando el foco en aquellos casos en los que los herederos no hubieran acreditado la condición de exiliados de sus ancestros. La decisión del alto tribunal no anuló concesiones de nacionalidad y tampoco es definitiva, pero afecta directamente a miles de altas en el CERA.
UN VISTAZO A...
Quienes obtuvieron la nacionalidad española por la ‘ley de nietos’ y aún no se habían inscrito en el CERA se encontraron con que el trámite quedaba suspendido. Quienes ya estaban anotados vieron cómo su registro en el CERA se quedaba en el limbo de cara a cualquier convocatoria electoral. Como recuerda Confilegal, la cuestión ya no era quién podía convertirse en español amparándose en la Ley de Memoria Democrática, sino quién podía figurar en el censo y votar.
Y todo a solo unos meses (eso se creía) de las elecciones.
¿Qué pasó el lunes? Que el panorama se complicó aún más. La decisión de Pedro Sánchez de adelantar las elecciones generales tras el fracaso de sus decretos exprés sobre vivienda sumó un nuevo elemento de presión al embrollo judicial de la ‘ley de nietos’: el calendario. A fin de cuentas, la convocatoria del 29-N se publicó después de que miles de personas con nacionalidad española viesen cómo se suspendía su derecho a participar en las elecciones.
Tanto se complicó la cosa, que el martes el Supremo dio un plazo de 48 horas a la Abogacía del Estado, la JEC, Fiscalía y Iustitia Europa y Vox para que se pronunciasen.
Sobre la mesa, una duda: ¿Debe el tribunal emplazar a participar en el proceso a los miles de afectados por las medidas cautelares, personas ya nacionalizadas a las que se les ha suspendido el derecho a voto? ¿Se arriesga el Supremo a un choque con el Constitucional? Es una cuestión relevante porque el alto tribunal quizás contase con dictar sentencia antes del próximo verano (cuando finalizaba la legislatura), pero resulta casi imposible que lo haga antes del 29-N.
¿Y qué ha pasado? Que a la vista del elevado número de personas que recurrieron a la 'ley de nietos' parece muy difícil comunicarse con todos los afectados, a los que habría que explicar además qué inscripciones en el CERA se ven realmente afectadas.
El Supremo ha pedido a las Oficinas del Censo Electoral que desglosen las altas de personas nacionalizadas al amparo de la instrucción de 2022 y las que se ajustaron a lo previsto directamente en la Ley de Memoria Democrática. El problema es que no llega con apretar un botón. Esa clasificación exige revisar miles de expedientes. Y los consulados tienen el calendario en su contra.
Teniendo en cuenta que las elecciones se celebrarán el 29 de noviembre, el censo que se utilice debe ser el cerrado en agosto y debe exponerse para consulta el 12 de octubre. A la vista de esos plazos, la Abogacía del Estado ha alegado que resulta "materialmente imposible" comprobar caso por caso para saber quién cumple y quién no las condiciones para votar. De ahí que reclame retirar las medidas cautelares.
¿Qué argumenta? "La Sala se encuentra en la necesidad de valorar, ponderar de forma proporcional, el sacrificio del derecho fundamental al sufragio activo que se está imponiendo, sin trámite de audiencia alguno, a 163.020 españoles", señala el Abogado del Estado. En su opinión, las medidas cautelares adoptadas por el Supremo no solo privan del derecho de voto a miles de nacionalizados, tampoco permiten a los afectados "ningún tipo de justificación".
En resumen: toca "ponderar intereses". "Ante el riesgo del sacrificio inmediato de un derecho fundamental, lo que debe primar es el ejercicio del derecho particular", subraya. "O se suspende a todos los españoles inscritos en el CERA (pues los datos que en él se tienen son, globalmente, los de los españoles sin distinción alguna) o no se suspende a ninguno, porque resulta materialmente imposible distinguir a unos de otros en el brevísimo plazo de tiempo disponible".
¿Se han oído más voces? Sí. Fiscalía ha reclamado al Supremo que permita votar a los nacionalizados al amparo de la 'ley de nietos' el 29-N y advierte de que el adelanto electoral exige revisar las medidas cautelares. Por su parte, Iustitia Europea exige la suspensión cautelar de las elecciones del próximo 29 de noviembre y que la convocatoria electoral eche el freno "el tiempo estrictamente indispensable" para garantizar que se ejecutan las órdenes del Supremo.
Otra voz que se ha sumado al debate en las últimas horas es la del ministro de Justicia, Félix Bolaños, quien ha advertido que España corre el riesgo de acudir a las urnas con "un censo alterado". "Le estamos pidiendo con todo el respeto al Tribunal Supremo que resuelva cuanto antes esa cuestión, porque imagine el escenario: se va a las elecciones, se vota y después se decide que la demanda no tenía ningún sentido y que esas personas tenían que haber votado", planteó Bolaños durante un acto en Sevilla.
¿Tanto puede influir en el 29-N? Depende de a quién le preguntes. La sospecha de que los nuevos votantes favorecerán en las urnas al partido gobernante (PSOE), el mismo que ha sacado adelante la medida, ha llevado al PP a tachar la 'ley de nietos' de "ingeniería electoral". En Vox incluso han ido más allá al acusar a Sánchez de intentar "el mayor pucherazo electoral del régimen de 1978". Desde la Abogacía del Estado se argumenta sin embargo que el peso de los nuevos electores sería tan reducido que, en la práctica, "no tendría un impacto significativo" en los resultados electorales.
¿Hay datos? Los del Gobierno muestran que, si bien la 'ley de nietos' ha tenido un alcance considerable, ese impacto se descafeína de forma considerable en las urnas. Según sus registros, la puerta abierta en octubre de 2022 despertó el interés de más de 2,4 millones de personas, pero a cierre del pasado agosto (fecha clave de cara al censo del 29-N) solo habían obtenido la nacionalidad cerca de 600.000.
Todo indica que el número de inscritos para votar es muy inferior. En sus alegaciones al Supremo, los servicios jurídicos del Estado hablan del "derecho al sufragio activo" de 163.020 personas y, basándose en las estadísticas de participación, reducen el dato aún más. "Se trata, en términos estadísticos, del voto de 14.120 personas". Iustitia eleva los censados desde las elecciones de 2023 a 408.262, aunque sin distinguir la vía de nacionalización.

articles.title: Pour mieux repérer la poussière sur vos sols, le Dyson V12 Detect Slim Absolute est à 449 €
articles.text:
L’aspirateur balai Dyson V12 Detect Slim Absolute est à 449 €
Le Dyson V12 Detect Slim Absolute associe une brosse éclairante pour sols durs, un capteur de particules et plusieurs accessoires dans un format compact.
Boulanger propose le Dyson V12 Detect Slim Absolute à 449 €, contre un prix de référence affiché de 649 €. Cela représente 200 € d’économie. L’appareil est neuf, vendu et expédié par Boulanger. Le retrait gratuit en magasin est proposé selon les disponibilités locales.
Une brosse éclairante pour repérer la poussière
La brosse Fluffy Optic utilise une lumière dirigée sur les sols durs pour rendre la poussière fine plus visible. Elle permet de mieux repérer les zones à nettoyer sur un parquet ou un carrelage.
Le V12 Detect Slim intègre également un capteur piézo, qui compte les particules aspirées et permet d’adapter automatiquement la puissance. L’écran LCD affiche les informations relatives aux particules collectées : un retour visuel sur ce que l’appareil ramasse pendant le nettoyage. Dyson annonce une puissance d’aspiration maximale de 150 AW.
Le pack proposé par Boulanger comprend aussi une brosse Motorbar, adaptée aux tapis et aux sols durs, avec un système destiné à démêler les cheveux et les poils. Une mini-brosse motorisée et un suceur long complètent l’ensemble pour les textiles et les espaces étroits.
Un format compact et jusqu’à 60 minutes d’autonomie
Avec un poids d’environ 2,4 kg, cet aspirateur sans fil mise sur la maniabilité. Il se commande par un bouton marche-arrêt, sans avoir à maintenir une gâchette enfoncée pendant toute la séance. En retirant le tube, il peut également servir d’aspirateur à main avec les accessoires fournis.
L’autonomie annoncée atteint jusqu’à 60 minutes, avec une durée réelle qui dépend du mode utilisé et des conditions de nettoyage. Une recharge complète demande environ quatre heures. Son collecteur de 0,35 litre contribue au format compact, mais implique des vidages plus fréquents lorsque la quantité de poussière ou de poils est importante. Une station murale et le chargeur sont inclus pour le rangement et la recharge.
