articles.title: Why Moove is leaving the Nigerian market it was built in
articles.text:
Six years after Moove put 76 cars on Lagos roads and asked Uber drivers to pay for them out of their earnings, the mobility company is leaving Nigeria, its founding market, and handing many of those drivers their cars.
In a statement on Thursday, Moove said it will hand over eligible vehicles worth about ₦35 billion ($26.3 million) to the drivers, with no further payment due from October 1. Every Moove employee will also get a free car. The announcement came five weeks after Uber, Moove’s investor and its only ride-hailing partner in Nigeria, exited the country.
“Nigeria will always be where Moove started,” the company said in its statement, describing the handover as its way of thanking the customers and staff who built the business.
Moove’s exit is a knock-on effect of Uber leaving Nigeria. If you think of Moove’s Nigerian business as a lending business, then it relied on Uber earnings data to decide who got a car and ensure they kept paying. When Uber left Nigeria, that data went with it, and Moove lost its way to price and collect those loans.
With Moove’s future in robotaxi depots in the United States, its Nigerian business, which faced many challenges, no longer represents a solid business opportunity.
How we got here
When the International Finance Corporation (IFC), the World Bank’s private-sector lender, invested in Moove in 2021, it described a product that financed up to 95% of a car over two to four years, with drivers repaying a share of their weekly platform earnings. Uber was picked as the platform.
That same year, Ladi Delano, Moove’s co-founder and co-CEO, told Bloomberg that the company used ride-hailing earnings and performance data to make its credit decisions. Moove shared offices with Uber in Lagos, Johannesburg and Accra and said it had no plans to work with any of Uber’s rivals, including Bolt.
The exclusivity was essential to the business model. Moove kept its Nigerian drivers on Uber Go, Uber’s budget category, and in 2022 said it couldn’t generate the data it needed to underwrite loans if drivers used several ride-hailing apps.
The model depended on two things Moove did not control: Uber’s demand and the naira.
Moove funded part of its Nigerian fleet with dollar-denominated debt while its drivers earned in naira. When the naira fell, it hit Moove’s pricing. In February 2023, TechCabal reported that drivers paid ₦9,400 ($14.57) daily for Suzuki SUVs priced at ₦11.7 million ($18,134). Suzuki’s Nigerian retail price was ₦9.9 million ($15,344).
By 2025, Moove’s weekly remittance had doubled, going from ₦56,400 ($87) to ₦112,200 ($74). At 2025’s average exchange rate, ₦112,200 came to about $74 a week. That is less than the roughly $87 that ₦56,400 was worth at 2023’s rate.
While the naira was in freefall, drivers saw a lender squeezing them. They went on strike, and by November the Lagos State chapter of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC), the country’s largest trade union, was planning a protest at Moove’s office.
Demand on UberGo was also thinning. In January 2025, Moove drivers told Technext that ride requests had dried up and some were missing their targets. Some drivers said Moove sent agents posing as riders to catch them working on inDrive. Despite Uber losing market share to Bolt and inDrive, Moove kept its drivers tied to Uber.
Uber and Moove’s deep relationship
Uber called Moove its preferred fleet partner in sub-Saharan Africa. In March 2024, the ride-hailing giant led Moove’s $100 million Series B at a $750 million valuation, its first investment in an African startup, owning more than 10%.
When Nigerian drivers protested unfair working arrangements in 2023, Uber kept its distance, saying it had been made aware of concerns from a small group of drivers.
Hours after Uber’s exit on September 2, Moove dropped the Uber-only rule drivers had demanded for years. That solved the drivers’ problem but ended the single data stream Moove’s lending relied on. By then, Nigeria was already a small part of Moove.
In December 2024, Waymo, Alphabet’s self-driving car unit, hired Moove to run fleet operations, depots and charging in Phoenix and Miami. In August, Moove raised $250 million at a $2.1 billion valuation, reporting about 42,000 vehicles in 29 cities across 13 countries and $420 million in annual recurring revenue. The new funding will finance self-driving fleets and robot-run depots the company calls Nests. Nigeria is not a destination for any Nest, because the country cannot support the self-driving technology at scale.
Today’s handover looks like Moove’s cheapest way out. Without Uber’s data, Moove would have to collect repayments from drivers now working for Bolt and inDrive, in naira, for a company that no longer has Nigeria in its focus.
Giving drivers ownership ends a years-long fight and buys goodwill. Whether it is also generous depends on a number Moove has not shared: how much those drivers still owed on October 1.
Moove started in Lagos by putting cars in drivers’ hands on credit. Delano once said Nigeria taught Moove how to finance and run a fleet, and many of the drivers who paid for that lesson now keep the cars.
True scale demands moving beyond surface-level integrations to robust execution. We’ve filtered the noise out of Moonshot 2026, optimising the conference strictly for high-calibre connections between startup founders, global financial operators, enterprise leaders and individuals rewiring Africa’s technical frameworks. articles.title: Hopper cuts staff shortly after co-founder departs | BetaKit
articles.text:
Travel technology company Hopper appears to have laid off staff on its enterprise side, following the departure of the company’s co-founder last month.
The news: On Sept. 28, Hopper co-founder Dakota Smith announced on LinkedIn that he was leaving the company after leading its enterprise division, Hopper Technology Solutions, as CEO for the past three years. Shortly after, more than half a dozen employees posted on LinkedIn indicating their roles had been eliminated.
BetaKit reached out to Hopper for more details but has not yet received a response. In a LinkedIn message, Smith told BetaKit that he had nothing further to share on his departure and that he didn’t have insight into restructuring as his last day was in mid-September.
From the source: “Scaling an org from [less than] 200 employees to 1,200+ distributed across 37+ countries while keeping the bar as high as ours has been pure madness to say the least,” Kamil Eladas, a former technical recruitment manager who had worked at the company for nearly seven years, wrote in an Oct. 2 post. Eladas didn’t directly state whether his departure was due to the layoffs, but said that leaving the company was “bittersweet.”
The context: It’s unclear how the job cuts were distributed across the company, and whether Smith’s departure was related. HTS is Hopper’s B2B division that provides data, e-commerce, and financial technology services; it accounts for the majority of the company’s revenue.
Hopper has made multiple rounds of layoffs over the past few years as it has navigated changes to its partnerships. Earlier this year, Hopper client and US financial services giant Capital One brought the platform Hopper was developing, and the employees behind it, in-house. Hopper also inked significant deals this year, landing a partnership with Royal Bank of Canada to power its travel rewards program.
Final thought: The travel industry publication Skift reported that Hopper may be facing pressure from increased competition in Asia, due to travel company Booking Holdings’ upcoming consolidation of its brands Agoda, Priceline, and Booking.com.
Feature image courtesy Hopper.

articles.title: Hackers get $1,262,000 for 98 zero-days at Pwn2Own Ireland
articles.text:
The Pwn2Own Ireland 2026 hacking contest has concluded, with hackers collecting $1,262,000 in rewards after exploiting 98 zero-day flaws.
Ikotas Labs security researchers won this year's Pwn2Own Ireland edition with 42.5 Master of Pwn points and $361,000 earned over the three-day contest after hacking the Samsung Galaxy S26, OpenAI Codex, and the Oracle Autonomous AI Database.
They also collected the competition's top reward of $300,000 on the third day after chaining multiple zero-days to hack the Google Pixel 10.
Xint took second place with $240,000 and 27.5 Master of Pwn points, while Team ZyGoat secured third with $125,000 in prizes and 27.5 Master of Pwn points.
Interrupt Labs, Ikotas Labs, and Nguyen Thanh Dat of Viettel Cyber Security hacked Samsung's Galaxy S26 flagship on the first day, but the vendor already knew some of the exploited bugs. In all, competitors collected $388,500 after demonstrating 32 zero-day flaws.
On the second day, competitors earned $232,500 in cash awards for 45 unique zero-day vulnerabilities, with the highlight being PetoWorks, KAIST Hacking Lab's Kyeongmin Kim, and a team including Dimitrios Valsamaras, Ken Gannon, and Tenia Valsamara from CENSUS Labs, who took down the Galaxy S26 three more times.
On the third day, hackers rooted the Samsung Galaxy S26 again and took down the Google Pixel 10 three times. In total, today security researchers exploited 21 zero-days for $641,000 in cash on the final day of the contest.
This year, 29 research teams targeted products across seven categories: mobile phones (Samsung Galaxy S26 and Google Pixel 10), AI infrastructure, AI coding apps, messaging apps, smart home devices, printers, and a new category focused on wellness healthcare devices.
Apple's iPhone 17 was also a potential target, with a maximum award of $300,000 for a remote hack, but no contestant registered for an attempt.
Trend Micro's Zero Day Initiative (ZDI) organizes the competition to identify zero-day flaws before attackers exploit them in the wild. Pwn2Own rules require all devices and products to run the latest firmware versions, and contestants to compromise the target and demonstrate arbitrary code execution.
Vendors must patch zero-days disclosed during the Pwn2Own competition within 90 days before ZDI publicly shares details.
During Pwn2Own Ireland 2025, hackers demoed 73 zero-day flaws to earn $1,024,750. Summoning Team won the contest and collected $187,500 after hacking the Samsung Galaxy S25, the Home Assistant Green, the QNAP TS-453E NAS, and multiple Synology devices.

articles.title: Apple donne rendez-vous pour un événement imminent... et ne compterait pas s'arrêter là
articles.text:
C’est officiel, Apple donne rendez-vous pour de nouveaux produits dans quelques jours. Le géant de Cupertino vient d’annoncer une présentation pour le mardi 13 octobre, sous le slogan « Welcome Home ». Comme d’habitude, la firme n’a rien dévoilé des produits au programme de l’événement. Notez qu’il ne s’agit vraisemblablement pas d’une keynote traditionnelle, mais d’un événement presse, organisé à New York. Selon Bloomberg, une vidéo retransmise en ligne est néanmoins prévue.
 Welcome home. October 13. https://t.co/ChelGSDOTI
— Greg Joswiak (@gregjoz) October 8, 2026
Un HomePod avec écran
La star de l’événement prendrait la forme d‘un HomePod avec écran. Évoqué comme le croisement entre un iPad et un HomePod, l’appareil serait doté d’un écran carré d’environ 6 pouces. Taillé pour être disposé dans la cuisine, il servirait à piloter les objets connectés de la maison, à passer des appels FaceTime, à regarder des vidéos ou encore à consulter la météo et son agenda. Pour converser avec l’appareil, il faudrait s’adresser au nouveau Siri dopé à l’IA.
L’appareil, souvent baptisé HomePad dans les fuites, devrait embarquer une caméra et un capteur de présence, qui lui permettraient de reconnaître la personne présente dans la pièce. En fonction de la personne identifiée, l’écran pourrait afficher une interface personnalisée. Une version murale et une version posée sur un socle seraient dans les cartons. Côté prix, la rumeur évoque environ 350 dollars.
Ce n’est pas tout. Le HomePod mini devrait lui aussi être renouvelé, avec de nouveaux coloris, une puce réseau N1, et un processeur plus rapide, compatible avec Siri IA. Une nouvelle Apple TV 4K serait également prévue. Le boîtier profiterait d’une puce A19 ou A19 Pro, de plus de mémoire, de la puce N1 et d’une télécommande Siri améliorée. Dans la foulée, Apple dévoilerait la gamme de produits domotique développée avec LG.
Un troisième événement fin octobre
Apple ne compterait pas s’arrêter en si bon chemin. Après avoir levé le voile sur l’iPhone Duo et une armée de produits pour la maison connectée, la marque préparerait une troisième vague d’annonces à la fin du mois pour boucler l’année. Selon le journaliste Mark Gurman de Bloomberg, la troisième présentation aurait lieu « autour du » mardi 27 octobre 2026.
 NEW: Apple’s big October will continue on the 27th with a second event to launch the first touch-screen MacBooks, OLED iPad mini and M6 14-inch MacBook Pro & iMac. It follows the smart home launch this coming Tuesday the 13th. https://t.co/bh8Vqdgnr8 https://t.co/wmlNWXC41n
— Mark Gurman (@markgurman) October 8, 2026
Le produit le plus attendu de l’événement est un MacBook Pro recouvert d’un écran OLED tactile. Évoqué sous le nom de MacBook Ultra dans les fuites, il serait plus fin et plus léger que les ordinateurs actuels. Apple annoncerait aussi un MacBook Pro 14 pouces M6, un iMac M6, et un iPad mini avec écran OLED. Bref, le mois d’octobre s’annonce chargé chez Apple.

articles.title: 390 Meter unter dem Meer: Wie Norwegen den längsten Unterwassertunnel der Welt aus dem Fels sprengt
articles.text:
Rogfast: Norwegen sprengt einen 26,7 Kilometer Tunnel unter die Nordsee
Es ist kalt, es ist sehr, sehr laut, und – wenn ich ganz ehrlich sein darf – ich fühle mich alles andere als entspannt. Außerdem ist meine Schutzbrille beschlagen.
Ich befinde mich etwa 300 Meter unter der Nordsee, in einer dunklen, feuchten Höhle. Es riecht seltsam. Und mir wird immer bewusster, wie viel Druck Millionen Tonnen Meerwasser direkt über meinem Kopf ausüben. Sie üben eine Kraft von mehr als 35 Kilogramm pro Quadratzentimeter aus – wie ein Nashornbaby, das auf einer Briefmarke steht. Nur dank großartiger Ingenieurskunst werde ich nicht zerquetscht, ertrinke oder verschwinde einfach.
Dieser Text ist in der Ausgabe 7/2026 von MIT Technology Review erschienen. Darin beschäftigen wir uns damit, wie KI die IT-Sicherheit auf den Kopf stellt. Das Heft ist in unserem Online-Shop bestellbar und im Zeitschriftenhandel erhältlich.
Ein paar hundert Meter entfernt trifft jemand Vorbereitungen, um eine riesige Felswand zu sprengen. Zum Glück habe ich eine Sicherheitseinweisung erhalten und trage einen Spezialhelm. „Keine Sorge – falls du es nicht schaffst, lassen wir deine Sachen an dein Büro zurückschicken“, sagt die Geologin Anne-Merete Gilje mit ernster Miene. Norwegischer Humor.
Wie ein Straßentunnel unter Norwegens berühmten Fjord entsteht
Ich bin hier, unter den berühmten Fjorden Norwegens, um mir anzusehen, wie der bald längste und tiefste Unterwasser-Straßentunnel der Welt entsteht: Rogfast (kurz für „Rogaland Fixed Link“). Ich möchte verstehen, wie man eine 26,7 Kilometer lange Autobahn baut, die an ihrer tiefsten Stelle 390 Meter unter dem Meeresspiegel verläuft.
Norwegen hat in den letzten Jahrzehnten mehr als tausend Kilometer Tunnel gebaut. Die spektakuläre Lage des Landes macht solche Bauvorhaben notwendig; zwar sind die Norweger stolz auf ihre nach Kanada zweitlängste Küstenlinie der Welt, doch um die Westküste hinauf- und hinunterzukommen, sind entweder mehrere Fährfahrten zwischen den Inseln oder große Umwege erforderlich.
    „Wir können kein Buch kaufen, um nachzulesen, wie man das macht.“
Wenn er fertig ist, soll Rogfast zwei Fährverbindungen überflüssig machen und die fünfstündige Fahrt zwischen den südwestlichen Städten Stavanger und Bergen um 40 Minuten verkürzen. Vier Fahrspuren und zwei Verkehrskreisel führen dann tief unter den Fjorden Boknafjord und Kvitsøyfjord durch, und an einer Stelle wird nur eine relativ dünne Gesteinsschicht von 50 Metern die Autofahrer vom Grund der Nordsee trennen.

articles.title: Ring dévoile sa première serrure connectée, avec une idée maligne pour éviter les pannes de batterie
articles.text:
Ring présente sa première serrure connectée, avec une solution originale pour éviter les mauvaises surprises liées à une batterie déchargée. Une simple molette permet de lui redonner suffisamment d’énergie pour déverrouiller la porte.
Une serrure connectée qui tombe en panne de batterie au mauvais moment, c’est le genre de mésaventure que personne ne souhaite vivre. Les fabricants ont prévu différentes solutions pour éviter de rester bloqué devant chez soi. Ring a décidé d’emprunter une autre voie. La filiale d’Amazon, jusqu’ici principalement connue pour ses sonnettes vidéo et ses caméras de surveillance, vient de présenter sa toute première serrure connectée. Et sa particularité tient dans un mécanisme plutôt astucieux, qui permet de produire soi-même l’énergie nécessaire à son fonctionnement.
Ring mise sur une molette pour éviter les pannes de batterie
La nouvelle Ring Smart Lock possède une particularité inédite à ce jour : elle peut retrouver suffisamment d’énergie pour fonctionner même lorsque sa batterie est complètement déchargée. Comme l’explique Amazon dans son annonce, le dispositif intègre une molette qu’il suffit de tourner plusieurs fois pour rétablir temporairement son alimentation. L’utilisateur peut alors s’authentifier et déverrouiller sa porte sans avoir besoin d’une clé de secours ou d'une batterie externe.
Le fabricant entend ainsi répondre à l’une des principales inquiétudes liées aux serrures connectées. Si certains modèles conservent une ouverture mécanique traditionnelle, d’autres nécessitent une alimentation de secours pour fonctionner lorsque leur batterie est vide. Ring promet de s’affranchir de ces contraintes grâce à un mécanisme intégré directement à sa serrure. La marque ne mentionne pas la quantité d'énergie produite, ni le nombre de rotations nécessaires pour retrouver l’accès à son domicile.
Cette approche se distingue également de celle adoptée par Nuki. En mars dernier, nous évoquions sur Clubic le Smart Module du fabricant autrichien, un système directement intégré aux portes et alimenté en permanence par le bâtiment. Ring privilégie une solution autonome, destinée à remplacer une serrure traditionnelle compatible. Deux manières de répondre au même problème, même si la seconde conserve une batterie qu'il faudra recharger régulièrement.
Une serrure connectée qui renforce l’écosystème Amazon
Au-delà de son système de recharge, la Ring Smart Lock propose quatre méthodes de déverrouillage. Les utilisateurs pourront ouvrir leur porte avec leur empreinte digitale, saisir un code sur un clavier tactile rétroéclairé, utiliser l’application Ring ou passer par Alexa. L'application permettra également de vérifier à distance si la porte est verrouillée et de créer des accès temporaires, par exemple pour autoriser un proche ou un prestataire à entrer pendant une plage horaire déterminée.
Pour assurer sa connectivité, Ring fait appel à Amazon Sidewalk, un réseau partagé reposant sur les appareils Amazon compatibles situés à proximité. Cette technologie permet notamment de transmettre les informations d’état et de synchroniser les codes d’accès sans dépendre directement du réseau Wi-Fi domestique. La serrure pourra également communiquer avec les sonnettes, caméras et systèmes d’alarme Ring, tandis que les événements seront regroupés dans l'application de la marque. Une intégration qui renforce la place d’Amazon dans la sécurité domestique, mais qui suppose aussi de disposer d’une couverture Sidewalk suffisante pour profiter des fonctions à distance.
La Ring Smart Lock sera commercialisée début 2027 aux États-Unis, en trois finitions : noir, argent et laiton. Amazon n’a pas encore annoncé de disponibilité en Europe, ni précisé si son appareil prendrait en charge les standards domotiques comme Matter. Son installation est prévue sur les portes équipées d’un verrou américain à cylindre simple, ce qui pose également la question de sa compatibilité avec les portes européennes.
Pour les utilisateurs français, la promesse est donc séduisante, mais encore assez lointaine. Ring a peut-être trouvé comment éviter de rester à la porte à cause d'une batterie vide. Encore faudra-t-il que sa serrure puisse s’installer sur la nôtre.

articles.title: Why public capital isn’t enough to save India’s deeptech
articles.text:
Why public capital isn’t enough to save India’s deeptech
The most powerful derisker is not a fund at all. It is a customer. A Rs 200 crore procurement commitment from the defence, space or railways sectors does more for a series B round than a Rs 200 crore grant, because it validates revenue rather than science.
Can government funds derisk deeptech enough to make private capital comfortable in India? Partly. The state is well placed to absorb technology risk. It is far less able to remove the two risks that actually keep fund managers awake: time and exit. Unless policy addresses those, India will get plenty of capital without much conviction behind it.
Start with the momentum, which is real. India’s AI and deep tech investment reached $2.1 bn across 289 deals in 2025, and deep tech share of total VC – PE activity has climbed to roughly 15%, up from 4% in 2016. The 2026 numbers look even better at first glance through August, Indian deeptech companies raised $2.22 billion across 179 rounds against $861 million across 287 rounds in the same period last year.
Look closer, though. Funding rose about 2.6 times while the number of rounds fell by nearly 40%. The average cheque went from roughly $3 million to over $12 million, a four-fold jump. Private capital is getting comfortable with deeptech companies that are already derisked. It is not getting comfortable with the derisking itself. Money is crowding into proven AI and hardware winners, and fewer new bets are being placed. That gap is exactly what public funds should fill.
The state’s toolkit is now large. The Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Scheme, envisages a Rs. 1 lakh crore corpus over 6 years with Rs. 20,000 crore allocated in FY 2025-26 Union budget. Alongside it sits the Startup India Fund of Funds 2.0. SIDBI is mandated to deploy Rs 10,000 crores through SEBI registered AIFs, with the government's stake alongside private investors, who comprise a majority of the Fund corpus. The first version worked as a multiplier in 145 AIFs, which together invested more than Rs. 25,500 crores in over 1,370 startups. That is a leverage ratio of about 2.5x.
Now the maths is what matters. Spread evenly, the RDI corpus works out to about Rs. 16700 crores a year, or roughly $1.7 bn. That is very close to the size of India’s entire annual deeptech VC haul. The state is no longer a marginal anchor. It is an almost co-equal capital provider, and that scale can crowd private money in or crowd it out. But this will depend on which risk the money absorbs.
Technology risk means asking whether the product will work. Grants and lab-to-market funding (debt / equity) handle this well, and then RDI design targets it directly. Time risk is the mismatch between 8–12 year development cycles and 10 year fund lives, and patient fund-of-funds capital helps only partly. Exit risk is the weakest link.
The IVCA Bharat Deeptech Report 2026 notes that gaps persist in growth-stage funding and exits. Tracxn counts 104 acquisitions and 46 IPOs in the sector, set against 1,821 funded companies. That’s about one exit for every twelve funded startups over a decade. No LP will underwrite a fund on those odds, however much first loss cushion the government provides.
The most powerful derisker is not a fund at all. It is a customer. A Rs 200 crore procurement commitment from the defence, space or railways sectors does more for a series B round than a Rs 200 crore grant, because it validates revenue rather than science. Advance market commitments, outcome-based public purchase contracts and faster IDEX-style procurement would turn government from a financier into an anchor buyer. That is what private capital actually prices.
Corporate India is also ready to co-invest. Private industry’s share of total R&D spending passed the government’s, reaching 51.8% in 2023-24, as GERD rose to 0.84% of GDP. Yet peers such as the US (3.45%), China (2.58%), and South Korea (4.94%) invest far more. Some government funding through corporate venture arms and strategic acquirers would create the exit buyers the ecosystem lacks.
Sceptics raise fair concerns. State capital at this scale may inflate valuations. It may encourage “policy-shaped” startups that chase allocations rather than markets. It may also displace the private investors it is meant to attract. Israel’s Yozma programme worked partly because the government exited quickly. India’s design, through second-level managers and stake caps, gestures in that direction but has yet to be tested.
So the answer is a qualified yes. Government funds can make private capital comfortable, but only if the state thinks like a first customer and an early exit buyer, not just a generous LP.
Padmaja Ruparel, Co-founder, IAN Group

articles.title: Crea códigos QR y ubica a tus mascotas en pocos minutos si se llegan a perder
articles.text:
Los códigos QR dejaron de ser una curiosidad de supermercado para convertirse en una herramienta que cualquier persona puede fabricar y adaptar a su vida diaria. Con un generador gratuito en línea y datos básicos, es posible crear un acceso directo a información, contactos o archivos sin escribir nada a mano.
Desde compartir una red inalámbrica hasta guardar los primeros pasos de un bebé en video, estos códigos permiten concentrar información dispersa en un solo escaneo.
Usos practicos para los códigos QR
- Comparte tu wifi sin dictar la contraseña
Uno de los usos más prácticos para el hogar o la oficina es crear un código que conecte automáticamente a la red wifi. En lugar de dictar una contraseña larga, los invitados abren la cámara del teléfono y se conectan en segundos.
Para generarlo solo hace falta introducir el nombre de la red (SSID), el tipo de cifrado y la contraseña en un generador especializado, imprimirlo y pegarlo en la entrada o el escritorio.
El mismo principio aplica a la educación: los docentes pueden enlazar códigos a ejercicios adicionales en Google Drive o Dropbox, a videos de clase o a las soluciones de un problema para que el alumno corrija sus propias respuestas.
- Tarjeta de presentación y contacto de emergencia en el bolsillo
Un código QR puede reemplazar la tarjeta de presentación tradicional mediante un vCard que incluya nombre, teléfono, correo, cargo y enlaces a un portafolio. Al escanearlo, el contacto se guarda directo en el teléfono.
El mismo formato sirve para situaciones de riesgo. Una pulsera, llavero o tarjeta con un código que enlace a alergias, enfermedades crónicas, medicamentos y contacto de familiares permite que cualquiera con un smartphone acceda a esos datos en segundos ante una emergencia.
Las personas mayores pueden usar un código similar para llevar al médico la lista actualizada de medicamentos que sus familiares mantienen al día en una página web, sin cargar papeles sueltos.
La misma lógica protege a las mascotas: un código en el collar con teléfono, dirección y fotos del animal facilita que quien lo encuentre pueda devolverlo. En el equipaje de viaje, reemplaza la etiqueta con nombre y dirección visibles por un enlace privado que solo revela los datos al ser escaneado.
- Cobra pagos y centraliza tus redes sociales
Para quienes venden productos de forma informal, participan en ferias u organizan rifas, un código que lleve directo al perfil de pago en plataformas como PayPal, Venmo o Cash App evita errores de transferencia y ahorra tiempo frente a dictar un correo o buscar un usuario entre cientos de resultados.
Un código QR es, en esencia, una imagen escaneable que redirige a un contenido digital: un enlace, un contacto, una red wifi o un archivo. Basta con apuntar la cámara del teléfono para acceder sin escribir nada, lo que explica su utilidad tanto en pagos como en marketing o gestión de información personal.
Quienes mantienen presencia en varias redes, un blog o un canal de video pueden centralizar todo en una página de enlaces y asociarla a un único código. Así se evita imprimir varias direcciones distintas en tarjetas o pósters, y la información puede actualizarse sin cambiar el código impreso.
- Regalos, recuerdos y organización con un escaneo
Los códigos QR añaden una capa interactiva a invitaciones y obsequios. Es posible enlazar un código a un video de boda, una galería de fotos, la ubicación de un evento en el mapa o un formulario de confirmación de asistencia.
En tarjetas de cumpleaños o fiestas infantiles, un código puede llevar a una historia, una lista de reproducción o un mensaje personalizado grabado en video, de modo que un trozo de papel se convierte en un contenido que el destinatario puede ver cuando quiera.
La misma idea sirve para guardar memorias familiares: los primeros pasos o palabras de un bebé en video pueden quedar enlazados en una pegatina pegada al álbum de recortes, disponibles con solo apuntar la cámara.
Para la organización personal, un código puede enlazar a una receta en video pegada en la cocina, o a un itinerario de viaje completo con reservas, horarios y mapas, pegado en la maleta o el cuaderno de viaje.
Cómo crear tus propios códigos QR
Existen generadores gratuitos como goqr.me, QR Code Generator o Canva, entre otros, que permiten crear códigos para enlaces, texto, wifi, vCard y archivos sin conocimientos técnicos.
El proceso básico consiste en elegir el tipo de contenido, introducir la información necesaria, personalizar colores o formas y descargar el resultado en formatos como PNG, JPG, SVG o PDF.

articles.title: Fin du permis à vie : la France a jusqu’à fin 2028 pour choisir entre 10 et 15 ans — Frandroid
articles.text:
Le permis de conduire obtenu une fois pour toutes vit ses dernières années dans l’Union européenne. Le Parlement européen a adopté le 21 octobre 2025 la directive (UE) 2025/2205, qui revoit l’examen, le retrait et la validité du permis. Le texte est en vigueur depuis le 25 novembre 2025. Mais chaque pays a jusqu’au 26 novembre 2028 pour le transposer, puis un an pour l’appliquer. Les quelque 250 millions de conducteurs européens, Français compris, ont donc jusqu’à fin 2029 avant de voir la différence.
Bruxelles justifie la réforme par sa stratégie « Vision Zéro » : diviser par deux la mortalité routière d’ici 2030 par rapport à 2019, puis atteindre zéro mort en 2050. On en est loin. La Commission européenne a compté environ 19 800 morts sur les routes de l’UE en 2024. Pour 2025, ses premiers chiffres, publiés le 24 mars 2026, tombent à 19 400. Une baisse de 3 % en un an, trop lente pour la plupart des États membres selon la Commission elle-même.
Un permis qui expire, et un contrôle de santé pour le prolonger
Les permis voiture (B) et moto (A) seront valables 15 ans. Les pays où le permis sert aussi de pièce d’identité pourront ramener cette durée à 10 ans. Les permis poids lourds et bus devront être renouvelés tous les cinq ans.
Surtout, un contrôle médical sera exigé pour un premier permis comme pour un renouvellement, avec au moins un test de la vue et de l’état cardiovasculaire. Pour la voiture et la moto, chaque pays pourra remplacer ce rendez-vous par un formulaire d’autoévaluation, sur papier ou en ligne. Le contenu de ce questionnaire, sa fréquence et son éventuel coût ne sont pas encore fixés.
Les États pourront aussi raccourcir la validité du permis à partir de 65 ans, pour imposer plus souvent des contrôles médicaux ou des cours de remise à niveau. Les jeunes conducteurs auront une période probatoire d’au moins deux ans, et la conduite accompagnée sera ouverte dès 17 ans. L’examen intégrera les angles morts, les aides à la conduite et le risque du téléphone, avec plus d’attention aux piétons et aux cyclistes (qui ont leurs propres débats, comme le casque obligatoire, que la filière vélo rejette).
Les suspensions vont aussi passer les frontières. Aujourd’hui, un conducteur suspendu à l’étranger ne peut plus rouler dans ce pays, mais il garde le droit de conduire partout ailleurs dans l’UE. En 2019, environ 40 % des infractions commises par des conducteurs étrangers l’étaient ainsi dans une relative impunité, d’après le Conseil de l’UE.
Avec la directive 2025/2206, adoptée en même temps, une suspension d’au moins trois mois pour alcool, drogue, grand excès de vitesse ou accident mortel sera transmise au pays qui a délivré le permis. Ce pays aura 20 jours ouvrés pour prévenir le conducteur. Il décidera ensuite d’appliquer la même sanction, valable alors dans toute l’Union.
    Pour aller plus loin
Le permis de conduire sur smartphone est généralisé : comment ça marche
            
Le permis passera aussi sur smartphone, via le portefeuille européen d’identité numérique (une application officielle qui stocke ses papiers). Le format numérique doit devenir le format principal d’ici 2030. Les eurodéputés ont obtenu que chacun puisse demander une carte physique, délivrée en général sous trois semaines, avec une puce ou un QR code contre la falsification.
    Pour aller plus loin
Comment installer carte d’identité numérique, permis de conduire, carte Vitale et carte grise sur votre smartphone
            
En France, presque tout reste à écrire
Vous avez un permis au format carte bancaire ? Il porte déjà une date de fin. Depuis le 19 janvier 2013, les permis français sont délivrés pour 15 ans. Par contre, leur renouvellement reste une formalité administrative, sans aucun contrôle de santé. La directive devrait ajouter la visite médicale ou le questionnaire à cette échéance.
    Pour aller plus loin
Adieu Apple Pay, Google Wallet et France Identité ? Voici le nouveau portefeuille numérique européen
            
Comme le permis sert de justificatif d’identité en France, le gouvernement pourra choisir 10 ans au lieu de 15. Il n’a encore rien tranché. Le 14 juillet 2026, le ministère des Transports a seulement indiqué que la transposition était pilotée par le ministère de l’Intérieur, et aucun projet de texte n’avait été rendu public début août.
Sur le numérique, la France a de l’avance. L’application France Identité, du ministère de l’Intérieur, héberge déjà le permis de conduire. Elle doit devenir le portefeuille européen d’identité numérique d’ici fin 2026, l’échéance fixée à chaque pays de l’UE pour en proposer un.
Pour votre permis actuel, rien ne change tant que la loi française n’est pas votée, au plus tard le 26 novembre 2028. En attendant, regardez la case 4b au recto de votre carte : c’est sa date de fin de validité. Si elle tombe avant la réforme, le renouvellement se fait en ligne sur le site de l’ANTS, sans passer chez le médecin.

Class of 2016: PiggyVest
Would you trust three people in their early twenties with your hard-earned money? That was the ask PiggyVest’s founders put to Nigerians in 2016, the same year they lost ₦18 billion ($71 million) to MMM, a Ponzi scheme.
Winning that trust was only the start. PiggyVest spent its first four years relying on other companies’ licences, which cut its margins and what it could pay savers. In 2019, it dropped the name Piggybank.ng after the central bank made clear only licensed banks could use the word. In 2021, it survived a run of withdrawals that chief operating officer Odun Eweniyi calls the closest it came to failing.
Today, PiggyVest says it has 6.7 million users and paid ₦1.3 trillion ($983 million) back to savers in 2025 alone. Its parent company also owns Pocket, a payments app, and wants to become a financial ecosystem for every Nigerian.
[Read the PiggyVest profile →]

Your success and ours are the same story. Happy Customer Service Week. This year’s theme is The Extra Mile, and it’s the only way we know how to do this. Visit: fincra.com.
Companies
Moove exits Nigeria one month after Uber
Sometimes, you order a ride on Uber and see that little grey Suzuki S-Presso car pulling up. Well, the company that helped put some of those cars on the road is leaving Nigeria.
What happened? Moove, the mobility fintech that financed and rented cars to ride-hailing drivers, is shutting down its Nigerian operations six years after launching in Lagos. It says eligible customers will get full ownership of vehicles worth about ₦35 billion ($26.3 million), free of charge.
There’s a bit of history here: Eyebrows are naturally going up because Moove’s exit comes just over a month after ride-hailing giant Uber left Nigeria, saying it was reviewing its business priorities and where it wanted to invest across Africa. Moove hasn’t said Uber’s exit is why it is leaving, but the timing is hard to ignore.
Explain like I’m new here: Moove and Uber were practically joined at the hip in Nigeria. When Moove launched in 2020, it found drivers who wanted to make money from ride-hailing but didn’t have enough money to buy a car. Moove financed cars for drivers, letting them use those vehicles for work while paying towards ownership from their earnings. In 2020, Moove became Uber’s car-financing and vehicle-supply partner in sub-Saharan Africa, supplying vehicles including Suzuki Alto and S-Presso models. Uber later invested in Moove, leading its $100 million Series B round in 2024.
Money Mooves: By 2024, it had raised $460 million across equity and debt, valuing the company at $750 million. In August, it raised $250 million in Series C funding at a $2.1 billion valuation, joining the Lagos-born startup unicorn club. It was building a much bigger mobility business. In January 2025, it acquired Brazilian mobility startup Kovi, and later acquired Tokyo Taxi in Japan, adding established fleets to its growing global footprint. It also moved into autonomous vehicles in the United States through a partnership with Waymo, managing driverless fleets in Phoenix and Miami.
What happens now? For the drivers, the ending is actually a bit sweet. Moove says over 9,000 customers have used its drive-to-own and rental products in Nigeria. Eligible customers can keep their cars for free. The company continues to operate elsewhere, with 42,000 vehicles across 29 cities including Accra, Cape Town, Nairobi, London, Dubai, Cairo, as well as its autonomous operations in Phoenix and Miami.
Nigeria may have lost Moove, but for the drivers who spent years paying for those cars, the company is leaving behind the one thing its business was built to help them get.

True scale demands moving beyond surface-level integrations to robust execution. We’ve filtered the noise out of Moonshot 2026, optimising the conference strictly for high-calibre connections between startup founders, global financial operators, enterprise leaders and individuals rewiring Africa’s technical frameworks. Join us on October 28 & 29, 2026. Get your ticket.
regulation
South Africa wants new rules for gambling on your phone
Gambling is already tightly regulated in South Africa. The country has laws governing casinos, betting, and other forms of gambling, but phones have made it much easier to access gambling products from almost anywhere. Now, the government is looking at whether the networks carrying that activity should have a bigger role in regulating it.
What happened? Communications Minister Solly Malatsi has said he will engage the Independent Communications Authority of South Africa (ICASA), the country’s tech regulator, to put a guardrail around offshore gambling. Malatsi said existing gambling laws already regulate gambling activities, but acknowledged that the government needs to consider whether more consumer protections are needed when electronic networks are involved.
Explain like I’m new here: South Africa already has a gambling rulebook. The National Gambling Act and provincial laws govern gambling and betting, while the National Gambling Board (NGB) says interactive online gambling remains illegal. Online betting is allowed when it is offered by a licenced South African bookmaker. Yet, the Internet has made those lines harder to police. People can use the same phone and mobile network to place a legal sports bet, buy a gambling voucher or reach an offshore gambling platform.
A lot is already going into this: Since October 2025, the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition has been reviewing the National Gambling Act, with a new bill expected to reach Cabinet later this year. A Gambling Technical Committee has also been reviewing the legislation and how national and provincial rules fit together. In April, licenced bookmakers called on banks and payment providers to block transactions to offshore gambling platforms. Malatsi’s move is targeting the communications networks through which people access these services.
The ads are getting attention too: The National Gambling Board is also working on advertising regulations, with planned measures including responsible-gambling warnings and restrictions on placing gambling ads where most of the audience is under 18.
What happens now? Malatsi’s engagement with ICASA is still at the discussion stage. There is no new blanket ban on gambling through mobile networks. However, if the government eventually decides that networks should have a role, the rules could potentially focus on activities like how gambling platforms are accessed or whether unlicensed services should be blocked.

articles.title: Europa y China alcanzan un acuerdo que apunta a reducir a la mitad la llegada de coches híbridos chinos en cuatro años
articles.text:
La llegada de coches fabricados en China lleva tiempo poniendo a prueba a la industria automovilística europea. Los fabricantes del gigante asiático han ganado presencia en el mercado comunitario, especialmente en segmentos donde la electrificación está transformando la oferta de vehículos. Pero hay una diferencia importante que no siempre resulta evidente: un coche eléctrico y uno híbrido no reciben necesariamente el mismo tratamiento comercial. Y esa distinción ha terminado adquiriendo una dimensión que va mucho más allá de las preferencias de los conductores europeos.
Un acuerdo para reducir las importaciones. La Unión Europea y China alcanzaron este viernes un entendimiento sobre el comercio de automóviles híbridos tras dos días de negociaciones en Pekín, celebradas el 8 y el 9 de octubre. Maroš Šefčovič, comisario europeo de Comercio y Seguridad Económica, explicó que el acuerdo podría reducir más de la mitad los envíos de estos vehículos desde China al mercado comunitario durante los próximos cuatro años. El Ministerio de Comercio chino confirmó el entendimiento, aunque no precisó cómo se aplicará ni recogió expresamente esa reducción en su comunicado.
El origen está en los aranceles. Para entender cómo hemos llegado hasta aquí, tenemos que retroceder a octubre de 2024. Entonces, la Comisión Europea impuso aranceles compensatorios adicionales a los vehículos eléctricos de batería fabricados en China, tras una investigación antisubvenciones. Los recargos oscilan entre el 7,8% y el 35,3%, dependiendo del fabricante, y se suman al arancel ordinario del 10%. Sin embargo, aquella medida dejó fuera a los híbridos, tanto convencionales como enchufables, que siguieron pagando únicamente el arancel ordinario.
Una transformación que muestran los números. En 2023, casi siete de cada diez automóviles que la UE importaba de China eran eléctricos puros: el 69%, según Global Trade Alert. En 2025, esa proporción había bajado al 45%, mientras los híbridos convencionales y enchufables pasaban del 7% al 31%. Durante la primera mitad de 2026, estos últimos llegaron al 39% de los vehículos importados desde el país asiático. Hay otro dato que permite dimensionar el crecimiento. Financial Times señala que las importaciones mensuales de híbridos desde China pasaron de 3.800 unidades en octubre de 2024 a 50.000 en julio de 2026.
Lo anunciado no explica cómo se aplicará. El responsable europeo ha adelantado el alcance que podría tener el entendimiento, pero todavía quedan preguntas importantes por resolver. El comunicado conjunto difundido por el Ministerio de Comercio chino confirma el acuerdo sobre los híbridos dentro de las reglas de la Organización Mundial del Comercio (OMC), aunque no especifica qué mecanismo permitiría alcanzar la reducción prevista. Tampoco precisa cómo se supervisaría su cumplimiento ni si las condiciones serían iguales para todos los fabricantes.
No todas las restricciones son equivalentes. Bruselas había planteado que China limitase voluntariamente sus exportaciones de híbridos, pero Pekín se opuso en septiembre y alegó que el sistema vulneraba las normas de la OMC.
El automóvil es solo una parte. El entendimiento sobre los híbridos forma parte de una negociación que, según el Ministerio de Comercio chino, terminó con 16 puntos de consenso. Abarcan el equilibrio comercial y las inversiones, los controles de exportación, la propiedad intelectual y la reforma de la OMC. China también se mostró dispuesta a seguir facilitando, mediante un mecanismo de “canal verde”, la aprobación de licencias para exportar tierras raras e imanes permanentes a la UE.
El resultado dependerá de su aplicación. El siguiente paso será comprobar si el entendimiento alcanzado en Pekín se traduce en compromisos comerciales concretos. Se espera que ambas partes mantengan una reunión ministerial por videoconferencia en enero de 2027 y celebren una nueva ronda de negociaciones en marzo.

articles.title: Oral-B iO : ce lot de six recharges revient à environ 5 € par brossette
articles.text:
Le lot de 6 brossettes Oral-B iO Ultimate Clean est à 30,39 €
Destinées aux brosses à dents électriques Oral-B iO, ces six brossettes Ultimate Clean permettent de constituer une réserve de recharges.
Amazon propose le lot de six brossettes Oral-B iO Ultimate Clean noires à 30,39 €, en achat ponctuel. Cela représente une économie de 19,51 € par rapport au prix conseillé de 49,90 €, soit environ 39 %. Le prix le plus bas des 30 derniers jours indiqué sur la capture est de 31,99 € : la baisse par rapport à cette référence est donc de 5 %. L’offre est vendue et expédiée par Amazon.
Des brossettes exclusivement destinées à la gamme Oral-B iO
Ce pack comprend six têtes de rechange noires, dotées d’une tête ronde et de brins inclinés. Leur disposition vise à atteindre les zones difficiles d’accès et à nettoyer entre les dents. Il s’agit de recharges : le manche de la brosse à dents n’est pas inclus.
La compatibilité est le point à vérifier avant l’achat. Ces Ultimate Clean sont conçues pour les brosses électriques Oral-B iO. Les gammes Vitality, Pro, Smart et Genius utilisent d’autres brossettes ; les deux systèmes ne sont pas interchangeables.
Environ 5,07 € par recharge
À ce tarif, chaque brossette revient à environ 5,07 €. Le conditionnement par six permet de disposer de plusieurs recharges pour son appareil ou de répartir le stock entre plusieurs utilisateurs équipés d’un manche compatible.
Oral-B recommande un remplacement tous les trois mois. En suivant ce rythme, six brossettes correspondent théoriquement à 18 mois de recharges pour une personne, ou neuf mois pour deux utilisateurs. Cette estimation dépend toutefois de l’usure des brins, qui peut nécessiter un changement plus précoce.

articles.title: Bern-based Besso raises €4.29 million to scale its AI-powered trade regulation intelligence platform | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Besso, a Bern-based startup that helps companies manage the complexity of international trade regulations, has secured €4.29 million (CHF 4 million) in funding.
The funding came from a single large European family office, which opted to remain anonymous. This is a departure from traditional early-stage funding rounds, which have multiple backers, and the company says the funding raised from a single long-term investor was deliberate.
“We have always been very deliberate about building Besso around real customer demand rather than funding milestones. The traction we are seeing now tells us that the time is right to invest more aggressively in growth. Having one long-term investor take the entire round gives us both the resources and the focus to do exactly that,” said Philip Sieber-Gasser, founder and CEO of Besso.
Founded and headquartered in Bern, Switzerland, Besso helps multinational corporations turn the growing complexity of international trade regulation into a source of competitive advantage. It has built an AI platform that continuously monitors over 1,250 trade regulations and tariff schedules across global corridors, automatically identifying where companies are overpaying on duties and offering them opportunities to recover costs through preferential tariff rates and free trade agreement (FTA) eligibility.
According to the company, global tariff teams miss out on preferential tariff rates on around 30% of eligible shipments. This reportedly costs mid-size importers between $2 million and $15 million annually. In addition to cost, these trade teams are also grappling with more than 7,000 regulatory changes every week across major trade corridors, a figure that has grown due to geopolitics and tariff volatility.
Besso’s AI platform replaces the manual, error-prone processes reliant on spreadsheets, PDFs, and consultancy dependency that most companies currently use to manage their requirements. Besso has already built a strong roster of global clients, including Danone, Unilever, AB-InBev, BASF, Coca-Cola, Heineken, Philip Morris International and Syngenta. The company says additional Fortune 500 companies recently joined the platform.
Alongside its strong client base, the company has built a team with expertise in legal research and is supported by academic partners including the Geneva Graduate Institute, the World Trade Institute, and ETH Zurich. Its advisory board includes Jean-Daniel Gerber, a former Swiss Secretary of State for Economic Affairs, along with other leading trade law academics and AI specialists.
The company, a Venture Leaders alumnus, plans to use the funding to increase its headcount, scale capacity to serve a rapidly growing multinational customer base, and advance its technology platform through continued investment in product development and R&D.
“This is an important milestone for us, but the funding itself is not the destination. What matters is what it enables us to build from here,” added Sieber-Gasser.

articles.title: SenseHuman AI is building an AI-powered hardhat that watches your back | BetaKit
articles.text:
On a busy construction site, it can feel like you need eyes in the back of your head to avoid accidents. SenseHuman AI wants to provide you with those “eyes.”
The Edmonton-based startup has developed a hardhat imbued with AI machine vision, giving the wearer 360 degrees of worksite surveillance. The company has already had traction, signing customers and completing pilots. Now, co-founder and CEO Adil Muhammad says they need to meet demand.
“We want to scale up manufacturing … and we’re trying to get the attention of investors so we can scale.”
Adil Muhammad, SenseHuman
Originally from Pakistan, Muhammad founded SenseHuman AI last year alongside three co-founders: Gavin Mei, Vicente Gonzalez, and Gaang Lee. A graduate of the University of Alberta (U of A), Muhammad completed his master’s degree in civil engineering and spent time working in the U of A’s IHT Lab researching ways AI can be integrated into construction site safety. But it wasn’t his education that served as the lightbulb moment for Muhammad, but rather a video game.
“If you’ve ever played Call of Duty, there’s this minimap on the bottom of the screen. If something comes at you from the back, you see it on the minimap,” Muhammad said. “I thought, why not use the same thing with a worker?”
SenseHuman’s hardware doesn’t actually create a minimap. In fact, there are no screens at all. Instead, it uses four cameras and machine-vision software to create a 360-degree field of vision. If that software detects an imminent risk—like, say, a trench, ledge, or tripping hazard—it sends a vibrating signal through the hardhat in the direction of the danger. SenseHuman can even custom build the helmets to factor job site rules—like standing three metres from a piece of operating machinery—into its risk assessments.
SenseHuman’s platform isn’t perfect (it can’t yet reliably predict falling objects from above, and it can’t stop every accident on a job site from happening), but the company is focused on preventing the minor injuries that make up the lion’s share of job site incidents.
RELATED: From sawdust to seed round: ConstructionClock grows from Winnipeg
“I was reading a lot of incident reports from the Workers’ Compensation Board, and talking to different companies,” Muhammad said. “Every year you see news articles—and many more that go unreported—about accidents that lead to minor injuries. These are the main incidents that are happening, and these guys have the most pain in the industry.”
The Association of Workers’ Compensation Boards of Canada (AWCBC), a nonprofit body representing Canada’s workers’ compensation boards, reports that in 2024 there were more than 320,000 lost time claims, meaning an injury was serious enough that a worker could not be at work. Among that number, jobs in the trades, transportation, and equipment operators were far and away the most common.
Financial incentives
Beyond the potential safety benefits, there’s value for employers, too. Muhammad said SenseHuman’s cameras can create video footage—which excludes audio recording due to privacy concerns—that it claims has already been used by its pilot partner to investigate an accident.
WorkSafeBC, the BC provincial counterpart to the AWCBC, in its own report last May said that the construction industry had around 38,000 accepted claims, with nearly 5,800 of those involving falls and nearly 7,000 involving equipment or vehicular collisions. WorkSafeBC estimates total costs from those claims tallied at more than $1.3 billion.
While most workers’ compensation claims are paid by the province, companies still incur costs, either from subsequent investigations or fines levied against them after an accident. In Alberta, penalties can run into the hundreds of thousands of dollars.
Momentum and bottlenecks
Since launching last October, SenseHuman has had remarkable traction. In January, it received $250,000 CAD in pre-seed funding from OpenCircle Contractors Association, a non-profit construction industry association, alongside an additional undisclosed investor. It later sold its first five units to OpenCircle and has 12 smart helmets active in the field today.
SenseHuman has also completed several pilot programs, including Edmonton Unlimited’s Built World Venture Pilot program, where the company partnered with Sherwood Park, Alta.-based industrial contractor The Bartlett Group. It has used the feedback from those relationships to further tailor its product to industry needs.
“Right now, the main issue is that we have a lot of interest from companies, but we don’t have capacity to build more units,” Muhammad said. “We want to scale up manufacturing … and we’re trying to get the attention of investors so we can scale.”

articles.title: US Disrupts Chinese State-Sponsored Hacking Tools
articles.text:
The United States on Thursday announced the disruption of two hacking tools used by Chinese state-sponsored threat actors in attacks against US and foreign critical infrastructure.
Built by Integrity Technology Group (Integrity Tech), MicroScan has been used for vulnerability scanning, while FishHub has enabled network intrusions via spear phishing.
Integrity Tech, the US says, used a Mirai malware variant to build an IoT botnet that facilitated MicroScan’s use for reconnaissance against victims’ networks, including a US power company, NGOs, Japanese and Polish airports, and Taiwanese critical infrastructure entities and universities.
FishHub enabled Integrity Tech’s clients to access victim networks remotely, search for specific files, and exfiltrate them. The tool has been used in attacks against at least 20 universities in Taiwan.
The US seized the domains the threat actors were using to access MicroScan and FishHub, including c0cc[.]cc, 98aicai[.]com, 98aicode[.]com, outlook3650[.]com, youtubecard[.]com, and linkedinns[.]net.
In 2024, the US disrupted Integrity Tech’s Raptor Train botnet, and in 2025 sanctioned it for providing cybersecurity products to Chinese state-sponsored APTs such as Flax Typhoon. The European Union sanctioned the company in March 2026.
A new joint advisory (PDF) from government agencies in the US, UK, Australia, Canada, Japan, New Zealand, and Spain shows that MicroScan has been active since at least 2017, targeting Apache Struts, Juniper ScreenOS, Jenkins, OpenSSL, Oracle, Rejetto HFS, WebLogic Server, WordPress, and other services.
“This Python-based web application contains over 1,300 penetration testing scripts written to scan websites for specific vulnerabilities,” the advisory reads.
The tool was mainly associated with Flax Typhoon (also known as Ethereal Panda, Red Juliett, Storm-0919, and UNC5007) activity, but Integrity Tech is believed to have been working with other Chinese APTs as well.
Flax Typhoon was also seen using BBScan, dirsearch, Fscan, ksubdomain, masscan, Nmap, OneForAll, ShuiZe, and WPScan for reconnaissance, and command-line exploit utilities and the EBurst Microsoft Exchange password spraying tool for initial access.
The threat actors deployed VPN tools such as SoftEther for persistence and downloaded databases or manually extracted data from victims’ email addresses. They also used the PHP script Curlc4.txt and command-line utility office-cli for email exfiltration, and DC.ex to extract sensitive data from Active Directory.
“The threat actors collect account credentials and exfiltrate victim email data from on-premises systems and cloud-based services. Observed victims of email data theft included government organizations, law enforcement agencies, healthcare systems, and religious institutions located in Southeast Asia. In some instances, the threat actors restricted access to the exfiltrated data to only IP addresses from Xiamen, China,” the advisory reads.

articles.title: Exclusive: Automattic loses its interim CFO just weeks after boardroom shakeup
articles.text:
Automattic’s interim chief financial officer Jeremy Klaperman has left his position after less than a month, TechCrunch has learned. Klaperman had been elevated to the new job last month after the governance crisis at the WordPress.com parent company, which saw its entire board either quit or be fired.
The company confirmed the departure with the following statement, shared by Automattic’s director of communications Megan Fox: “Automattic will always be grateful for Jeremy Klaperman’s leadership. We wish him the best of luck on his next endeavor.”
Before serving as the organization’s interim finance chief, Klaperman had served as the CFO of Automattic’s VIP Enterprise business unit.
He was meant to replace the former CFO, Mark Davies, who had briefly become Automattic’s CFO after the company’s board members voted to put CEO Matt Mullenweg on leave in September. Within 33 hours of the board’s decision, Mullenweg retook the CEO role, and the board was wiped clean.
Automattic’s chief legal officer Andy Missan had also left the company alongside Davies. Both executives had signed reciprocal severance deals during Mullenweg’s short leave of absence, TechCrunch previously reported. Automattic’s new board of directors was announced in late September, and includes best-selling science-fiction author Hugh Howey; two co-founders of the now-defunct social app IRL, Henry Khachatryan and Krutal Desai; plus author Amy Chan.
A source at Automattic told TechCrunch that Klaperman was upset the board was considering external candidates for the CFO role. Though he was announced internally as interim CFO, the board never legally approved his title, the source said. In addition, there was a disagreement with Mullenweg over a work project related to employee performance reviews, which led to Mullenweg’s demotion of Klaperman back to his former position at VIP. Klaperman resigned shortly thereafter.
Automattic’s spokesperson did not comment on the reason for Klaperman’s departure. The company is still performing an external search for a qualified CFO candidate, we understand.
After publication, the company issued a statement via X post, which implies that Klaperman was offended by the board’s search for external CFO candidates.
It read, “At Automattic, we consider it best practice to evaluate external candidates for critical roles alongside internal people stepping up. We are always talking to and recruiting the best talent. Sometimes people are offended or surprised by this and they resign, sometimes it has led to amazing mentoring or advising situations. We won’t comment on any specific person, but as a company we’re always trying to optimize and redefine ourselves to serve our customers better and promote the ideals we aspire to around Open Source, freedom, liberty, autonomy, and hackers.”
When the company originally announced Klaperman’s new role as interim CFO internally on Automattic’s Slack, Mullenweg reiterated that he had “100% confidence” in the company’s cash and financial position.
Updated after publication with more information about Klaperman’s departure.

Lo más bestia en el mundo de los cargadores, para usuarios exigentes

articles.title: My brief romance with an AI bird feeder
articles.text:
It started off promising enough. Dozens of tiny, colorful birds were drawn to my garden just a few weeks after I mounted a $350 $269 Kiwibit Bird Feeder 2 Pro. “Looks like Great Tit!” read the first AI-driven alert sent to my phone. “Looks like Eurasian Blue Tit!” read another. I chuckled, still waiting for adulthood to kick in.
My brief romance with an AI bird feeder
Everything was great until he arrived.
Everything was great until he arrived.
This went on for days. Hundreds of miniature tits came to snack on expensive sunflower seeds already husked. They’d skulk about in nearby trees before flittering in to grab a single seed to be safely enjoyed in the canopy above.
I took great delight in my new house guests. I admired them in crisp 4K HDR video recordings. I looked for unique markings in the hope of naming my new feral pets. I clicked deeper into the Kiwibit app to read about my visitors’ migration habits, where they nest, and what they like to eat. It was all going swell until he arrived.
“Looks like Common Wood Pigeon!” came the alert. All I saw was a battleship-gray blob obscuring the live camera feed. The winged rat was so fat and imposing that he blocked the lens. Ugh, no, go back to the tourists!
In mild panic, I triggered the feeder’s Nuisance Animal Alarm, a feature typically reserved for squirrels and the like. The pigeon tensed, looked around, but wasn’t deterred by the audible siren that was surely annoying my neighbors. Soon it went back to gorging on the haute cuisine purchased for more refined guests. It ate and ate and ate. For 15 minutes, it ate until I walked outside and shooed it away.
Thereafter, that pigeon, or pigeons (who can tell) moved in. They’d perch for 30 minutes or more, slamming their faces into the seed pile with the clumsy enthusiasm of a tween bobbing for apples. Mice arrived below to feast on the spoils. Admitting defeat, I dismounted the expensive bird feeder and shoved it into a closet.
I’m not mad at Kiwibit. The “Bird Feeder 2 Pro 4K AI Camera with Solar Panel (Lifetime AI Included)” I tested was a joy to use, until it wasn’t. That’s not Kiwibit’s fault.
If you’ve been tempted to buy a smart bird feeder, I’d suggest starting with something simple, inexpensive, and without AI instead of going all in on day one — you can’t return a used feeder just because it attracts pests.

articles.title: Furieux contre Adobe, il recrée Photoshop et six autres logiciels avec l'IA
articles.text:
La série s’appelle ArtCraft et aligne sept logiciels calqués sur les piliers de la Creative Cloud, dont PhotoCraft, réplique de Photoshop publiée la semaine dernière sur GitHub. Derrière le projet, un seul homme : Brandon Thomas, un développeur d’Atlanta passé par les systèmes de paiement, « vétéran de quinze ans dans l’industrie » comme il se présente. L’intéressé assume des logiciels en version alpha, « loin d’être prêts », et promet des primes à qui l’aidera à corriger les bugs.
Sept clones, zéro abonnement
Le catalogue recouvre l’essentiel de la suite d’Adobe : PhotoCraft pour Photoshop, VectorCraft pour Illustrator, FilmCraft pour Premiere Pro, LightCraft pour Lightroom, EffectCraft pour After Effects, DesignCraft pour InDesign et PrintCraft pour Acrobat. Le tout est écrit en Rust, sans une ligne de code d’Adobe, et tourne en natif sur macOS, Windows, Linux et FreeBSD, ainsi que dans le navigateur. PhotoCraft ouvre et réenregistre les fichiers PSD, gère calques, masques et styles, et expose plus de 500 commandes pilotables par script ou par un agent IA : tout ce qui se clique peut aussi s’automatiser.
L’usage est gratuit, sans abonnement ; seuls les crédits de génération d’images par IA se paient. Vibe coding oblige, les bugs sont bien là : la transformation libre s’annule parfois toute seule, et la stabilité reste celle d’une alpha précoce. Lui qui se décrit comme tout sauf « un simple amateur occasionnel du vibe coding » en convient sans détour.
Pourquoi Adobe est la cible idéale
Adobe a soldé cette année, pour 150 millions de dollars, des poursuites fédérales engagées en 2024 qui l’accusaient de piéger ses clients dans leurs abonnements. Ce ras-le-bol nourrit une tendance de longue date avec le géant du logiciel créatif : plutôt que de payer chaque mois, certains développeurs font écrire leurs propres outils par l’IA, et ArtCraft en est la vitrine la plus ambitieuse.
Thomas a codé ses clones avec Claude Opus 5.5, le modèle d’Anthropic, dont Adobe est précisément partenaire : depuis fin avril, un connecteur officiel permet à Claude de piloter plus de 50 outils de la Creative Cloud. L’IA que l’éditeur met en avant pour enrichir Photoshop sert donc aussi, ailleurs, à le cloner gratuitement (quand ce n’est pas directement dans Claude que le clone arrive).
Pour l’abonné Creative Cloud, rien ne change ce matin : les clones plantent trop pour remplacer quoi que ce soit, et Adobe conserve des années d’avance fonctionnelle. Les alternatives gratuites à la suite Adobe ne sont pas pléthoriques, mais Affinity reste une référence solide pour remplacer le triptyque Photoshop, InDesign, Publisher.

articles.title: Competencia acaba de aprobar que cada vez más gimnasios de España sean en realidad el mismo gimnasio
articles.text:
Fumata blanca. La Comisión Nacional de los Mercados y la Competencia (CNMC) acaba de dar luz verde a una de las operaciones más importantes de los últimos años en el sector del fitness lowcost: la adquisición de Synergym por parte de VivaGym. La compra se había avanzado ya en abril, pero estaba pendiente del visto bueno del organismo regulador. Se desconoce el importe de la venta o el calendario que manejan las cadenas, pero algo sí está claro: teniendo en cuenta que Synergym gestionaba 164 clubes en mayo y VivaGym presume de tener más de 240 gimnasios repartidos por España, en el horizonte del fitness patrio asoma un nuevo gigante.
De ahí que la decisión de la CNMC suponga más que un simple visto bueno para una compra. En la práctica avanza hacia la paulatina concentración del negocio del fitness.
¿Qué ha pasado? La operación se anunció en abril, pero estaba pendiente de la CNMC, que acaba de darle su visto bueno ahora. El organismo regulador de la competencia ha decidido dar luz verde a VivaGym para que adquiera Synergym, una cadena de gimnasios fundada en Málaga en 2013 y que ha crecido con rapidez hasta cerrar 2025 con 160 gimnasios. VivaGym no le va a la zaga. La compañía se fundó en 2011 y en los últimos años se ha expandido con fuerza en España, en gran medida gracias a la adquisición de otras cadenas.
No se conoce la cuantía de la operación ni cuándo podrá completarse. Lo que sí ha trascendido es que, hasta entonces, tanto Synergym como VivaGym mantendrán su actividad igual que hasta ahora: de manera independiente, conservando sus respectivas marcas, equipos y operativas. "La resolución de la CNMC supone un paso importante para poder avanzar en la operación", recalca la CEO de VivaGym, Cristina Burzako.
¿Por qué es importante? La razón principal es cuantitativa. Synergym y VivaGym eran por separado dos pesos pesados en el negocio del fitness español. Juntas, sumarán alrededor de 450 gimnasios, una amplia red de centros que estarán distribuidos además por gran parte del país.
Ahora mismo VivaGym presume de gestionar más de 240. Synergym cerró el primer trimestre de 2026 con 164 clubes deportivos, una cifra que se ha ampliado desde inicios de año con inauguraciones en Valencia, Barcelona y Burgos y que espera elevar a 210 en los próximos meses. No es su único objetivo. La firma malagueña quiere lograr una facturación de 100 millones de euros.
UN VISTAZO A...
¿De dónde viene el dinero? Esa es otra de las claves. Con los gimnasios convertidos en un negocio cada vez más jugoso, que mueve ya más de 3.200 millones de euros solo en España, el sector ha captado el interés de grandes inversores. Detrás de VivaGym está de hecho Providence Equity, una gestora de capital riesgo estadounidense que parece decidida a ampliar su huella en el mundo del fitness. De hecho, ahora mismo está pujando también para hacerse con la cadena gala Fitness Park, valorada en alrededor de 600 millones de euros.
Providence anunció su desembarco en VivaGym Group hace poco más de dos años, en junio de 2024. Hasta entonces la cadena española había estado ligada a Bridges Fund Management. En ese momento VivaGym gestionaba ya 104 gimnasios con más de 315.000 socios repartidos entre España y Portugal (lejos de los 15 centros que controlaba en 2015) y el objetivo de Providence era acelerar su expansión ibérica. Y lo ha hecho. En los últimos años ha ido reforzándose con la compra de una decena de operadores, como Smartfit, Macro Fit, Altafit o One Fit. Ahora a esa larga lista se sumará Synergym.
¿Por qué esa expansión? Lo comentábamos en abril, cuando se hizo público el acuerdo entre VivaGym y Synergym: si la cadena respaldada por Providence quiere consolidarse en el low cost, necesita convertirse en un operador lo suficientemente grande como para presionar a caseros y proveedores al negociar sus precios. Al fin y al cabo VivaGym no es el único que ha apurado el paso. Enfrente tiene a Basic Fit, que gestiona más de 240 gimnasios en España, a los que se suman instalaciones en una decena de países europeos.
¿Tanto crece el sector? Sí. Las encuestas del CSC y EuropeActive muestran que cada vez es más fácil encontrarse con españoles abonados a gimnasios. Si a comienzos de siglo representaban apenas el 3% de la población adulta, ahora superan el 30%. Y las cadenas de gimnasios privadas parecen haber sacado tajada de ese boom: su número de abonados se ha incrementado un 26,5% en solo una década (2015-2024).
Según el primer informe sectorial de la Fundación Activa, en el que también se han implicado la consultora Deloitte y Fneid, el sector del fitness mueve ya más de 3.200 millones de facturación y aglutina a 8,3 millones de usuarios. El estudio muestra además que el fitness ha entrado de lleno en la sociedad (tasa de penetración del 16,5%) y que el número de españoles que aseguran practicar deportes de forma habitual (87%) supera holgadamente la media europea (64%).
¿Y más allá de las cadenas? El informe de Activa deja sobre la mesa otra idea interesante que refleja cómo en el mundo del fitness no solo cambia la demanda, también lo hace la oferta. Los gimnasios de barrio siguen representando el colectivo más numeroso, pero solo si nos fijamos en las instalaciones. Si prestamos atención a las listas de abonados, son las cadenas las que arrastran más clientes. Y por goleada.
Traducido en cifras: el 69% de los centros los gestionan operadores independientes, frente al 31% controlado por cadenas; sin embargo, el 65% de los usuarios paga sus cuotas a estas últimas. El motivo de ese desequilibrio es obvio: el éxito del formato low cost hace que a los gimnasios de barrio les resulte difícil competir con cadenas como Synergym o VivaGym, tanto en dotación como en precios. Con todo, las cadenas no solo triunfan en el low cost. Algunas están explotando con éxito el mercado del fitness premium.
